#2305. 3 novembre 1985, la punizione di Maradona alla Juventus. Mandando Tacconi in porta

Il 3 novembre del 1985, allo stadio San Paolo in Fuorigrotta, il Napoli ospita la Juventus. Da una parte i bianconeri allenati da Giovanni Trapattoni, che provengono da una striscia di otto vittorie consecutive. Dall'altra Diego Armando Maradona che non ha ancora vinto una partita contro i piemontesi. E sembrava che potesse continuare così, almeno fino a diciotto minuti dalla fine.

Al ventisettesimo del secondo tempo, l'arbitro Redini concede un calcio di punizione di seconda, all'interno dell'area di rigore della Juventus, per un fallo di Scirea su Bertoni. Lo spazio per far passare la palla è esiguo, a sedici metri dalla porta e con la barriera molto vicina. Il tocco leggero, all'indietro, è di Eraldo Pecci, mentre l'argentino dà una pennellata alla palla, con il sinistro, scavalcando la barriera e mandando il pallone all'incrocio dei pali, con Tacconi che non può far altro che finire dentro il sacco. È il gol, meraviglioso, dell'uno a zero che sarà poi definitivo. È la prima vittoria per Diego Maradona contro la Juventus, giocata contro campioni come Platini, Cabrini e Scirea.

NAPOLI Garella, Bruscolotti, Carannante, Bagni, Ferrario, Renica, Bertoni, Pecci (45’ Buriani), Giordano (60’ Caffarelli), Maradona, Celestini. Allenatore: Ottavio Bianchi

JUVENTUS Tacconi, Favero, Cabrini, Pioli, Brio, Scirea, Mauro (75’ G. Pin), Bonini, Serena, Platini, M. Laudrup. Allenatore: Giovanni Trapattoni

Stefano Vecchi, tecnico dell'Inter U23, ha parlato ai microfoni di nuovacosenza.com al termine del match perso di misura sul campo del Cosenza: "Sicuramente tre impegni in una settimana possono pesare, ma abbiamo usato tutto l'organico, alcuni dei giocatori che avevano giocato martedì oggi non sono stati impiegati. Abbiamo ruotato tanti elementi, quindi non credo che il problema sia stato quello. È stata una partita molto combattuta, con tanto agonismo. Ce l'abbiamo messa tutta anche noi, ma siamo stati puniti su un calcio d'angolo dove sono stati più bravi. Non ricordo grandi occasioni da gol per il Cosenza, al di là di quell'episodio. Noi, invece, soprattutto all'inizio, abbiamo avuto qualche tiro e qualche situazione potenzialmente pericolosa che avrebbe potuto permetterci di andare in vantaggio. Poi la gara è diventata una bella battaglia e alla fine l'ha vinta il Cosenza".

All'inizio il Cosenza sembrava accusare un po' di timore reverenziale, mentre l'Inter aveva preso in mano il gioco con personalità. Poi la partita è cambiata.

"Noi abbiamo messo pressione, purtroppo quando siamo arrivati negli ultimi metri abbiamo trovato un muro che non siamo riusciti a superare. In quelle situazioni serve qualcosa in più dal punto di vista qualitativo, la giocata del singolo che riesca a creare superiorità, e oggi non siamo riusciti a trovarla. Voglio comunque fare i complimenti alla squadra per l'impegno, da elogiare sotto questo punto di vista. Siamo mancati negli episodi, e gli episodi poi indirizzano una partita".

"È una squadra gagliarda, con buonissimi giocatori. Lo sapevamo già prima della partita e ritenevamo che la sua posizione di classifica fosse un po' bugiarda. Oggi abbiamo visto una squadra che lotta. Noi dobbiamo anche imparare a giocare queste partite sporche, lo stiamo facendo ma in alcuni momenti perdiamo lucidità".

#2300. Santos impresses in first Man Utd appearance but cannot prevent defeat by Wrexham

Andrey Santos made a bright first Manchester United appearance as they fell to a pre-season friendly loss to Wrexham in Helsinki.

Sam Smith scored the only goal with an easy finish six minutes before half-time, moments after heading against his own crossbar defending a corner.

United were without the players who have featured at this summer’s World Cup – including new signing Youri Tielemans – as well as Benjamin Sesko, but Michael Carrick put out a strong starting XI in front of 20,000 spectators in the Finnish capital.

Santos, who became United’s first summer signing when he joined from Chelsea at the start of the week for an initial £48m, took his place at the base of midfield alongside Mason Mount.

Speaking just before the match, Michael Carrick had praised the 22-year-old’s attitude, saying: “He’s settled in really well, he’s a fantastic character. He’s buzzing to be here, you can see that.”

The Brazilian’s first involvement was to clear the ball away after Tom Heaton failed to gather under pressure from Smith seconds into the game.

Santos was left on his backside by Lewis O’Brien eight minutes in but the chance came to nothing for Wrexham as the flag went up. More encouraging was his sliding block on O’Brien moments later and he soon settled in, showing a good range of passing and winning several duels in a busy display.

However, Phil Parkinson’s side, who played their first pre-season friendly against Wisla Krakow in Poland last weekend, were looking brighter and threatened again when Bailey Cadamarteri nicked the ball off Ayden Heaven on the edge of the box before the defender recovered.

United’s first chance was a Joshua Zirkzee shot that fizzed wide in the 24th minute and they almost went ahead when Smith tried to clear a cornerm but instead sent a header on to his own crossbar in the 36th minute.

Moments later Smith was on the scoresheet at the other end and it looked all too easy as he was left with a tap-in after O’Brien’s cross appeared to go through Harry Maguire’s legs.

Sam Smith with the winning moment 🤌🔴⚪️#WxmAFC pic.twitter.com/YzTvnzIpz6

Twenty-one of the 22 players were replaced at half-time, with only Wrexham’s Aaron James staying on, and Carrick sent out a side entirely composed of academy products, facing a decent test against a Wrexham side now including the likes of Conor Coady and Kieffer Moore.

United dominated the ball but struggled to fashion chances as the pace of the game dropped. Instead, Wrexham threatened with a low shot from Davis Keillor-Dunn but Radek Vitek made the save.

When Ethan Wheatley prodded Harry Amass’ cross goalwards in the 78th minute, it was their first shot on target, but Dan Ward made the save before holding a low drive from Shea Lacey.

Dan Gore hit the deck in the single minute of stoppage time, but his optimistic penalty appeal was waved away.

We knew it wouldn’t be perfect - that’s only natural for the first pre-season game - and the main thing is that everybody came through it in good shape. No injuries so we can move onto the next step next week.

[Andrey Santos] and Mason [Mount] did some really good things and connected really well. There’s loads of little positives to take. The sharpness at the top end will come as we move through pre-season.

I was really pleased with the second half team. They controlled the game really well against a team who aren’t easy to play against. The boys took responsibility and their quality; they can really be proud of themselves.

Man Utd appeal unsuccessfully for a penalty when Dan Gore goes over in the area. Seconds later, the referee blows the final whistle. Wrexham, who were under pressure for much of the second half, have held on to beat Manchester United in a muted pre-season friendly in Helsinki.

Sam Smith scored the only goal in the 39th minute, having headed against his own crossbar three minutes earlier. There were 21 changes at half-time, 11 for Man Utd and 10 for Wrexham.

Andrey Santos, part of an experienced first-half XI, had a decent debut after signing from Chelsea in the week. The senior players looked understandably rusty, and a very youthful replacement XI were more dominant than their seniors. But they struggled to create clear chances and Wrexham deserved their win.

Full-time in Helsinki 🇫🇮First pre-season minutes in the tank for 22 Reds ✔️

Wheatley finds the underlapping Amass, whose pullback is cleared a little desperately by Wrexham. Amass, still only 19, looks really promising at left-back.

Man Utd’s youngsters continue to press for an equaliser. They haven’t created much but the rest of their second-half performance has been impressive.

Ward makes another comfortable save, this time when Shea Lacey tries his luck from 22 yards.

The left-back Harry Amass beats his man and curls a cross that bounces towards Ethan Wheatley at the near post. He stabs it goalwards and Ward makes a comfortable save. Tough chance, though Wheatley did well to get across the defender.

Man Utd’s best move of the second half. Dan Gore runs onto a return pass from Shea Lacey and sweeps a low ball into the six-yard box that is held at the second attempt by Danny Ward.

Wrexham substitution Alex Moore replaces Aaron James, who was the only starter on either side to play part of the second half.

The first chance of the second half falls to Wrexham. After a neat move through midfield, Davis Keillor-Dunn gallops into the area and drives a low shot that Radek Vitek saves well with his legs.

Kamason is booked for a late tackle on Dobson. That looked a bit harsh, certainly in a friendly.

Wrexham - in a back five, heaven forfend - are defending well and keeping the opposition at arm’s length. Unlike Argentina, Man Utd haven’t really tried any crosses yet.

No attempts at goal in the second half, on or off target, from either team. But the young Man Utd side have played some purposeful stuff and have had around 66% possession.

No chances to report but the young Man Utd side have started well, dominating possession and playing with greater urgency than their elders.

And this is the youthful XI that Michael Carrick has put out for the second half.

Man Utd (4-2-3-1) Vitek; Kamason, Devaney, Armer, Amass; Collyer, T Fletcher; Lacey, Gore, Williams; Wheatley.

Wrexham have made 10 changes, with Aaron James the only survivor from the first half. This is their new XI.

Our second-half XI 👇🔴⚪ #WxmAFC pic.twitter.com/pechlNMwxJ

Manchester United begin the second half having made 11 changes at half-time. We’ll have the full teams shortly, all being well.

Wrexham lead after a low-key first half in Helsinki. Sam Smith scored to enliven a half of few chances. Andrey Santos was lively on his Manchester United debut, gobbling up the ground defensively and playing forward at every opportunity.

We should have very different teams - perhaps completely new XIs - for the second half.

39 min: Man Utd 0 Wrexham 1 (Smith) Sam Smith gives Wrexham the lead. It came from a well-worked throw-in on the left. Thomason played a one-two before slipping a crisp pass into O’Brien in the area. His precise low cross, through the legs of Maguire, gave Smith a tap-in from three yards.

Man Utd hit the bar Mason Mount’s inswinging corner from the left is headed against his own crossbar by Sam Smith, woh was off balance as he challenged Leny Yoro. That’s the closest we’ve come to a goal at either end.

Broadhead wriggles away from Andrey Santos on the edge of the area, but Santos snaps back at him and Broadhead curls over the bar.

Zirkzee pulls up gingerly after being caught by a Wrexham player. Looks like an in impact injury rather than a muscle problem.

Santos and Mount probe on the edge of the Wrexham area. A through ball is cut out and rebounds towards Zirkzee, who whistles a snapshot wide from 20 yards. Not a bad effort.

Patrick Dorgu’s shot is blocked on the edge of the area. United are starting to find a bit of rhythm after a slow start.

Cadamarteri surges into the area and is about to shoot when Heaven makes an excellent lunging challenge. Wrexham look more likely to score at this point.

Smith barges Andrey Santos over long after the ball has gone. A bit of a needless challenge, one that Santos did not especially appreciate.

Both teams look rusty, United in particular. Wrexham have been a bit more direct and slightly more dangerous in attack.

Andrey Santos loses the ball in midfield, leading to a one-on-one chance for Sam Smith that is well saved by Heaten. Smith was offside so it wouldn’t have counted.

That opportunity aside, it’s been a predictably quiet start - lots of passing in midfield from United in particular.

The new signing Andrey Santos makes an important interception after 40 seconds. Nathan Broadhead seemed to foul the keeper Tom Heaton in the United area, but play continued and Broadhead’s ball across was turned behind by Santos.

Wrexham, in their blue change strip, kick off from right to left as we watch.

Both teams line up for the usual pre-match formalities. Harry Maguire and Matty James, a former Man Utd academy player, are the captains.

We’ve been back in training 10 days and we’re taking it step by step. It’s great to be back at it again.

Andrey Santos is a fantastic character and he’s settled in really well. He’s buzzing to be here and he’ll do really well for us. We’re not expecting anything crazy special today - it’s a step, just get your eye in and get back on the pitch. I’m really looking forward to the progression he shows while he’s here.

Youri Tielemans is targeting more silverware after completing his £35m move to Manchester United.

Tielemans has signed a five-year contract at Old Trafford after United triggered his release clause at Aston Villa.

The Belgium international played a key role in helping Villa lift the Europa League last season, but pushed for the move to United after turning down the offer of a new contract in the West Midlands.

“The ambition from everyone at the club is extremely clear; we are all determined to push for the biggest trophies,” he said.

“Signing for such a special club feels incredible, it is the culmination of years of dedication since I first fell in love with football. I have had the privilege of experiencing success in the game and it has only increased my determination to achieve more.”

I’m not sure when Man Utd last played Wrexham in a friendly, but the most recent competitive meeting between the sides was in January 1995. It was three days after Eric Cantona tried to kick xenophobia out of football at Selhurst Park, so United’s 5-2 win was somewhat overshadowed.

Andrey Santos starts in what is a pretty strong United XI.

Lining up for our first fixture of pre-season! 🇫🇮Watch LIVE on MUTV ⤵️

Our first-half XI in Helsinki 🇫🇮🔴⚪ #WxmAFC pic.twitter.com/WrXbc2B7JQ

The World Cup final? Pah! The 2026-27 Premier League season is just over a month away, and Manchester United’s pre-season begins this afternoon with a friendly against Wrexham in Helsinki.

Man Utd have started many seasons with a whimper since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement 13 years ago, but there’s plenty of summer optimism around Old Trafford. Michael Carrick overachieved so spectacularly as caretaker manager that a full-time appointment became inevitable. Now all he has to do is maintain that league form across a full season while also juggling the Champions League.

United have filled part of their midfield void by signing Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa. Tielemans is having a post-World Cup break but Santos is part of a United squad that also includes Bryan Mbeumo, Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, Mason Mount, Patrick Dorgu and Leny Yoro.

“Everything about Manchester United is special,” said Santos after signing for the club earlier in the week. “It is an incredible feeling to join a club that some of my biggest idols have represented. As a midfielder, I am really excited to have the opportunity to learn from Michael Carrick. He is the perfect coach to help me take the next step in my career and push to achieve my dreams.”

Wrexham have ambitions to play United in a competitive fixture sooner rather than later. They missed out on the Championship playoffs but will go again with a very similar squad.

“This is a great test for us, it really is,” said their manager Phil Parkinson. “As always, when we were in the other divisions we looked to these games as a test and this will be absolutely no different.

“The out-of-possession stuff becomes really important against the better quality teams. But as we’ve always done, we’re not just going to these games to stop the opposition.”

After 55 long days...It's a United matchday! 🇾🇪❤️

#2298. Il nuovo Sarri della Serie A ha seriamente rischiato di farsi cacciare a metà agosto, ma ora raccoglie i frutti di 26 anni di lavoro. E ai piani alti c'è chi si sfrega le mani

"Dal modello di gioco alla preparazione della partita: affrontare il Napoli di Maurizio Sarri". Nel 2018 Massimiliano Alvini a Coverciano otteneva il patentino Uefa Pro con una tesi con questo titolo. Da sempre estimatore del tecnico che oggi vive momenti molto complicati all'Atalanta, allena da 26 anni. Ha ottenuto sette promozioni e partendo dalla Promozione ha scalato tutte le categorie. Prima il Signa e poi il Quarrata, il doppio salto col Tuttocuoio per iniziare dopo nove stagioni di onorata carriera nel calcio regionale una lunga traversata tra Serie D e Serie C. Ha saggiato il campionato cadetto per la prima volta sei anni fa, poi due stagioni più tardi la prima avventura in Serie A: diciotto gare alla guida della Cremonese senza vincerne una e il ritorno in cadetteria per ricostruirsi. Lo Spezia, il Cosenza e poi la svolta definitiva a Frosinone.

Quella di Massimiliano Alvini non è la storia di un predestinato, ma quella di un tecnico che ha sempre creduto di poter arrivare in Serie A. Che quando poteva accontentarsi di una carriera discreta ha imposto il salto di qualità prima a sé stesso e poi alle sue squadre. "Ci ammazza ogni giorno sia a parole che con gli esercizi. In allenamento piangiamo, ma alla fine sorridiamo in partita. Lavoriamo tantissimo, in spogliatoio sento solo ragazzi che si lamentano di quanto fatichiamo, però poi in partita sentiamo nel corso quanto ci fa bene questo lavoro", ha dichiarato recentemente Daniel Birligea, attaccante che adesso con l'infortunio di Antonio Raimondo sarà chiamato a dare molto di più alla causa giallazzurra.

Oggi Alvini guida una neopromossa sesta in classifica che ha conquistato venti punti in dieci partite. Per origini, per curriculum e per percorso di crescita sembra poter diventare il nuovo Maurizio Sarri. Può emulare il percorso di un allenatore che proprio come lui s'è consacrato tardi, ma poi s'è rifatto con gli interessi. Che oggi è in difficoltà, ma ha espresso un calcio magnifico alla guida del Napoli e poi ha vinto con la Juventus e col Chelsea. Questo Alvini oggi non può non essere sulla bocca e nei pensieri di tutti i presidenti di Serie A, ma solo due mesi e mezzo fa il suo divorzio dal Frosinone sembrava cosa probabile. Il più quotato dai bookmakers. Ricordate?

Era il 16 agosto e dopo la gara di Coppa Italia contro la Juve Stabia sulla campagna acquisti decisa dal fondo statunitense si esprimeva così: "Sono giocatori che non ho scelto. Sono giocatori che sono arrivati, li devo allenare, li devo conoscere. Devo conoscerli per schierarli. Io non sono stato coinvolto nel mercato: io e Castagnini siamo stati coinvolti soltanto nelle conferme dello scorso anno di Cittadini, Calvani, Raimondo e Fini. E poi Amey e Desplanches. Il resto dei giocatori sono arrivati e ci vorrà del tempo per conoscerli e capirli". Nel mirino i dirigenti del fondo Clara Vista Investment Partners, un rapporto che sembrava destinato a finire in pochi giorni e che oggi non può che essere diverso. Ma in quel discorso c'è tutto l'allenatore di Fucecchio che in questi 26 anni non è cambiato: spigoloso e sincero, disposto a perdere ma non a sacrificare le sue idee.

Alvini il 16 agosto aveva ragione perché il Frosinone che oggi vola in campionato ha avuto grazie al fondo Clara Vista la forza di trattenere Ghedjemis e investire circa 25 milioni per Bobcek e Schmid. Per Hasa, Terzic, Birligea, Tchato e Fayed, per ingaggiare Grillitsch e Akpoguma. Ma oggi se i canarini sono lì in alto è soprattutto per la volontà di Alvini di confermare il blocco della promozione. Di trattenere Calò quando tutti tranne lui pensavano fosse un giocatore di Serie B, di puntare su giocatori come Palmisani e Oyono, su Calvani e Raimondo. Su Monterisi, Cittadini, Bracaglia, Cichella, Fini, Kvernadze e Ghedjemis. Tutti calciatori che oggi sono sulla bocca di tutti, ma quanti tifosi neutrali li conoscevano fino a poche settimane fa? E soprattutto, quanto è aumentato oggi il loro valore in meno di tre mesi?

L'impressione è che oggi solo Palmisani, Raimondo, Calvani, Kvernadze, Ghedjemis e Schmid messi insieme valgano non meno di 150 milioni di euro. Non tutti sono di proprietà del Frosinone, ma tutti resteranno fino alla fine della stagione e poi si vedrà. Perché oggi Clara Vista è importante soprattutto per dare al club questa forza economica, una stabilità che permette al Frosinone di avere già una rosa molto ricca grazie soprattutto allo straordinario lavoro di Massimiliano Alvini. Cinquantasei anni di cui 26 trascorsi sulle panchine di tutte le categorie, esperienze a tutti i livelli fondamentali per arrivare esattamente dov'è adesso.

Primo posto in solitaria? Per me non cambia l’obiettivo, ma hai vinto bene una partita non facile. Hai preso punti sulle inseguitrici, ti sei allontanato ancora dal settimo posto. Secondo me ieri è mancato, a parte il ritmo, l’apporto di giocatori importantissimi; se mi bloccano a sinistra, in mezzo o a destra devono lasciare qualcosa, e lì sono un po’ mancati Belahyane e Frattesi. Isaksen mi è sempre piaciuto tanto, ho sempre detto che ha grandi qualità ma è timido, poco coraggioso. Sostengo da tempo che, trovando la chiave giusta, sarebbe diventato un grande giocatore e ora stiamo vedendo questo.

#2294. Avellino, Favilli: "Siamo una squadra forte che può fare bene ma serve equilibrio"

L'attaccante dell'Avellino Andrea Favilli è stato ospite di Speciale Serie B, trasmissione in onda su Sportitalia. Queste le sue parole riportate da TuttoAvellino.it.

"La vittoria sul Pisa? Siamo contenti, era una partita importante, arrivata dopo 3 risultati così così, inoltre una vittoria arrivata contro una squadra molto forte. Ora ci prepariamo per il derby con il Benevento. Da pisano era una gara speciale, la gara contro la squadra della mia città. Ma sono felice di aver vinto”.

Gli infortuni: “Ho pagato molto a caro prezzo la sfortuna. Quest'anno sono contento perché ho fatto un bel ritiro, ho messo le basi per una buona stagione. Sto bene per fortuna”.

Su mister Ballardini: “Abbiamo raggiunto un grande obiettivo l'anno scorso, i playoff erano una chimera al suo arrivo. Siamo contenti per quei mesi insieme, è stato bello davvero, il mister ga compattato il gruppo e l'ambiente, ponendo basi importanti”.

Sulla squadra: “Con mister Nesta eravamo partiti con altre idee tattiche, poi dopo la gara con l'Arezzo siamo virati per il 3-5-2 e per me per le mezze ali che abbiamo, con il centrocampo a tre questa squadra rende meglio. Il campionato è lungo, ci sono sempre degli alti e bassi che fanno alzare e abbassare gli umori. Bisogna avere continuità ed equilibrio, testa bassa. Io credo che la squadra sia molto forte, ci sino giocatori che spostano come Russo che in questo momento è tra i migliori della B. E il nostro gioiellino dai. Però c'è bisogno di equilibrio, venivamo da tre gare senza vincere e si sentivano i primi mugugni, ora dopo il Pisa c'è entusiasmo. Serve equilibrio. La Serie B ha alzato il livello, non ci sono squadre materasso come 10 anni fa, dove sapevi già che quelle 2-3 sarebbero retrocesse. Da alcuni anni non è così, tolto il Palermo, che fa un campionato a sé, credo che tutti possono fare bene e la sorpresa può esserci, sia in positivo che in negativo. Se sarà l'Avellino in positivo? Speriamo”.

Sui migliori attaccanti del campionato: “Se sta bene, credo che Belotti possa fare 25 gol, è troppo forte, fuori categoria, il Modena è una squadra che attacca tanto. Contro di noi non c'era, ma il Gallo è uno che il gol ce l'ha nel sangue”.

Un rimpianto: “Parlare di rimpianti è difficile, avrei voluto avere la serietà e la determinazione di oggi quando avevo 19 anni. Avrei voluto giocarmi le chance in Serie A con la testa di adesso. Io spingo forte e spero di riprendermi quello che ho perso per strada. Ho 29 anni, qualche anno buono posso farlo ancora”.

Una parola per descrivere il gruppo Avellino: “Siamo pazzi scatenati”.

Giovanni Di Lorenzo, terzino del Napoli, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni a DAZN, dopo il match contro la Juventus: “Abbiamo tante partite sulle gambe e non stavo già bene prima della partita, dispiace perchè volevo continuare, ma per non peggiorare sono uscito. Dispiace perchè avevamo avuto un approccio propositivo nel primo tempo, poi nella ripresa non abbiamo mantenuto lo stesso livello. Era importante per noi per il morale e per la classifica, siamo amareggiati. E’ un momento difficile, ci sta mancando la continuità, facciamo delle buone partite e poi altro meno buone, anche durante la partita non riusciamo ad essere continui. Ora lavoriamo e continuiamo a stare insieme per ribaltare la situazione, dobbiamo migliorare la classifica. Se siamo in questa situazione significa che tutti dobbiamo alzare il livello, me compreso. Siamo consapevoli del momento per migliorare, poi i risultati in questo momento non ci aiutano, ma la squadra farà di tutto per migliorare. L’abbraccio con Spalletti? Mi ha chiesto come stava la famiglia, abbiamo un bel rapporto e ricordo con piacere gli anni sotto la sua guida. E’ sempre bello rivederlo”.

#2289. Pellegrino contro il Sassuolo vuol dire partire da 1-0. A Firenze segna solo di piede

Si è finalmente sbloccato Mateo Pellegrino. L'attaccante argentino è stato fra i protagonisti del ritorno al successo della Fiorentina, capace di espugnare il Mapei Stadium per 2-4. Un gol che ha cambiato la partita della viola che fino a quel momento stava rischiando di andare all'intervallo in svantaggio e depressa e che invece ha fatto scattare la scintilla che ha portato alla vittoria. Ci volevano i neroverdi, con i quali il giocatore ha un conto aperto: in 3 partite giocate contro di loro ha sempre segnato.

52 giorni di digiuno in Serie A, gli stessi che ha impiegato la Fiorentina per vincere una partita. Da allora prestazioni mai all'altezza, tante insufficienze rimediate e risultati che latitavano. Colpa anche di prestazioni di squadra non all'altezza, che hanno lasciato il giocatore isolato e senza sfruttare al meglio le sue qualità nel gioco aereo.

Pellegrino si è presentato a Firenze con caratteristiche chiare: a Parma, nel 3-5-2 di Cuesta i cross per il centravanti erano uno schema fisso per trovare la via del gol, che ha portato di fatto a 11 reti di testa sulle 15 complessive. Qualità mai sfruttata quest'anno, non a caso fin qui le 4 reti segnate fra campionato e Coppa Italia sono arrivate solo di piede: 3 di sinistro e 1 di destro, considerando anche la Coppa Italia. Rende l'idea delle difficoltà fin qui emerse: il suo xG è di 1.61 e la sua media tiri in porta a partita è di 0.50. Paradossalmente l'argentino è riuscito a segnare più di quanto potesse essere previsto, statistiche alla mano. Dati che vanno necessariamente migliorati. E chissà che questa rete non lo abbia sbloccato.

#2288. Tuchel learns lesson as England clinch third place in 10-goal thriller

Was this evidence of England head coach Thomas Tuchel already learning lessons from the Argentina collapse? Let’s hope so.

With England on the ropes and in danger of throwing away a lead against France, Tuchel resisted the temptation to flood his team with defenders and was rewarded with a World Cup bronze medal.

England looked on course to secure an emphatic victory to clinch the nation’s best World Cup finish since 1966 and yet Tuchel was left with the exact same scenario that had gone so badly against Argentina in the semi-final.

Leading by four goals at half-time, England somehow went into the final hydration break of this bronze medal game with a single-goal advantage. This time, Tuchel steered England over the line by getting his late substitutions right.

Jude Bellingham stepped off the bench to cap a wonderful tournament for him with the goal that made sure England finished the World Cup in third place.

It may have resembled an exhibition match at times, with France failing to turn up in the first half. But England’s thrilling 6-4 victory will send Tuchel home from the United States feeling a little bit better, even though he is not yet off the hook for what happened in Atlanta.

The fact that success against France was earned with a Bukayo Saka hat-trick, as well as goals from Declan Rice, Ezri Konsa and Bellingham, will prompt more debate over Tuchel’s decision-making when it really mattered. Not least why Saka watched the entire Argentina game from the substitutes’ bench.

Tuchel cut a relaxed figure, changing his touchline attire to a casual white T-shirt and tracksuit bottoms. But his team meant business, as they raced into a stunning four-goal first-half lead.

Saka played like a man with a point to prove. He scored twice and produced the shot from which England won the corner for Konsa’s goal in the opening 45 minutes. Was this a message to Tuchel or simply the winger taking out his frustration on France?

France looked uninterested from the start and it was a loose Désiré Doué pass that gifted possession to Rice. As England’s captain for the evening strode forwards, Doué did not bother to track him and Rice curled a lovely shot into the corner of the net to give Tuchel’s team a third-minute lead.

It's a quick start from England! 🦁⚡Declan Rice fires home the opener in the third minute against France ⚽ pic.twitter.com/ID4u3rXOuM

Having been criticised for sending on three defenders against Argentina, Tuchel started with five attacking players on the pitch and just Rice in front of the defence.

Saka had a goal correctly ruled out for offside before his shot was blocked for a corner, from which England doubled their lead. Rice turned provider, as he sent in a perfect delivery that was headed past goalkeeper Mike Maignan by Konsa five minutes before the first hydration break.

The Three Lions double their lead! 🦁⚽Ezri Konsa rises highest from Declan Rice's corner to head home 🙌 pic.twitter.com/8BfI1LSDOQ

While Tuchel would have been delighted with his team’s start to the game, Saka’s influence raises just as many questions as answers.

Saka was the next England player on the scoresheet. He sent Marcus Rashford away on goal. Rashford’s shot was saved, but England kept the ball alive and Saka eventually found the back of the net via a deflection.

The Three Lions lead France by three goals! 🦁🔥Bukayo Saka finishing off a quick England counter-attack ⚽ pic.twitter.com/9SCfE3uH3v

England had been given much sterner tests by DR Congo and Panama, and yet Tuchel’s players deserve praise for capitalising on such a terrible first-half performance from France.

Ebererchi Eze could not have believed that he was given the time and space to turn and pick out Saka on the stroke of half-time. He did so superbly and Saka easily added England’s fourth goal.

🗣 "France are being taken apart by England!" Bukayo Saka scores his second for the Three Lions' FOURTH goal against the two-time world champions 🤯 pic.twitter.com/4RshXY692E

It perhaps summed up France’s mentality that Kylian Mbappé, who threatened on a couple of occasions in the first half, reacted to England’s fourth goal with what appeared to be a slight smirk.

Tuchel’s name had been booed by some of those, mostly neutral supporters, inside the Hard Rock Stadium ahead of kick-off.

His star has undoubtedly fallen as a result of the Argentina defeat and yet nobody could have failed to have been impressed by what his and his players produced in the first half on Saturday night, however bad France had been.

When Tuchel made a change at half-time, there was no Dan Burn sent on to try to see out a 4-0 win. Instead, it was an attacking substitution with Ollie Watkins replacing Rashford. It immediately backfired, but Tuchel was later rewarded for trying to remain positive.

Watkins’s first act was to lose the ball on the halfway line to start a France attack that ended in a goal. Michael Olise played in Mbappé, who slotted the ball past Dean Henderson, who was given a rare chance ahead of Jordan Pickford.

France substitute Bradley Barcola pulled another goal back in the 54th minute, which meant that England’s four-goal advantage had been halved in just nine second-half minutes.

There was still no call for Burn, as Tuchel stuck to his gung-ho approach and Henderson had to save well from Ousmane Dembélé, who had also been sent on at the break. England had lost their balance with the half-time change and Olise was the next France attacker to go close.

Dembélé tested Henderson again before Mbappé got France’s third goal just before the final hydration break to pass Lionel Messi as the World Cup’s all-time top scorer. Like they had against Argentina, England had dropped deep and invited pressure as their opposition grew in confidence.

Kylian Mbappe scores his 22nd World Cup goal to become the leading goalscorer in the history of the competition ⚽🔥👏 pic.twitter.com/sDTNnW0kLZ

Having led so comfortably at half-time, England went into the final quarter of the game with a slender one-goal lead – just as they had against Argentina in Atlanta.

Olise somehow missed a sitter after arriving late on the end of a low ball across the penalty area and Tuchel decided it was time for more changes. But it was Elliot Anderson and Bellingham he called for, rather than any extra defenders, and it ultimately paid dividends.

Bellingham almost dribbled his way through to put the result beyond doubt, before Olise squandered another wonderful opportunity. Mercifully, Djed Spence won an 85th-minute penalty that allowed Saka to complete his hat-trick.

Bukayo Saka completes his hat-trick from the penalty spot! ⚽3️⃣England lead France 5-3 in the closing stages of this game 🦁 pic.twitter.com/EnYOg8UAvT

There was still time for Dembélé to briefly up England’s anxiety levels again, before Bellingham put the finishing touch to what has been an outstanding World Cup for him with a brilliant goal.

Jude Bellingham grabbing England's SIXTH goal against France! 🦁Driving over the halfway line before firing a shot into the bottom corner 🔥👏 pic.twitter.com/l0B0BVs548

The players made sure to invite Jason Steele on to the stage to receive a medal. The Brighton goalkeeper is not in England’s World Cup squad, but travelled to North America as a training goalkeeper.

Of course I would love to have played more but it’s too late to talk about that. I try to do my talking on the pitch and it’s done now, move on. I’m fit.

We built and built across the tournament. We had some amazing results and in the end we fell short against Argentina. It hurts a lot to all of us and I’m sure it’s the same to the fans back home but we have to hold out head high and focus on the next one.

France are not hanging around for the ceremony. They are down the tunnel as organisers set up a stage to hand out the bronze medals. Probably sums up their attitude to the game.

Enough for four matches, what happened here. We had a brilliant first half, then a turbulent second half. You could see the difference of what one day makes and the difference in the schedule. We are so, so tired and drained from the last weeks.

So a massive compliment and full respect - the mentality that we showed. Going through all the adversity is absolutely brilliant.

I was afraid of the physical demands of the match. We know the quality and speed of France, and they have much less schedule for them. It was less demanding.

They had one more day in-between the semi-final to digest, and they had way less travel distances than us.

We played in the heat, at altitude. I was worried physically. You could see it in the second half, the cramps and all the tiredness, but I was never worried about the mentality.

I have said it before, this team has created something very special, and they showed it again.

However we got here England have had their best World Cup since 1966. Whatever criticism Thomas Tuchel received after Argentina defeat he deserves to keep his job and the chance to put things right in 2028 #england

Some players from France and England are huddled near the halfway line praying. Among them are Dayot Upamecano, Maxence Lacroix, Trevoh Chalobah and Bukayo Saka. Very different atmosphere to the Argentina defeat three days ago in Atlanta. They are playing Wonderwall here as they prepare for the bronze medals to be handed out but it is not very celebratory this time.

When does the second set start? That was as much as you could hope for from a third/fourth-place play-off. Some slack defending, some high-quality combination play and lots of entertainment. England’s victory stops things spiralling further for Tuchel, but there will be a sense of what might have been, not least the fact Saka played no part in the semi-final.

Bellingham’s seventh goal of the tournament, which is the highest tally by an England player at a World Cup. The game was stretched, but it was a fantastic individual goal from Bellingham, carrying the ball forward from the halfway line. He showed great composure not to take the shot too early, taking extra touches to finish with aplomb.

A seventh goal of the tournament for Jude Bellingham! 7️⃣⭐The most EVER by an Englishman at a single World Cup 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿👏 pic.twitter.com/YACnNWvqW1

Good work from Reece James to keep the ball and then defend well against Barcola.

What a barmy game this has been. Upamecano started the move with good defending and a surge forward, and then Dembele cuts inside Chalobah and buries a shot into the bottom corner.

🇫🇷 Ousmane Dembele scores France's fourth goal against England ⚽ pic.twitter.com/U4gCVb1tQw

Spence down and receiving some treatment for cramp after winning a challenge against Olise. France not happy with the stoppage in the game.

Excellent Rice challenge, and then Bellingham wins a free-kick in midfield. Rice can hardly run yet managed to time his challenge well. Trevoh Chalobah replaces Marc Guehi.

Seven minutes of added time to play, and France have just been caught offside from their own short corner.

That is England’s first World Cup hat-trick since Harry Kane scored three against Panama in the 2018 finals. But Bukayo Saka’s treble is also the last England hat-trick in all competitions since.... Bukayo Saka. The Arsenal forward also scored three times in the win over North Macedonia in 2023.

That was very unselfish from Jude Bellingham, because had he scored the penalty it would have been his seventh goal of the tournament. That would be the most goals scored by an England player at a World Cup.

Sends Maignan the wrong way, and picks out the bottom corner. Saka has his hat-trick, and England are surely assured of third place and the bronze medal/trophy. England’s players will be most pleased to avoid extra time.

Bukayo Saka completes his hat-trick from the penalty spot! ⚽3️⃣England lead France 5-3 in the closing stages of this game 🦁 pic.twitter.com/EnYOg8UAvT

Won by Djed Spence, who was too sharp by Malo Gusto. Once the England full-back got his toe to the ball, it was a stonewall penalty. Morgan Rogers played the pass to release him on the overlap.

Bellingham or Saka for the hat-trick? Bellingham has the ball in his hands, but then passes it to Saka for the hat-trick.

Qunsah off, Reece James on. That also looks a case of cramp in very humid conditions in Miami.

Now Olise misses a sitter! Great interplay in the box involving Olise and Dembele, five-a-side football between the France forwards, but the finish was lacking. Olise, and then the referee, receive some treatment for cramp.

England with a great chance to wrap the game up but Bellingham fluffed his lines! Burst through, the benefit of fresh legs, but he carried the ball too close to Maignan and then Rogers’s follow up was blocked.

Ivan Toney and Eberechi Eze are the players coming off, Bellingham and Anderson on, which adds some strength to England’s midfield.

That is a big cheer for Bellingham coming on, one of the stars of the World Cup and appreciated by the neutral. His job here is to see out a win.

France continue to dominate, and they have a free-kick in a crossing position. Cleared by Eze. Elliott Anderson is ready to come on, as well as Bellingham. Digne finds Mbappe, but Konsa makes a good block. Rogers then does well to make it stick and buy a foul.

Great chance for France to equalise, but Michael Olise opened up his foot too much and his shot flew past the post. France look like scoring every time they venture into England’s defensive third. Mbappe goes down looking for a penalty, but nothing doing, before Digne fouls Saka in the box. May have been knee on knee contact, looked a sore one for Saka. Bellingham is ready to come on.

Rice is still out there, soldiering on. Somewhat surprising that Tuchel has not added fresh legs since his half-time changes. Better spell of possession in the last few minutes from England. There have been 15 shots on target in this game.

Play has stopped immediately after the goal for the hydration break. Tuchel mist be thinking about changes. Rice is struggling.

A penny for Mikel Arteta's thoughts watching this: if one of his first comments during pre-season isn't an eruption about how Declan Rice has been asked to play again, he will have mellowed. He's as tired as an also ran at the end of the Grand National.

This is a fantastic France goal, razor sharp link up play between Mbappe and Olise at the edge of the box, and the France captain’s finish was unerring. Drilled into the bottom corner with his left foot. Liquid football. Defending remains optional in this game, but that goal would have graced any game. Mbappe’s 22nd World Cup goal.

Over to you Lionel! Mbappe’s 10th goal of the World Cup means he is the clear leader in the Golden Boot table - but Lionel Messi has a chance in the final tomorrow to add to his eight goals. You would not bet against Mbappe adding to his total here. England have been guilty of dropping deep again, just like they did against Argentina. They are a 4-4-2 with Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney partnering each other. This was just before the “hydration”, so Tuchel could change it up now.

Kylian Mbappe scores his 22nd World Cup goal to become the leading goalscorer in the history of the competition ⚽🔥👏 pic.twitter.com/sDTNnW0kLZ

There is a loud chant coming from the stands: “Mexico!” That shows the diversity of the crowd here, with empty seats in sections including the England supporters. In just one small block of fans in front of the press box, there are shirts from Colombia, Inter Miami, Chile and USA.

France should probably be back to within one goal, but Ousmane Dembele scuffed his shot from a favourable position in the box and it was a simple save for Henderson. Then the goalkeeper pushes away a long-range hit by Upamecano.

Delightful scooped pass over the top of the France defence by Eze but Toney could not bring the ball under his spell off his chest. Then Spence does brilliantly to win a tackle and then turn defence into attakc with a surging run forward.

Morgan Rogers with a sloppy pass inside his own half, and Olise fires wide from the edge of the box. He had so much time and space to line it up. Some fatigue starting to show in England’s legs now.

This is what Tuchel was talking about when he discussed England playing under pressure. France have decided to show up and all of a sudden the deficit is only two goals. Get ready for a testing half an hour.

England go close to another set-piece goal, but Maignan saves well after Toney rose to meet Rice’s inswinging delivery. There are surely going to be more goals in this game.

Henderson stands up well to save from Dembele, but the flag belatedly was raised for offside. A lot of wasted energy for Declan Rice, who had sprinted back some 60 yards to defend. England now the team being repeatedly exposed in transition.

Mbappe with the ball inside Quansah, who loses track of Barcola and with his pace that is always fatal. It looked like Barcola might have overrun the ball, but he got his shot off in time to find the bottom corner.

It's a second goal for France! 🇫🇷Kylian Mbappe's long pass finds Bradley Barcola who fires home 🔥 pic.twitter.com/h4GvkBZOSN

Great play from Eze, close control and quick feet to skip through two or three France challenges in midfield, and he tried to chip Maignan from the halfway line. Always drifting wide.

Composed football from England, playing out from deep in their own half with Rice finding Rogers between the lines. Saka with a pass into Watkins but his shot was tame. Then England and Spence were caught forward, but Rice got his toe to the ball ahead of Olise. Then Rabiot volleys not far wide. Chances galore in this game.

France reduce the deficit through Mbappe’s ninth goal of the tournament. Watkins was caught in possession by Upamecano on halfway, and France found Olise free in the No 10 zone. Lovely through ball splits the England defence, and Mbappe finishes first time beyond Henderson with his left foot.

France hit back after the break! 🇫🇷💥Kylian Mbappe pulls one back with his ninth goal at the 2026 World Cup ⚽ pic.twitter.com/Hxfg1s46ER

Hernandez, Konate, Cherki and Doue off, Digne, Upamecano, Barcola and Dembele on for France.

Ollie Watkins replaces Marcus Rashford for England.

England will fly back home tonight with the feel-good factor of a win against a World Cup heavyweight but it would be foolish to think any of Thomas Tuchel’s problems are solved. In fact, Bukayo Saka’s two first-half goals only leads to the question: why was he left on the bench against Argentina? And Ezri Konsa for that matter. England did not lose a game that Konsa started and it was harsh to bench him against Argentina last Wednesday.

No frustration, I’m a little bit emotional, I can’t find the words to describe just how proud I am of these players. They are playing a game with broken hearts, I see 11 lads out there with broken hearts. I’ve seen them around the hotel the last few days, broken hearts. They can build a performance like that just through pride of playing for England, the team spirit we’ve built over the last seven weeks it’s been a privilege to watch. I know the cynics will say it is too late but we still play against a world class opponent.

4 - France have conceded four first half goals for the first time since a EURO qualification match against Yugoslavia in April 1968.WOW. pic.twitter.com/SePSwONNA8

Well, hands up who had this scoreline on their “bronze final” bingo card? A scarcely believable 45 minutes, and England have surely secured third place for this World Cup. There has been a lot to like about their attacking play, but for many it will make the frustration of Argentina sting all the more. France have been half-hearted in their defensive approach, but England have put them to the sword in style.

Just the four minutes of first-half stoppage time to play.

It is not a consequential game, but this is still a heck of a half from England. They are making mincemeat of a ragged France team. Eze with a lovely turn in midfield and through ball to his Arsenal team-mate Saka, and he found the bottom corner with an early finish. Four goals before half time.

🗣 "France are being taken apart by England!" Bukayo Saka scores his second for the Three Lions' FOURTH goal against the two-time world champions 🤯 pic.twitter.com/4RshXY692E

France are playing like they have been on the beach since their semi-final defeat by Spain last Tuesday. Tuchel won’t read too much into England’s best finish at a World Cup since 1966. He wants his team to perform under pressure and there has been none of that in this game.

Almost a fourth for England, Rashford’s low cross seemed to run under Toney’s foot when the striker would have had a tap in. Moments earlier, there was another great defensive recovery from Rice to block a Gusto pass.

Saka with a curling cross which is just beyond Rogers and drifts wide of the far post. France showing no signs of tightening up.

Breaking in behind this France high line has been like shelling peas for England. Saka’s pass initially released Rashford on the break, and he had plenty of time to think when running through on goal. Maignan saved, Saka’s rebound was blocked, but it feel back for Rashford who kept his head and picked out Saka who passed the ball into an unguarded net. Pretty farcical France defending.

That was a very close offside call from VAR for Saka’s goal. With Mike Maignan out of his goal, England needed to stay behind two France defenders. Marcus Rashford was about a foot onside before teeing up the third.

The Three Lions lead France by three goals! 🦁🔥Bukayo Saka finishing off a quick England counter-attack ⚽ pic.twitter.com/9SCfE3uH3v

Good save from Dean Henderson to deny Mbappe, who sat down two England defenders. You were waiting for the net to ripple, but his effort was too close to Henderson.

Then England break and Saka is in behind the France back four again, but his first touch is a little heavy, and he can neither get his shot off nor round Maignan.

England looking lively in attack again, Rashford with a delicious nutmeg on Zaire-Emery, before unleashing a swerving shot from almost 30 yards. Maignan was scrambling but he made the save. Rice then makes another ball recovery in midfield.

There is a bronze medal at stake but this match has the feel of an exhibition. There is no intensity to France’s press. Michael Olise is extremely hard-working usually but has allowed opponents to run past him. Players are only coming alive with the ball at their feet.

Quick feet from Mbappe inside the England box, but Declan Rice was well-positioned to win an important challenge. Half an hour into the game, and Mbappe is yet to nudge ahead of Messi in the Golden Boot race.

Guehi with a goal-line clearance after Mbappe squeezed a shot beyond Henderson, but the flag was up for offside in any case. It looked a close call on the replays, was a clever pass by Doue to find Mbappe. Henderson also did well to get something on the shot.

Play has now resumed, and England are back on the front foot after a Rice diagonal out to Quansah.

Time for the first hydration break of the game. Miami is one of the World Cup venues where it is probably appreciated.

You can only play the game in front of you, but England have done that well so far. They find Toney free in the box, but he cannot get his shot off on the swivel.

Mbappe laughing as we walks back to the halfway line, so France are not feeling too stressed, but England are 2-0 up in Miami. Good inswinging delivery from Rice, and Konsa rose highest on the six-yard line to glance a header into the far corner.

The Three Lions double their lead! 🦁⚽Ezri Konsa rises highest from Declan Rice's corner to head home 🙌 pic.twitter.com/8BfI1LSDOQ

Saka is causing France’s defence all manner of problems, this time Eze released him in behind the French defence. Lacroix did well to stick to his task and deflect Saka’s shot over the bar for a corner.

Marc Guehi sticks out a leg to block Mbappe’s low cross after the French forward dropped a shoulder and showed his burst of speed over a few yards. England defend the corner. The game continues to feel open, there’s more space for the attackers on the pitch than there would be in a semi-final.

Bukayo Saka has the ball in the net but the flag goes up for offside. Correct decision, he had just strayed a yard ahead of Hernandez. It was a crisp finish, cutting back inside and finding the bottom corner with his left foot. England finding it quite easy to get in behind France.

The entertainment continues: Cherki with a strike from the edge of the D, which was parried by Henderson before Spence hurried his clearance. Zaire-Emery picked up the loose ball but could not do enough with it.

He did not know too much about it, but an important recovery run from Spence enables him to get his heel to the ball when it looked like Mbappe was away. England continue to move the ball well, looking quite fluent going forward, which will only serve to frustrate fans further.

England flowing forward again, Saka in behind Hernandez and lifting in a cross that came all the way to Rashford at the far post. One touch to control, the second to shoot, but his effort was blocked, deflected behind for a corner. Rice’s delivery is too deep.

Mbappe with a shot inside the England box but it is blocked by the legs of Rice. This kind of game tends to be either soporific or care-free and entertaining, and it feels like this is going to be the latter.

That was Declan Rice’s first World Cup goal – and a beauty of a strike at that. It is still a strange decision to play him and add to his workload. This is not a game to judge Thomas Tuchel’s team on either, as France are not playing with urgency.

Doue with a sloppy pass across midfield when there was a chance for France to break, and Declan Rice intercepted. No France defender stepped out to engage the Arsenal man, and he was able to carry the ball forward unopposed. The finish was sweet, the ball was passed into the bottom corner from just outside the box.

It's a quick start from England! 🦁⚡Declan Rice fires home the opener in the third minute against France ⚽ pic.twitter.com/ID4u3rXOuM

The early indications are that Eze is playing in a deeper midfield position alongside Rice. Good pass from Dean Henderson into the free man Djed Spece behind France’s press. Then Rashford whips in a promising cross form the left towards Ivan Toney.

As expected, there are a fair few empty seats here. In the end where some England fans seem to be congregated there are blocks of green seats visible from the opposite end of the stadium. It could be quite a strange atmosphere with most of the supporters inside the stadium neutrals. There are a lot of Mexico and Colombia shirts.

For the penultimate time in this tournament, it’s time for the giant flags on the pitch and the anthems. Rice and Mbappe lead out their teams.

Tuchel booed when his name read out and picture shown at the Miami Stadium

This is a big evening for Dean Henderson making his first World Cup appearance. The Crystal Palace goalkeeper, 29, earns his sixth cap and an opportunity to stake his claim for the No1 jersey next season.

No, never [did he hesitate about playing them] because Declan gets more and more fit. He gets his fitness back and his health back and for Bukayo there’s no concerns. He didn’t start, he didn’t play in the semi-finals. He’s a key player for us and ready to go.

It’s just common sense. We have so many kilometres in the legs. We have so many travel kilometres in our bones. We have a day less recovery. We come from 10 men in altitude. We come from overtime here in Miami. These two guys, they gave everything physically in every match,. They were ready to go again but we keep them and have them to finish the match for us.

0 - This is England's first FIFA World Cup campaign to not see a Manchester United player feature in any of their games since 1958.Unused. pic.twitter.com/LN3L3e7q5q

We have to regroup, and we have to pick ourselves up and try to finish the tournament on a high.

I have always been hungry for this opportunity. It was frustrating. I only got a few minutes, but that is how football goes sometimes.

Now is my chance to prove I should have got more minutes. There’s a lot of goals in the team and on the bench.

Hopefully, we can bring goals, and hopefully we can finish the tournament on a win.

Thomas Tuchel has risked angering Arsenal by selecting Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka for this game. Rice has been recovering from illness and was running on empty for the last two games. He has also suffered neural pain in his hamstring and describes himself as playing “an obscene amount of games”. This is surely a chance to have a breather. Saka has been managing an Achilles injury all tournament and did not feature against Argentina on Wednesday.

2 - Declan Rice is the second Arsenal player to start a major tournament game for England as captain (World Cup/EURO) after Tony Adams at EURO 1996.Privilege. pic.twitter.com/MWlX7HiWXX

Seven changes to the team that was beaten by Spain, with Zaire-Emery starting in midfield. Rayan Cherki is preferred to Ousmane Dembele.

France XI: Maignan; T. Hernández, Lacroix, Konate, Gusto; Rabiot, Zaïre-Emery; Doue, Cherki, Olise, Mbappe

Subs: Akliouche, Barcola, Dembele, Digne, L. Hernandez, Kante, Kone, Kounde, Mateta, Risser, Saliba, Samba, Tchouameni, Thuram, Upamecano

Some of Tuchel’s regular starters do drop to the bench: Pickford, Kane and Bellingham the notable names. Slightly surprising that Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka both start given their ongoing niggles. It is a very attacking team with Rice sitting behind Morgan Rogers and Eze. Is Tuchel making a point there?

England XI: D. Henderson; Quansah, Konsa, Guehi, Spence; Rice, Eze; Saka, Rogers, Rashford; Toney

Subs: Pickford, O’Reilly, Stones, Anderson, Kane, Bellingham, Chalobah, J. Henderson, Burn, Gordon, Watkins, Madueke, Trafford, James

Kobbie Mainoo’s back injury means that he not only misses out today, but it also means he ends this World Cup without playing a single minute of the tournament. Ivan Toney gets his first start and you’d imagine Trevoh Chalobah will get off the substitutes’ bench at some stage for his first World Cup minutes. It’s certainly an attacking team, but it’s also a slightly strange one.

Our XI to face France 💪 pic.twitter.com/UexpADmHPr

Matt Law was one of the journalists in Tuchel’s absorbing pre-match press conference, and says he appeared wounded and possibly shaken. Matt writes: “There was some spikiness from Tuchel, when he deflected the odd question back to the reporter who asked it, and he was fidgety when not speaking, messing with the earpiece in front of him on the desk and twisting the wires. He did not look comfortable.”

The Morgan Rogers transfer to Chelsea means that two England players have moved for a British record fee during this World Cup.

Elliot Anderson moved to Manchester City for £116m and Rogers has cost Chelsea £117m. That means England have two players who have moved for a combined £233m during this tournament.

England vice-captain Declan Rice cost Arsenal more than £100m in 2023. I haven’t done the maths, but it’s fair to guess that England’s first-choice starting line up would be worth near enough £1bn.

He takes an excellent set-piece and his athleticism is to be admired, but do you ever see him dictate the tempo of a match in the way that Rodri will attempt to do for Spain when they face Argentina on Sunday in New Jersey? The blunt answer is no. He doesn’t have cute, clever balls in his armoury.

There was a bolt of lightning in the distance on arrival at the Hard Rock Stadium. The last thing this Bronze match needs is a delay to prolong the agony of this match. John Stones was distraught doing his pre-match media duties yesterday. It is harsh to ask players to get themselves up for this game after the devastation of losing to Argentina on Wednesday.

Morgan Rogers is on his way to Chelsea for a record £117m fee, in news which comes as a blow to Arsenal’s summer transfer plans. Rogers started the semi-final on England’s right flank and he is likely to be involved again tonight.

He leaves France having won a World Cup and reached the final in another. This team has arguably played the best football of the lot, but will finish empty-handed. The smart money is on Zinedine Zidane replacing him, who won three consecutive Champions Leagues while Real Madrid head coach. So he knows his way around knockout football.

Neither England nor France wanted to be playing this game in Miami, but they can have no complaints about the nature of their semi-final defeats.

Tournament favourites France were comprehensively outplayed by Spain, with their feted front four of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Bradley Barcola and Michael Olise all turning in below-par performances.

England’s defeat by Argentina was perhaps not as much of a surprise, but the nature of Thomas Tuchel’s team’s second-half collapse was just as alarming as France’s no-show.

England’s manager was fiercely criticised for replacing Anthony Gordon with Ezri Konsa and switching to a back five in the 72nd minute, but Tuchel has since defended his decisions.

“If you are asking if I regret my decisions, if this is the question, then I say no. I don’t regret my ‌decisions because I ‌felt that we became ⁠too passive,” said Tuchel.

“I took several decisions, trusting my instinct, my intuition, my experience, trusting my competitiveness, and I took the decision in order to help the team and get the result.

“I would regret if I didn’t help. I would regret ⁠if we didn’t react, but I have no regrets over the decision itself.”

Quite how strong Didier Deschamps and Tuchel decide to go with their teams is anyone’s guess. There has been some suggestion that Mbappe will start to give him the chance to beat Lionel Messi to the Golden Boot.

Some of England’s regular starters, such as Declan Rice, look physically spent, so there could be some rotation, and even a chance for players such as Kobbie Mainoo who has not played a minute of football at the tournament.

The third/fourth-place play-off has been rebranded as the “Bronze Final” for this tournament, and Tuchel was keen to point out that finishing third would be England’s best World Cup result since 1966. They lost this fixture against Belgium in 2018, but the way that game has been widely forgotten speaks volumes.

Antonio Cassano, dagli studi di "Viva El Futbol", è tornato sulla sconfitta dell'Inter nel derby contro il Milan: "L'Inter sta facendo malissimo, con una squadra del genere non ti puoi permettere di fare partite così brutte. Come di consueto, Daniele Adani, ex calciatore e ora opinionista, è intervenuto in diretta sul canale di Viva el Futbol.

L'ex difensore dell'Inter ha analizzato il momento dei nerazzurri e in particolare la sconfitta nel derby per 3-1 contro il Milan, nella sfida valida per il 10° turno di Serie A disputata sabato sera a San Siro.

"Le strade del cambiamento, del rimodellamento, delle nuove idee… Diceva il grande Luca Vialli che le 'idee invecchiano presto'. Questo si sa, ragazzi, che le idee invecchiano presto. Quindi probabilmente il rinnovamento di qualche dinamica di lavoro e di campo, a livello di stimoli e di motivazioni, lo devono fare tutti, soprattutto i manager. Gli allenatori in Inghilterra sono chiamati manager perché si occupano di un'area anche più vasta, cioè sono più coinvolti anche nelle cose extracampo. Quindi un grande manager deve saper toccare i tasti giusti".

#2285. Atalanta, Ederson: "Ritiro fondamentale per ripartire. Fischi a fine gara? Giusti"

23:10 - José Ederson, giocatore dell’Atalanta, ha commentato così in conferenza stampa il match contro il Parma nel post gara. Tuttomercatoweb vi riporta le parole del giocatore presso la New Balance Arena.

Come si commenta una gara come questa? "Stasera secondo me i nostri tifosi hanno trasmesso tutto quello che è stato oggi. Ci si aspettava una vittoria, però purtroppo abbiamo perso. Difficile spiegare una gara come questa. Nel primo tempo potevamo fare almeno due gol, nella ripresa siamo andati in difficoltà. Dobbiamo lavorare molto di più ed essere più cattivi e solidi".

Nei momenti di difficoltà come ci si rialza? "Nei momenti di difficoltà abbiamo sempre reagito bene. Sembra che vada tutto male, ma in questo momento serve lavorare un po' di più: stare insieme su cosa migliroare come squadra. Avere maggior equilbrio difensivo: oggi un po' insieme serve lavorare. Serve lavorare molto di più".

Che stato d'animo si affronta una situazione di questo tipo? "Nel primo tempo c'è stato entusiasmo, poi abbiamo preso gol alla fine e ci ha fatto sicuramente male. Nell'intervallo eravamo insieme per cercare di ripetere l'aggressività del primo tempo. Purtroppo non ci siamo ripetuti: quando subiamo gol sembra che siamo fragili. Dobbiamo essere più forti e più cattivi. Se abbiamo preso un gol a fine primo tempo bisogna essere equlibrati. Purtroppo non ci sentiamo tranquilli nell'esprimere questa solidità".

Cosa ti ha colpito del discorso nel finale dei tifosi? "Loro ci hanno trascinato dall'inizio alla fine. Erano molto delusi nonostante abbiano spinto la squadra per 95 minuti. Loro volevano capire il perché di questa situazione. Non si può iniziare in un modo e finire in un altro. E' stato giusto il discorso dei tifosi alla fine. Ora faremo molto di più ed è quello che posso dire: chiedo ai nostri tifosi di starci vicino. Loro sono stati positivi con noi e dobbiamo recepirla anche noi questa positività. Uniti ritorneremo a vivere momenti importanti".

#2281. Gordon si è già preso il Barcellona: "E non avete visto ancora il meglio di me"

Tre gol e quattro assist nelle prime 13 presenze sono il biglietto da visita di Anthony Gordon al Barcellona. Arrivato in estate per 70 milioni di sterline, l'esterno inglese ha parlato alla vigilia della sfida di Champions League contro l'Aston Villa, confrontando la pressione blaugrana con quelle vissute nelle precedenti esperienze: "La sfida di unirmi al Barcellona è diversa da quelle che ho affrontato in passato, perché all'Everton ho lottato per la salvezza per due o tre anni, il che è stato difficile. Al Newcastle lottavamo forse per la Champions League e per risalire la classifica, e ora con il Barcellona lotto per ogni trofeo".

Tre realtà completamente differenti che, secondo Gordon, hanno contribuito alla sua crescita: "Mi sono piaciuti molto tutti e tre perché offrono diversi spunti per aiutarti a crescere come persona". Adesso, però, l'obiettivo è vincere: "Credo che competere su tutti i fronti per ogni trofeo sia senza dubbio la cosa più gratificante. La gente pensa che ci sia più pressione, ma in realtà è una pressione migliore rispetto alla lotta per la salvezza".

L'impatto con il Barcellona è stato positivo, ma Gordon è convinto di avere ancora ampi margini: "Ho iniziato piuttosto bene, considerando che è un paese nuovo per me. È un grande cambiamento, una nuova squadra. Ma posso fare molto di più". L'inglese chiede soltanto tempo per completare l'adattamento: "Penso che mi ci vorrà del tempo per crescere davvero, per sentirmi a mio agio e poi, quando succederà, penso che vedrete il meglio di me, che sicuramente non avete ancora visto. Sono qui solo da due mesi e mezzo. Mi sono adattato piuttosto bene, ma con più tempo a disposizione posso fare molto di più e sicuramente lo farò".

#2280. Lazio, la forza dei cambi e un aspetto da correggere: dentro il primato

Otto gol, sei marcatori e due successi diversi: la squadra di Gattuso trova nuove risorse, ma concede ancora nel primo tempo.

La Lazio prima in classifica ha mostrato due modi diversi di vincere nella stessa settimana. A Sassuolo ha segnato sei volte, contro il Cagliari ha dovuto aspettare l’83’ per completare la rimonta. Due partite che, lette insieme, aiutano a capire cosa stia sostenendo il rendimento della squadra di Gennaro Gattuso.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il punto di partenza sono i 28 punti conquistati su 30 disponibili, con nove vittorie e un pareggio. Come certificato dalla Lega Serie A, si tratta della miglior partenza nella storia del club. Il confronto fra le ultime due gare aggiunge però qualcosa alla fotografia del primato: la capacità di trovare protagonisti e soluzioni differenti.

Il 6-2 contro il Sassuolo nasce da una partenza immediatamente produttiva. Taylor segna al 2’, Thorstvedt pareggia al 7’, poi Isaksen e Floriani Mussolini portano i biancocelesti sul 3-1 entro il 18’. La Lazio aveva dunque già costruito un doppio vantaggio prima dell’espulsione del centrocampista neroverde, arrivata al 31’.

La superiorità numerica resta un elemento da considerare nell’analisi del risultato. Non cancella quanto costruito prima, ma impedisce di leggere tutti i novanta minuti come un confronto nelle stesse condizioni. Dopo il momentaneo 2-3 di Esposito, Zaccagni ristabilisce le distanze prima dell’intervallo e Noslin completa il punteggio con una doppietta nella ripresa.

Contro il Cagliari, invece, la Lazio deve recuperare lo svantaggio firmato da Nzola. Isaksen pareggia al 36’, mentre la rete decisiva arriva soltanto nel finale con Pinamonti.

Il conteggio delle due gare restituisce otto gol e sei marcatori differenti: Taylor, Isaksen, Floriani Mussolini, Zaccagni, Noslin e Pinamonti. È un dato significativo sulla distribuzione delle reti. In questa settimana il risultato non è dipeso da un solo finalizzatore: hanno contribuito giocatori di reparti diversi, titolari e subentrati.

La vittoria sul Cagliari offre l’esempio più concreto del peso della panchina. Pinamonti e Pedraza, entrati entrambi al 55’, costruiscono l’azione del sorpasso: lo spagnolo serve il pallone che l’attaccante trasforma di testa all’83’. Con l’ingresso del centravanti, Noslin si sposta sulla fascia. Cambiano gli uomini e anche la disposizione offensiva. News

Come riportato da LazioPress.it nella conferenza del 1° novembre, Gattuso ha riconosciuto l’energia portata dai cambi, spiegando anche che la squadra aveva pagato qualcosa dopo aver schierato quasi sempre gli stessi nelle tre partite ravvicinate. La rimonta suggerisce quindi una risorsa importante: poter modificare una gara complicata attraverso le alternative disponibili.

Resta un aspetto sul quale lavorare. Tutti e tre i gol subiti nelle ultime due partite sono arrivati prima dell’intervallo, mentre entrambe le riprese si sono chiuse senza reti incassate. Due incontri non bastano a definire una tendenza, ma indicano una differenza da approfondire nella gestione delle fasi della gara.

La lettura del primato passa anche da qui: una Lazio capace di segnare con uomini diversi e di trovare risposte dalla panchina, che conserva margini di miglioramento. I risultati premiano il lavoro di Gattuso; il confronto fra Sassuolo e Cagliari mostra quanto contino anche le soluzioni a disposizione quando la partita prende una direzione inattesa.

#2279. De Roon e il dito medio ai tifosi della Roma nel 2023: "Sono sulla buona strada per farmi perdonare"

Il centrocampista della Roma, Marten De Roon, ha preso la parola al fianco di mister Gian Piero Gasperini nella conferenza stampa pre-Manchester United. Tra i vari argomenti trattati, l'ex Atalanta ha commentato anche il suo inserimento progressivo nello spogliatoio giallorosso. Di seguito le sue parole in merito.

Sei sulla buona strada per farti perdonare dai tifosi della Roma? "Sono sulla buona strada, le prestazioni sono sempre quelle che contano. Ma mi ha fatto piacere essere applaudito quando sono uscito col Cagliari. I fatti dimostrano sempre quello che vali".

Come ti stai trovando alla Roma? L’Atalanta ha rinunciato troppo presto a te? "Io sto bene. Da quando sono arrivato mi serviva ritrovare ritmo e condizione fisica, l’abbiamo messa a posto durante la sosta. Lo staff e il gruppo mi hanno accolto benissimo, sapevo che potevo ancora contribuire e son contento di come sta andando".

Marten de Roon ha un conto in sospeso con i tifosi della Roma per un episodio risalente all’aprile 2023. Dopo una vittoria dell’Atalanta contro i giallorossi, il centrocampista pubblicò infatti sui social una foto con il dito medio accompagnata dalla frase: "Quando le tue radici calcistiche sono a Rotterdam e batti la Roma", scatenando comprensibilmente le polemiche tra i sostenitori romanisti.

#2278. Juventus-Napoli 2-0, le pagelle di IamNaples.it: ingenuità di Marianucci, tante insufficienze

Il Napoli esce sconfitto dall’Allianz Stadium contro la Juventus. Decidono le reti di Alajbegovic e Boga nel 2-0 finale. Di seguito, le pagelle di IamNaples.it.

Meret 5,5: Ha poco da rimproverarsi sui due gol subiti. Per il resto, fa ciò che deve. Su Cabal viene aiutato dal palo.

Di Lorenzo 6: Nonostante qualche incertezza, mantiene la dritta la rotta. La sua assenza nel secondo tempo si sente. 46′ Rrahmani 5,5: Un discreto ingresso, poi affonda come tutti.

Marianucci 5: Attento e concentrato per quasi tutta la gara. Sulla fascia da ammonito commette un fallo ingenuo e si fa espellere.

Rafa Marin 5,5: Si arrangia come può quando il Napoli inizia a concedere campo e occasioni. Nel finale si prende un giallo per frustrazione.

Olivera 5,5: Dopo un buon primo tempo, nella ripresa cala vistosamente. Poi esce per infortunio. 79′ Beukema s.v.

Anguissa 5: La sua aggressività permette al Napoli di creare qualche buona opportunità come il tiro di Lang. Nella ripresa cala pure lui. Guarda da vicino Alajbegovic senza intervenire sul gol. 79′ Giovane s.v.

De Bruyne 5,5: Smista diversi palloni, magari non sempre in modo rapido. Però ha anche pochi giocatori da poter servire. Non al top fisicamente. 46′ Gilmour 5: In sofferenza perenne, entra quando inizia la debacle.

McTominay 5: È un fantasma per tutta la gara. Tocca pochi palloni, s’inserisce poco, non si fa sentire molto nemmeno nei contrasti.

Politano 5,5: Mette un bel pallone sulla testa di Lucca e impegna Vicario in uscita. Qualche buon ripiegamento. 61′ Vergara 5,5: Non cambia la musica nell’ultima mezz’ora e dopo l’espulsione di Marianucci la partita finisce.

Lucca 5,5: Vicario gli nega il gol con una buona parata su un suo colpo di testa. Qualche duello vinto coi difensori avversari.

Lang 5: Spreca una buona chance nel primo tempo spendendo il pallone troppo alto. Nella ripresa non si vede mai.

Landucci (Allegri) 5: In queste condizioni gioca un discreto primo tempo, dove vengono costruite anche delle buone opportunità per Lucca e Lang non concretizzate. Nel secondo tempo i cambi portano a delle modifiche tattiche, in linea generale però non viene praticamente mai giocato. Il rosso a Marianucci poi chiude i conti.

#2277. James Penrice's ‘turned a corner’ claim as Badredine Bouanani hails ‘crazy’ support

James Penrice reckons Rangers have “turned a corner” but insists there is still plenty more to come after they booked their place in the Premier Sports Cup final.

The Ibrox side overcame Aberdeen 1-0 at Hampden, with Ryan Naderi grabbing the late winner to send Derek McInnes’ men back to the national stadium in December.

Penrice, who played in a more central midfield role before switching back to left-back, was delighted with the victory and hailed Naderi for delivering when it mattered. He said: “It is excellent. We stuck in there today and got our goal. It is a proper striker's goal for Ryan.

Penrice believes Rangers’ resilience was crucial as they kept pushing for the breakthrough despite the prospect of extra time looming. He added: “We were all pushing. We created a number of chances. You have seen this season the resilience to keep going until the final whistle. It has paid off for us.

“It is a proper striker's goal for Ryan, and he has been excellent. He has been our guy supplying the goals.

"We are buzzing to get there, getting into the final, and that is the main thing.”

James Penrice and Badredine Bouanani speak after victory for @RangersFC at Barclays Hampden 🔵 "We've kind of turned a corner... it's getting better" 🗣️ #PremierSportsCup https://t.co/BBGIXZRbN2

— Premier Sports (@PremSportsTV) October 31, 2026

Rangers have now gone 11 games unbeaten, and Penrice believes their previous meeting with Aberdeen proved to be a turning point. But he warned there remains significant room for improvement despite their impressive run.

He said: “Aberdeen last time was probably the shift. We have turned a corner, but it is still not completely there. We can do a lot more on the pitch and score a lot more goals, but it is getting better.”

Badredine Bouanani was named Man of the Match after an impressive display but admitted he was frustrated not to get on the scoresheet himself. He said: “I had a few chances. I need to work in training. I need to score one or two goals today, but it is okay.

"I am going to work in training next week and hope next game I will score.”

Bouanani also hailed the Rangers support after sampling the Hampden atmosphere. He said: “Crazy fans. At home at Ibrox, it is always special, and today was also crazy. Very happy about the win.

And the winger insists he is relishing life at Rangers. He added: “Since I have been here, I enjoy every game. With the teammates, they are really good. We can give everything for them.

"I enjoy every game, and especially today was crazy.”

#2276. Pinamonti scelse la Lazio: il tentativo del Celta durante lo stallo col Sassuolo

L’attaccante ha poi deciso da subentrato la sfida col Cagliari: per lui due gol e un assist in 198 minuti.

Andrea Pinamonti voleva la Lazio anche quando, durante l’estate, il Celta Vigo ha cercato di inserirsi nella trattativa con il Sassuolo. Secondo quanto riportato da TUTTOmercatoWEB, L’attaccante ha mantenuto la propria scelta nei giorni in cui l’accordo con i neroverdi faticava ad arrivare. Ora il suo gol da subentrato contro il Cagliari, all’Olimpico, accompagna il primato in classifica dei biancocelesti.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il Sassuolo continuava a chiedere un trasferimento a titolo definitivo. La Lazio, con poca liquidità a disposizione, incontrava difficoltà nel trovare un’intesa per portare Pinamonti nella Capitale. La trattativa ha attraversato così una fase di stallo, senza procedere nei tempi auspicati.

In quel periodo il Celta Vigo ha provato a inserirsi con decisione. Il club spagnolo si è detto disposto a soddisfare le richieste economiche sia del Sassuolo sia del calciatore. L’operazione, però, era legata alla partenza di Borja Iglesias: gli spagnoli avrebbero dovuto trovargli una sistemazione per fare spazio in rosa all’italiano.
