Manchester United’s preparations for the new season continue in Norway as they take on Rosenborg in their second pre-season game. These sides did meet in a pre-season friendly two years ago in July 2024, with Rosenborg winning that encounter 1-0.

Manchester United kicked off their pre-season against Wrexham nearly a week ago, which they lost 1-0 in Helsinki. Michael Carrick opted to deploy two different XIs for each half, meaning 22 players got a run-out. Manchester United kick off their Premier League campaign at newly promoted Hull City on August 22.

They have added two midfielders to their ranks over the last few weeks, both from the Premier League. Brazilian Andrey Santos has joined from Chelsea whilst Belgium’s Youri Tielemans has arrived from Aston Villa. Santos made his first Manchester United appearance in the loss to Wrexham whilst Tielemans is yet to feature having made the knockout stages with Belgium at the World Cup. A number of players are still yet to return from World Cup duty, including the likes of Lisandro Martinez, Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo, although Rashford still faces an uncertain future.

Former Leeds goalkeeper Karl Darlow has also arrived but he is currently recovering from a minor procedure. Benjamin Sesko is still trying to shake off a shin injury whilst Matthijs de Ligt is not yet available due to a back injury which plagued for most of last season. Manuel Ugarte faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines having picked up a serious injury whilst playing for Uruguay at the World Cup. After this game, the level of competition for Manchester United for the rest of pre-season ramps up a number of notches, with the likes of Atlético Madrid and back-to-back European champions PSG to come over the next couple of weeks as Carrick’s men prepare for a season in which they return to the Champions League.

Rosenborg are in the midst of their league campaign in Norway and are experiencing a tricky campaign. They are currently 10th in the Norwegian top flight, having won just four of their 13 league games thus far, but their form has picked up of late as they have won three of their last five games. They won their last match 3-0 against Start six days ago.

#2261. Haissem Hassan on Celtic goal drought, Maloney guidance & one area for improvement

In football, end product is the defining trait of any winger. From Jimmy Johnstone to Jota, Celtic have a storied history of successful wide men, with Haissem Hassan the latest man eager to make his mark.

Hassan joined the club for an initial fee of £6 million from Real Oviedo this summer following an impressive World Cup campaign with Egypt that ended in a Round of 16 defeat to eventual finalists Argentina.

So far in Glasgow, though, Hassan has struggled to perform consistently, unable to fully replicate the international displays that brought his name to the attention of several European clubs.

If anything, the 24-year-old has shown his talent in bursts. He breezed past Celta Vigo's Marcos Alonso last Thursday, carrying Celtic 80 yards up the pitch and winning a corner.

An apex showing in the 7-1 shellacking of Hearts stands out too, but Hassan has yet to find the net for Celtic.

Indeed, two assists in 15 appearances across all competitions suggests a winger still searching for that crucial end product.

"Defensive-wise I need to improve. On the attacking side I need the numbers on goals and assists," Hassan said. "I should not be losing my head about it. I just need to focus on training.

"When I get the minutes, I need to try to produce and contribute to the team's performance. I will focus on doing this.

"In terms of defending, the team in Spain asked me a lot as well. The teams you play against are also good teams and they asked me to defend more."

Haissem Hassan in action for Celtic. (Image: Stuart Wallace / Shutterstock)

Hassan's lack of goals isn't for a want of trying. He forced Dundee United goalkeeper Jack Walton into a fine save after coming off the bench during Wednesday evening's 2-2 draw and unleashing a rasping effort from range.

He also rattled the left post after cutting inside and leaving three Hearts players for dead a fortnight ago.

"I am really keen to score my first goal for Celtic and also add assists," Hassan continued. "The goal feels closer and closer.

"The other day I was close. The game before that I assisted goals so hopefully it will come soon."

Seven of Hassan's 15 Celtic appearances have come from the start.

Manager Martin O'Neill isn't short of wide options, with Jota, capable on both flanks, recently returning from an 18-month anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Camilo Duran, the club's current top scorer, can play on the right while Hyun-jun Yang and James Forrest remain viable picks.

Callum Osmand has also started featuring on the left-hand side. Hassan relishes the competition for places.

"The wingers in this team are at a really good level," he said. "When I go on the pitch, I have to give my best.

"But the competition is good for us all. If one player comes out and does really well, the rest of us know we have to do even more. It's been really good so far."

Assistant manager Shaun Maloney guides Celtic's wingers, having featured out wide during his own playing career.

"Shaun helps me a lot," Hassan explained. "He is close to the players and always tries to help the players. He had a good career as a winger.

"Whenever he comes to me and speaks to me, I always try to listen and take it into account. Having him as a reference point really helps me."

Hassan qualifies to play for Egypt through his parents, though he grew up on the outskirts of Paris and speaks fluent French and Spanish. The transition to life in Glasgow, he says, has been relatively straightforward, even if a slight language barrier exists.

"I am happy here. It's a nice city," he adds. "I live here with my family and they are happy here, too. It is cold but it is good! It's a big city that has it all so I'm happy here.

"It happens in Glasgow that I meet fans. It's good to feel the love of the fans. I try to stop as much as possible and take a photo with them.

"I like the culture. But I have been living in France and Spain where people have dinner quite late. Here it's very early so it's the only thing I need to get used to!"

Despite the cold weather, for Hassan, joining Celtic was a simple call: "I made the decision myself to come over here. It's a big club and I thought it would help me be a better player and improve my career.

"I didn't have to speak to anyone else for those reasons."

Although still transitioning to life at Celtic, Hassan played for Egypt during the recent international break, starting two crucial AFCON qualifiers against Angola and South Sudan.

A double-header against Malawi lies ahead later this month.

"It feels good to play for the national team," Hassan stated. "You represent your country and it's a great honour.

"There is a bunch of great players in the national team and I enjoy playing with them.

"The games against Malawi are really important. If we can win, it would take us top of the table and give us the opportunity to play at the next AFCON."

For now, though, Hassan's focus remains on getting off the mark at Celtic.

O'Neill's side travel to face Falkirk on Sunday afternoon before welcoming Besiktas to Glasgow in the Europa League on Thursday evening.

Pointless from their first three fixtures, Celtic realistically need a win against the Turks.

"We still have five games to go," Hassan asserted. "A win over Besiktas would give us confidence and hope.

"If we win the rest of the games or get as many points as possible, we definitely hope we can qualify for the next stage.

"This game is at home. We have the fans with us and hopefully we can get a good result and move forward.

"I don't think the Europa League has been a disappointment as such. We have a good team, good management but the results have cost us.

"We are struggling a bit now. But we can improve and we'll try to play in the best way possible."

#2258. Spalletti in conferenza stampa: “Successo meritato, complimenti ai ragazzi”

Luciano Spalletti, allenatore della Juventus, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni in conferenza stampa dopo la vittoria contro il Napoli: “I calciatori hanno messo mano a questa voglia di riguadagnarsi la fiducia dei nostri tifosi, hanno fatto duelli e corse per i compagni e per la squadra, senza avere il dubbio di buttare via una corsa e hanno vinto una partita in maniera meritata. Gli si fanno i complimenti, se questo primo passo non lo fanno da soli quando si cade in basso, diventa difficile dire e fare qualsiasi cosa. Solo loro possono fare certe cose, se non fai duelli e vinci i contrasti e hai il coraggio di avere campo libero alle spalle per dargli addosso e guadagnare metri, di rimanere alti con tre attaccanti come nel secondo tempo. Tu stai lì, li aiuti affinchè arrivi uno che fa il primo passo che è contagioso per tutti gli altri, si torna ad avere una mezza identità e si vince una partita fondamentale con enormi difficoltà. Fino ad ora perdevo, io però ora posso dire che siamo in tredici, non ho i cambi. Altrimenti dico come tutti, datemi le armi per essere a livello. Oggi non possiamo essere paragonati a nessuno, oggi tutti a urlare su Cambiaso ma chi potevo far entrare? Non ce ne sono altri, mi piaceva far giocare altri ma a qualcuno puoi dedicare la partita del giovedì. Vediamo come sta Cabal e come sta McKennie, poi se alle scuderie fa comodo dire che la Juventus deve vincere lo scudetto e fa comodo portare avanti certe idee. Se gli si leva pressione giocano con più tranquillità, oggi non si può competere per niente e se non recuperiamo qualcuno si rimane in questa situazione. Per noi era una partita enormemente difficile, il Napoli aveva gli stessi punti nostri e mi sembra di esser arrivato diversamente al match: loro hanno vinto a Monza e noi abbiamo perso. Abbiamo fatto leva sulle debolezze del Napoli e viceversa? Il Napoli ha preso in mano la gara e ci ha creato difficoltà nell’agganciarli, non riuscivamo a trovare quello che era il nostro avversario nelle scalate e negli scivolamenti di squadra. Ci sono venuti addosso uomo contro uomo, noi tentando di aiutare e mettere in condizione l’attaccante non ci riuscivamo nel primo tempo. Vicario ha fatto una gran parata su Lucca, poi abbiamo fatto qualche duello a viso aperto e siamo migliorati, è stata una partita sottolivello per entrambe al 45′. Poi siamo rimasti su con i tre attaccanti nella ripresa, Di Lorenzo non c’era più e nel ruolo è il migliore a spingere. Qualche volta ci abbiamo provato in maniera sconquassata, il nostro stadio col suo supporto è la vera faccia di chi partecipa al fianco della squadra. C’è voluto un gran gol di Alajbegovic, lui ha questo tiro da fuori, e poi Boga come gli altri nella ripresa sono entrati bene, con la fiducia di chi aveva già messo mano alla situazione. Il Napoli? Lo sa meglio Allegri, l’ho abbracciato a fine partita: ci siamo incontrati e salutati, è un piacere come sempre perchè non è vero che con lui non parlo perchè ci siamo antipatici. Ci siamo fatti i viaggi in treno assieme, Landucci è stato due giorni interi a casa mia in campagna, poi voi volete scrivere che Landucci mi ha detto delle brutte cose, dipende dalla scuderia alla quale appartenete. Cabal ha giocato una partita straordinaria, anche in un ruolo non suo andando ad attaccare, secondo me è stato uno dei migliori. Il modulo? Quando giochi contro difese così, anche se giochi a cinque contro tre attaccanti la difesa la devi rompere e noi abbiamo deciso di farlo con McKennie e Kalulu su Olivera e Lang. Se loro hanno un solo attaccante non puoi rimanere a cinque, devi cambiare la sua organizzazione e fisionomia di sistema di gioco. Però la mia era una idea voluta, nel secondo tempo sarebbe stato più basso McKennie perchè Alajbegovic volevo tenerlo più alto senza Di Lorenzo”.

#2255. L’Udinese cambia: Runjaic esonerato, arriva Zanetti. I dettagli e come può giocare

L’Udinese cambia allenatore dopo il pesante avvio di stagione. Il club friulano ha esonerato Kosta Runjaic e affidato la prima squadra a Paolo Zanetti, che ha firmato un contratto fino al 30 giugno 2027. La decisione arriva al termine di un periodo molto negativo per i bianconeri, reduci da sette sconfitte nelle ultime otto partite di campionato, con un solo pareggio nel mezzo. Si chiude così dopo oltre due anni l’esperienza di Runjaic all’Udinese: il tecnico tedesco aveva chiuso al dodicesimo posto la sua prima stagione in Serie A e al decimo quella successiva, valorizzando diversi giocatori poi diventati centrali anche sul mercato, da Atta a Bijol, passando per Lucca e Kristensen. Il rendimento della stagione 2026/27 ha però portato la società a cambiare strada.

Per Zanetti si tratta della quarta esperienza in Serie A dopo Venezia, Empoli e Verona. Il tecnico vicentino aveva riportato i lagunari nella massima categoria dopo 19 anni, prima dell’esonero nel finale della stagione 2021/22. In Toscana ha centrato una salvezza con tre giornate d’anticipo nel 2022/23, mentre la stagione seguente è terminata dopo un avvio disastroso. L’ultima esperienza è stata quella all'Hellas: salvezza nel primo anno, poi l’esonero nel febbraio 2026 con la squadra all’ultimo posto.

Dal punto di vista tattico, almeno inizialmente, non è scontata una rivoluzione. Zanetti in passato ha utilizzato il 4-3-1-2 e il 4-3-3, ma nelle ultime esperienze ha lavorato soprattutto con la difesa a tre, alternando 3-5-2 e 3-4-2-1: proprio quest’ultimo è stato il sistema scelto da Runjaic nelle ultime giornate. Davanti a Okoye può quindi restare una linea a tre, mentre Vojvoda, Zanoli, Kamara e Arizala sono profili adatti a lavorare sulle corsie. A centrocampo Karlstrom può agire davanti alla difesa, con diverse alternative per gli altri posti. Particolare attenzione andrà riservata a Nicolò Zaniolo, che può partire da destra sulla trequarti e avvicinarsi alla porta. Davanti, invece, Keinan Davis resta il riferimento: può giocare con una seconda punta nel 3-5-2 oppure da centravanti unico con due giocatori alle spalle, soluzione molto simile a quella già utilizzata dall’Udinese nelle ultime settimane.

#2253. Martin O'Neill admits it's 'remarkable' Celtic still top after Falkirk loss

Martin O'Neill acknowledges that it is "remarkable" that Celtic remain top of the Scottish Premiership after dropping more points against Falkirk.

The Hoops were well beaten by the Bairns, 2-0, as they lost their second game of the season.

Their defeat followed a 2-2 draw with Dundee United last midweek and added to a gloomy recent spate of poor performances and results in all competitions which sits at just three wins from 10 matches in all competitions.

For O'Neill he insists he saw enough from his side this afternoon to suggest they should have beaten their opponents.

🗣️ “Remarkably, we’re still top of the league.” 🗣️ “We came from a mile behind last season to win the league.” 🗣️ “I keep out the noise.” Martin O’Neill says Celtic will “get a reaction” after their 2-0 loss to Falkirk ⤵️ https://t.co/DN1V5FRHbE

— Sky Sports Scotland (@ScotlandSky) November 1, 2026

But he admits they missed too many chances, as has happened too often this campaign already with Celts missing the chance to go seven clear at the summit.

"Is there any worry? Remarkably we're still top of the league," O'Neill said when asked the question by Sky Sports' Luke Shanley.

"We came from a mile behind last year to win the league. On two or three occasions as well. We're still in a decent position at this minute and we've played a lot of football as well."

Pushed by the reporter as to whether he feels Celtic could still be better, O'Neill added: "Of course we could. I'm not sure about your point here, I've just tried to explain to you, we missed goal after goal today.

"Their goalkeeper was magnificent, man of the match, so if we take even half our chances we would've won today."

#2251. Le ambizioni della Roma passano (anche) dal Teatro dei Sogni: la vigilia pre-United

La Roma si prepara alla trasferta di Old Trafford contro il Manchester United, in programma domani alle 21.00 per la quarta giornata della League Phase di Champions League. Alla vigilia, Gian Piero Gasperini ha presentato la sfida in conferenza stampa, definendo i Red Devils una squadra di grande valore nonostante le difficoltà recenti: "Ci prepariamo come se affrontassimo il miglior Manchester". Il tecnico giallorosso ha parlato anche delle assenze di Pellegrini, Dybala e Koné, sottolineando la necessità di adattarsi alle difficoltà e di continuare a migliorare: "La perfezione non esiste, ma cerchiamo sempre di migliorarci".

Al fianco dell'allenatore è intervenuto anche Marten de Roon, che ha speso parole importanti per Gasperini, definendolo un tecnico unico e sottolineando l'intensità del suo calcio. Il centrocampista ex Atalanta si è detto soddisfatto del proprio ambientamento nella Capitale: "Lo staff e il gruppo mi hanno accolto benissimo, sapevo che potevo ancora contribuire". De Roon ha evidenziato anche la crescita della Roma, pur riconoscendo alcuni aspetti da migliorare, soprattutto nella fase difensiva. Sulla sfida contro lo United, ha ribadito il rispetto per un avversario di grande tradizione, ma anche la volontà di ottenere un risultato importante da parte dei suoi.

All'Old Trafford si affrontano due squadre con stati di forma differenti: il Manchester United di Michael Carrick, alla ricerca di una vittoria per rilanciare la propria stagione, e una Roma reduce da quattro successi e un pareggio nelle ultime cinque partite. I padroni di casa dovrebbero schierarsi con il 4-2-3-1, affidandosi a Bruno Fernandes alle spalle di Mbeumo. Gasperini dovrebbe invece confermare il 3-4-2-1: Gollini in porta, Mancini, Ndicka ed Hermoso in difesa, con Molina, Cristante, De Roon e Wesley a centrocampo. Soulé e Mora agiranno alle spalle dell'inamovibile Malen. Arbitra l'incontro lo spagnolo Jesus Gil Manzano.

#2250. Wouter Vrancken reveals Hearts star in hospital after Hibs defeat

Wouter Vrancken has revealed Tomas Magnusson was taken to hospital after being forced off for Heart of Midlothian in their Premier Sports Cup semi-final defeat to Hibernian.

The manager was left deflated at full-time as his side fell 2-1 to their rivals with a return to Hampden Park next month within touching distance.

The Jambos had led the action within the first four minutes when Claudio Braga found the net but their opponents turned the game on its head before half-time thanks to goals from Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath.

Vrancken was concerned with more crocked stars with both Magnusson and Calvin Miller having to go off injured.

And the Belgian head coach has now explained the extent of those issues. "I didn't see Tomas because Tomas is to the hospital," said Vrancken. "Calvin was in a brace but it's always difficult to say directly after the game. So we have to wait for a scan tomorrow or the day after.

"The doctor and medical staff, they did their concussion test on the pitch, at that moment. (Magnusson) passed the concussion test and then he came to me to come in.

"Then he was going left and right, he couldn't stand on his legs anymore. When I saw it, there's no doubt in your head that you're going to let him on the pitch at that moment, because you cannot take the risk.

"Then he saw it himself also at the moment. He said, 'no, I can't do it. And then we had to change him, and now he's to the hospital, so I don't know."

#2249. ‘I do like that shout’: West Ham urged to consider former Tottenham Hotspur boss by talkSPORT man

West Ham are aiming for an immediate promotion back from the Championship this season under the guidance of current head coach Nuno Espirito Santo. WHUFC are positioned in 8th place in the table and are in the play-offs along with Wolves, West Brom, Southampton, Birmingham City and Stoke City after their first 13 fixtures.

The Hammers were relegated from the Premier League last season after they finished in the bottom three along with Burnley and Wolves. Nuno kept his job at the London Stadium in the summer but he is starting to feel the pressure now.

Cundy, who played for Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur and Ipswich Town, has delivered his verdict on the situation at the London Stadium on talkSPORT: “I understand the frustration from West Ham fans. I completely get it because they’re West Ham, they should be in the Premier League but they’re not and they’re getting schooled at home. They need to sit tight. However, I do like Thomas Frank. I do like that shout. It feels like it fits doesn’t it.”

West Ham lost 3-1 at home to West Brom last time out. They are back in action on Wednesday night with an away trip to Cardiff City as they look to bounce back.

Frank is available for West Ham if they decide to sack Nuno. However, it may be hard for WHUFC to persuade him to drop into the second tier.

The Dane guided Brentford to the top flight in 2021 and subsequently kept them there. He was then handed the Tottenham Hotspur job in June 2025.

However, the ex-Brondby man struggled to make an impact at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. He won 34% of his 38 matches in charge of the North London outfit and lasted only eight months at the helm in the end.

Frank was given the chop by Spurs in February and has since been out of the game. He will be weighing up his options as he carefully considers where to go next.

Frank would be ideal for West Ham if they managed to get him. He knows the league well and understand what it takes to get out of it.

He is an experienced operator who has overseen over 550 games from the dugout so far in his career. He worked wonders at Brentford and could do similar with WHUFC.

Nuno remains in the job for now though and needs to get some results quick. The Hammers will want to return to winning ways against Cardiff City.

If not, the heat will be further intensified on their head coach. As well Frank, there are others out of work right now like Scott Parker, Sean Dyche and Vitor Peireira.

#2248. Thuram striglia l’Inter, Chivu ritrova Pio dal 1'. A Rotterdam per dimenticare il derby

L’Inter prova a lasciarsi alle spalle il 3-1 incassato nel derby con il Milan ripartendo dalla Champions League. Questa sera, martedì 3 novembre, i nerazzurri saranno di scena a Rotterdam con il Feyenoord, in una gara che pesa anche sulla corsa alle prime otto dopo il ritardo nelle prime uscite. Marcus Thuram, alla vigilia, non ha nascosto uno dei problemi emersi nelle ultime settimane: l’approccio alle partite. "L’importante è non fare finta che non ci sia questo problema: l’abbiamo capito tutti, spero che possiamo fare meglio", ha spiegato l’attaccante francese, condividendo le parole già pronunciate da Barella e Bastoni. Il riferimento è soprattutto ai primi minuti delle gare: "In questa fase abbiamo faticato e non deve capitare nuovamente".

Il tecnico romeno riparte dalle certezze e prepara anche qualche scelta precisa in attacco. Lautaro Martinez non sarà ovviamente a disposizione e Pio Esposito, dopo essersi ripreso, sembra destinato a giocare accanto a Thuram. Più complicata la situazione di Ange-Yoan Bonny, recuperato in extremis per il derby dopo giorni condizionati da febbre alta, vomito e debolezza. "Pio si è ripreso, credo che le scelte in attacco sono chiare", ha anticipato Chivu. Thuram, dal canto suo, ha assicurato di stare bene nonostante sia stato utilizzato con grande continuità dopo la sosta: "È il sogno di tutti giocare sempre, sono molto felice". E, se necessario, si è detto disponibile anche a giocare da unica punta.

La partita contro il Feyenoord arriva quindi subito dopo la delusione del derby, ma Chivu non vuole trasformarla in un processo alla squadra. "La sconfitta si accetta, si analizza. Bisogna ripartire dagli errori, ma anche dalle certezze" ha spiegato il tecnico, ricordando come l’Inter sia ancora pienamente in corsa per il proprio obiettivo europeo. Dopo le prime due sconfitte è arrivato il successo con lo Shakhtar, ottenuto anche giocando in inferiorità numerica: proprio quell’atteggiamento, secondo Thuram, deve diventare lo standard. "Quello che abbiamo avuto in dieci dobbiamo averlo sempre, in qualsiasi competizione". A Rotterdam servirà anche gestire l’impatto iniziale del Feyenoord, particolarmente aggressivo in casa. Giovanni Van Bronckhorst, tecnico degli olandesi, ha definito l’Inter una squadra "completa" e abituata a queste partite, pur sottolineandone alcune vulnerabilità. Per i nerazzurri, la prima risposta dovrà arrivare proprio dall’approccio.

#2247. Morton may be struggling but charity is bringing hope to the community

Christmas is an important time of the year for Morton in the Community. Since 2019 the social impact arm of the struggling Championship club has taken part in Festive Friends, the programme run by the SPFL Trust to provide turkey and trimmings for those who need them most.

For the first time families from the east end of Greenock will also be invited to Cappielow for a separate dinner this year while a Boots and Pieces pop up shop in the town centre provides sports kit and equipment for  a community ranked the most deprived in the country.

“Think of the pressure families come under at Christmas,” says charity Chief Executive Brian McLaughlin. “They come under pressure to put stuff on their credit cards and it’s such a difficult time for everyone. Even for businesses and football clubs….”

For the local football club in Greenock this Christmas threatens to be more difficult than usual. Morton face a financial short-fall of £320,000 after main sponsors Dalrada failed to make promised payments on time.

A recent financial update from Financial Director Kenneth Weldin refused to rule out administration by ‘early to mid December’ unless a solution arrives soon. A fans’ Fighting Fund has raised over £70,000 and might buy a little more time.

The best hope now lies with a consortium of local businessmen led by businessman Raj Samrai and featuring local billionaire Sandy Easdale.

A £150,000-a-year investment package is on offer in return for 60 per cent of the club and ownership of Cappielow.

While there appears to be no great enthusiasm for an offer amongst members of Morton Club Together - the fan ownership group - 427 of the 1200 members voted in favour of a period of due diligence in order to give both parties a chance to work through the structure and terms of a deal. Alternative options are thin on the ground.

Working from an office in Cappielow, the charitable arm of the football club can do nothing but continue to offer help and support for a community which now has one more financial hardship to fret over. Shipyards and heavy industry left Greenock decades ago and the loss of the football club which has played out of Cappielow since 1879 would feel like another savage blow.

“This club has been a big part of my life for 20 years,” says McLaughlin. “My grandad used to be a steward at Cappielow and my dad and his twin brother used to jump the turnstiles.

“Saturday at 5pm is either the best or the worst part of a supporter’s week. And these are difficult times.

“But we can’t control what happens on that side of things.

“What we can control is the work that we do to support the wider community during difficult times.”

A former player with Greenock Juniors, McLaughlin always had a plan to forge a career out of football in some capacity.

After completing a degree in Sport Development he worked as a community coach for Street League before joining his local club as a Development Officer in 2014. In 2018 he was appointed Chief Executive of Morton in The Community, an award winning operation running over 20 initiatives to engage locals aged from 18 months to 80.

Billed as ‘The Heartbeat of Inverclyde’ the ticker of the local club has faltered more than once over the years.

There was a previous brush with administration until the Rae family - local confectioners - stepped in to prop things up and absorb years of losses. A move to community ownership in 2021 saw Morton Club Together assume majority control of a debt free club.

Where other fan owned operations appointed a figurehead, a captain of industry, to run the show Morton rely on volunteers with little or no experience of running a football club. And placing all their eggs in one financial basket proved a calamitous mistake when the Dalrada money dried up.

An investment package by Dutch ownership group Estrella has since been turned down and MCT members now debate why the local consortium should gain a 60% stake in the club and control of Cappielow simply for handing over the same amount of money every month as they do.

Resigned to the fact that fan ownership at Morton in its current form has failed many now fear that rejection of the consortium’s offer would render Greenock Morton the ghost of Christmas past.

“I am optimistic about everything,” says McLaughlin. “What I say to our staff and volunteers is that we need to focus on controlling the controllables.

“We are here to support the club any way we can. Because the club is a key part of the community and we really hope that the future is positive.

“If we do our bit we will be okay and we will continue to support people and I think we will be alright.

“And, touch wood, I think the football club will be okay as well.

“If they can continue to provide the football we will continue to build and provide the projects that Inverclyde needs.”

The needs of Greenock and its surrounding areas are deep-rooted. In the Scottish Index of Multiple Deprivation of 2020 Inverclyde was found to be the most deprived data zone in Scotland, with extreme scores for income, employment, health (including drug related hospital admissions), education and crime.

Around half of the region’s population live in the three of the most deprived localities. Workless households are amongst the highest in the UK while premature mortality is in the top 10 across local authorities.

“Inverclyde is top of the league table in so many areas for the wrong reasons,” says McLaughlin.

“At one point we were the covid capital of Scotland.

“We are top in terms of health and poverty rates and child poverty is through the roof.

“As a father that really affects me because I look at my two year old son and wonder what kind of life I want to give him. And what can I do to help other people have a better life?”

While the national game is regarded as a curse on society by some politicians at Holyrood, Morton in the Community are just one of the club charity arms reaching into local areas to improve lives through the power of football. Their work is neither sexy or appreciated and goes largely unseen.

This week marked the 50th anniversary of Morton’s greatest ever player, Andy Ritchie, moving to Greenock from Celtic.

Signing in time for a Wednesday night game against Davie Cooper’s Clydebank in October 1976 his first impressions of Cappielow were unfavourable. An old fire in the home dressing room stunk of gas and he gained the impression that Vikings had just looted the main stand stand and moved to for the escape boats 20 minutes before his arrival.

Viewed as a slightly archaic, shambolic, old school 20th century football stadium, Cappielow hasn’t changed a great deal in the five decades since. And yet, where the old shutters only opened for games and training sessions in days gone by, Morton in the Community have spent the last seven years since 2019 quietly turning the old place into a multi-purpose hub for those who need someone to talk to.

“That time from three to five on a Saturday is so important to a lot of people. But it can’t be the only time a stadium is open,” McLaughlin observes.

“What I really love about this job is that it’s not just dealing with the people who live for the three to five on a Saturday.

“People come in here and say, ‘I’m not a football fan, I have never been in here.’

“And that doesn’t bother me one bit because what happens on the pitch will happen. We can’t control that.

“What we can control is the impact we have on peoples’ lives.

“We can offer them a bit of hope. We can give them a wee bit of direction. Or a bit of support.

“That’s probably the biggest source of satisfaction for me. When I look back and say, ‘you know what? We helped someone today.”

Grassroots football offers weekly sessions. Worried that football is becoming a middle class game, McLaughlin grew up kicking a ball around the streets of Braeside but sees the cost of participation rising to a level parents can no longer meet.

“Football is becoming very expensive now. When I grew up I was fortunate because we played football in the street with a plastic ball using lampposts or bottles for goalposts and a driveway as a pitch.”

For a number of reasons that doesn’t happen now. Inverclyde has some of the highest stats in Scotland for childhood obesity in the under-fives and McLaughlin wants to introduce the kids of the area to movement, physical activity, sport, football, gymnastics via the charity’s nursery programme. To play football any way they can.

“We have delivered free provision for football holiday camps. We have also trialled ‘pay what you can’ for parents to walk in and put a tenner in a bucket, a pound in a bucket or nothing at all.

“And what you find is that the numbers are double or triple what we would normally get.

“We did a background survey asking people if they could afford to pay the normal £12 a day and the overwhelming answer was ‘no. The cost of playing football is a real issue now.”

Football now accounts for just 60 per cent of the charity’s activities they roll out. On a Monday night Team Talk opens the stadium up for those who feel the need to have a cup of a tea, a biscuit and just talk. On a Friday morning they co-host a session with Moving On Inverclyde, a local drug and alcohol recovery charity.

“Last week we had 16 men in a room. Some were 18 some were 50 plus, some had high flying careers, some less so.”

He takes pride in the story of one man who refused to leave his own home for years. He is now one of the charity’s volunteer facilitators, delivering programmes for Scottish Action for Mental Health after completing a degree.

“And all that started with coming to a freezing cold Cappielow on a Monday night for a cup of tea...”

For Inverclyde finding the money to keep the lights on at Cappielow is not just a case saving one of Scotland’s oldest football clubs. For some of the area’s most vulnerable people it’s a lifeline.

#2245. Guimaraes will not force Newcastle exit like Isak, says Howe

Eddie Howe is confident Bruno Guimarães will not demand to leave Newcastle United for Arsenal and echo Alexander Isak’s acrimonious departure to Liverpool last summer.

Howe admitted he could not guarantee that Guimarães will still be at the club in September but gave a strong defence of his captain’s character and insisted the Brazil international will return for pre-season training next week as planned.

Given the huge gap between Newcastle’s valuation of Guimarães and what Arsenal have indicated they would be willing to pay for the 28-year-old, there is a belief on Tyneside that the only way the captain would join the London club is if he behaved as badly as Isak did 12 months ago.

Newcastle value Guimarães at £100m, while Arsenal, through intermediaries, have only indicated they would be willing to pay about £60m including bonuses.

Isak did not travel on the club’s pre-season tour to Asia and then went on strike, refusing to train or play, until Newcastle agreed to sell him to Liverpool for a British record £128m on deadline day.

Asked if he feared a repeat of that with Guimarães this time around, Howe replied: “I’ve spoken to him as I would do with Bruno normally. He is a fantastic person and we have had some really good conversations both before, during and after the World Cup. What we speak about obviously has to remain private but he is a great player and a great person.

“Look, I don’t know what is going to happen with Bruno. That is up to other people to speculate about but also other people to have conversations about which I’m not a part of. I don’t think it is fair to compare situations and what happened previously. You’ve got to look at this in its own right.

“Bruno is captain of our football club. He has been an unbelievable player and person all the time we have worked together. I speak on behalf of everyone at the football club when I say we absolutely love him and of course everyone wants him to stay.

“The plan is for him to come back on July 31, he gets an extended break because of the World Cup and is currently enjoying a holiday with his family... There is nothing to say that Bruno won’t be back training with us.”

"We've had some really good conversations" 🗣️Eddie Howe speaks on Newcastle's transfer window so far and speculation around Bruno Guimarães ⚫️⚪️ pic.twitter.com/zB1W31Fne0

Arsenal’s interest in Guimarães is well known but there has been little progress since they began their pursuit more than a month ago.

Whether Arsenal can come up with an offer that tempts Newcastle into negotiations remains to be seen but it is thought the Premier League champions will try to harden up their interest before Guimarães returns for pre-season training.

Newcastle United were held to a 1-1 draw by Gateshead in their second pre-season friendly of the summer. A 79th-minute own-goal saved the Premier League club’s blushes but what did we learn from the match?

Steur did not grab many headlines when he arrived from Ajax for £20m earlier this month because of Sandro Tonali’s move to Tottenham Hotspur. But those familiar with Dutch football would have been excited that Newcastle had signed him.

The 18-year-old has impressed with his performances in training and gave a glimpse of his significant potential in his first public display. He is young and sources have told Telegraph Sport that he must develop physically before he is ready to play every week in the Premier League – but you can already see he has a very high ceiling.

As you would expect from a player described as Ajax’s best midfield prospect for a generation, he is assured on the ball. He is also a progressive passer, always looking to break the lines to get his team moving forward. Eddie Howe will love him.

Whisper it, but there were shades of Bruno Guimarães in his style of play, in the way he took the ball under pressure, in tight spaces, and played on the turn. Patience will be needed but the signs are really encouraging.

Guimarães’s future is all supporters have wanted to speak about for weeks. I was at a wedding on Friday and it felt like everyone asked me about it at some point – including the bride and groom immediately after completing their first dance.

It has already become a summer-long transfer saga that has not progressed since Arsenal’s interest was revealed last month. Telegraph Sport has repeatedly checked whether there have been any fresh developments over the past week and the answer from senior Newcastle sources has remained consistent: there are no talks ongoing and nothing has accelerated, despite claims Arsenal were preparing an official £70m bid.

However, Newcastle need clarity from their captain. He is due back for pre-season next week and is expected to fly to Spain for their training camp on July 31. He has intimated he would like to move to Arsenal but unless Newcastle receive a bid that matches their asking price, he and his representatives have been told he will not be allowed to leave.

Schär has been a brilliant player for Newcastle, but at the age of 34 and coming off the back of a serious ankle injury, he looked understandably rusty against Gateshead.

This will be the former Switzerland international’s ninth season at St James’ Park and he was at fault for giving away a soft free-kick that led to Gateshead scoring first.

Schar accepted a contract extension earlier this summer on reduced terms and although Howe values his quality and experience, he is going to be a back-up centre-back this season.

Neave, 19, started the game as Newcastle’s centre-forward as Will Osula was missing and Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa were given additional time off after playing in the World Cup for Germany and DR Congo respectively.

But those players will return to training next week and, although Neave forced a good save in the first half, he is not ready to start in the Premier League. There is little point keeping him around as a fourth-choice striker when he needs to be playing regularly at this stage of his career.

A loan move is on the cards and he could be a really smart signing for a Championship club or a team competing at the top of League One. The most important thing is that he gets regular senior games rather than hangs around at Newcastle on the fringes of the first-team squad.

Eddie Howe has said "he does not know" what will happen with Bruno but pretty strong defence of his character and denied similarities with Isak. Said they have spoken regularly throughout the summer and he will be back for pre season training on July 31st #nufc

Eddie Howe’s side will head down to Ashton Gate before jetting off to La Manga for a training camp on July 31, which will feature many of those who played in the World Cup, including Bruno Guimarães who has been linked with a move to Arsenal.

In Spain, Newcastle will face Valencia at the Mestalla, before returning to the UK to play Everton at Murrayfield. They will then host Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg at St James’ Park for their final tune-up matches before the Premier League season starts.

The referee brings this contest to a close and it finishes a goal apiece at Gateshead International Stadium. Not the result Howe was hoping for, but he can at least find some comfort in a positive showing from new signing Steur in the heart of midfield.

Newcastle ended up with 76 per cent of the ball and created three ‘big chances’ but lacked the cutting edge in the final third to make that dominance tell. Credit must go to Gateshead who defended resolutely and took their best chance of the match.

Important pre-season minutes 👊 pic.twitter.com/FpzYVdbc0C

Bone picks Pivas’ pocket on the edge of the box but the Serbian defender does well to recover and Jaouen gets a rare touch on the ball as he clears his lines.

Triple substitution from Howe. Hall, Ramsey and Willock make way for Salia, Munda and Charlton.

Sanusi and Park replace Murphy and Barnes.

There is the first yellow card of the match. Home lands an overzealous challenge on Willock in the centre of the pitch and receives a booking for his troubles.

Ferreira is then played into the left channel and unleashes a shot which is turned behind for a corner by Desbois, who has been awesome this afternoon.

Jaouen, Miley and Ferreira replace Pope, Shahar and Neave.

Gateshead are sitting deeper meaning that their penalty area is often getting quite congested.

Murphy switches wings to create an overload with Barnes down the left and flashes a cross into the box which is dealt with by Gateshead. Newcastle need more invention like that if they are to break down this stubborn Gateshead side.

An immediate chance for the hosts’ front man Boatswain at the start of the second half. The ball just gets away from him.

Newcastle have work to do and, unlike last weekend against Darlington, Howe sticks with the same XI at the start of the second period. Gateshead also unchanged.

Newcastle go into the break a goal down. There have been chances for the visitors, who dominated the ball in that first period. Expect changes at the interval.

Gateshead’s goal came against the run of play and was there first shot on target. It’s not great from Fabian Schar, who conceded the free kick competing for a long ball down the middle and Nick Pope was a little slow off his line to smother the shot too.

Neave comes close to opening the scoring, firing an effort across the face of goal that goes behind for a corner.

Hall then gets a shot away from the edge of the box, but cannot keep his half-volley down and the ball sails over the bar.

Newcastle look most dangerous when Schar steps up and punches in those line-breaking passes. Gateshead defending resolutely, though, keeping things compact across the backline.

Murphy earns his side a free-kick down the right. He delivers the ball himself, with the box loaded with Schar and Murphy, and the former steals in to the near post but cannot quite stoop down low enough to get a meaningful contact on the ball. Desbois gathers without fuss.

Newcastle have won a glut of corners down their left, all of which have been taken short. The latest is played out to Steur who rains in a cross which is claimed by the goalkeeper.

Sean Steur looks like a player... some really nice touches from the young Dutchman. He is always looking to make a progressive pass and has been a real bright spark. Newcastle have dominated the game. As you would expect against opposition four divisions below them

Another tidy involvement from Steur, who disguises a pass to Ramsey on the edge of the box. The ball is worked into the path of Murphy and deflects out for a corner. The former Ajax midfielder is growing in confidence.

Hall puts in another ball from the left, this time to the back post, where the ball is headed away by Ferguson.

New signing Steur is starting to creep forward, carrying the ball nicely and picking it back up in the right channel. He stands a cross up to the near post but Murphy’s header is dealt with by Desbois.

Hall works a yard of space in a dangerous area down the left moments later, but the ball ricochets back off him and out for goal-kick.

Hall punches in a lovely ball down the line for Barnes to run on to, but the move is snuffed out by Robinson.

It does seem strange that this game has not sold out. There are thought to be about 7,000 fans inside the stadium, which once had a capacity of more than 11,000 when it was one of the country’s premier athletics venues. They even used to have Diamond League events here not so long ago.

But the capacity has been steadily reduced for safety reasons and it is rarely used for anything other than local athletic events and Gateshead FC games.

There were officially only 50 tickets left for sale a few minutes before kick-off, but there are lots of empty seats.

Chadwick lofts a tidy cross in from the left, but Boatswain’s header drifts wide of the mark. The chance came off a decent spell of possession from Cattermole’s side, the most fluent they have been in this match so far.

Ramsey regains possession high up the pitch and releases Barnes who plays in Murphy, but the Newcastle forward mistimes his run and the linesman’s flag goes up. A promising counter.

Ramsey is brought down on the edge of the box as he tries to break free and the referee awards a free-kick. There are a few contenders to take it (Schar, Barnes, Hall) but in the end it is Barnes who gets a shot away, but his curled effort flies just wide of the mark.

Another weighted ball over the top from Schar puts Anifowose under pressure in the left channel but his ball across the face of goal is cleared to safety by a team-mate.

Newcastle circulating the ball in front of Gateshead’s first line of pressure. The hosts regain possession but struggle to find a way through Newcastle’s midfield.

Schar getting a few early touches as he makes his return from injury. He plays a long, raking diagonal out to Barnes who cannot quite get past his man.

Neave tests Desbois with a well-struck effort off the next phase of play.

The officials and both sets of players line up behind a banner with the message ‘Rest in peace, Kevin Keegan’. Newcastle are in their new navy-blue away shirt, with Gateshead in their home white-and-black kit. A minute’s silence is then observed immaculately.

The tributes left in honour of Kevin Keegan outside St James’ Park is a sight to behold, with flowers, shirts and scarves covering the ground and steps in the south-west corner. It is a very moving thing to behold as people come to pay their respects to the Newcastle legend.

There will also be a minute’s silence before today’s game against Gateshead.

It has been a difficult and, at times, acrimonious 12 months for Eddie Howe, who must have wondered whether the job was still worth the hassle given the criticism and online vitriol he received at times last season.

Few would have blamed him if he had quit, but Howe has always been fully committed and always knew there would be a period like this to come through.

He has been in the job almost five years and last season was the first time he had been vilified by a section of the fanbase. It left its mark. The boos that followed defeats at St James’ Park hurt and he worried the unity that had powered the team’s success had fractured irreparably.

The apparent collective shrug that greeted another run to the Carabao Cup semi-final, while guiding the team into the knockout rounds of the Champions League for the first time was a source of bewilderment and frustration.

Howe has not complained or moaned. Although he wobbled towards the end of last season and there were some calling for him to be sacked, he was supported and encouraged by those above him. That loyalty mattered.

The problem is, negativity lingers in the fanbase. Even a picture of Howe at pre-season training, posted on social media by the club, led to abusive comments questioning his ability and character. Some of it was toxic. It was rightly called out by other supporters.

Goals from Elliot Anderson (wonder what happened to him?!), Allan Saint-Maximin and Jay Turner-Cooke helped Newcastle overturn a 2-0 half-time deficit when they last visited Gateshead International Stadium in 2023.

Speaking through Gateshead’s club media, Cattermole said of facing Newcastle: “It’s obviously a different test. We have to respect the opposition, they’re a high-quality team and it might not be what we’re getting in our league but we’ll still try to implement what we believe we want to be in and out of possession. It’ll be a great physical challenge for us.

He added: “They [my players] have all shown up great. What a game for them. What a game for them to go and test yourself against some big names and fantastic coaching staff, for us all it’s a great challenge for us. We hope we give them a good test, we hope we give them the challenge they want as well. I played in many of these games as a player as well. We expect it to be competitive.”

💬 "What a game for [the players] to go & play."Lee Cattermole talks tomorrow's game against @NUFC at the GIS ⤵️📺👉 https://t.co/DGuJRosJ2K pic.twitter.com/rccs5FzhG6

A classic first-game-of-pre-season vibe to Newcastle’s team sheet as established stars rub shoulders with youngsters from the academy.

Only one of their four summer signings, former Ajax midfielder Sean Steur, starts the game and there will be a lot of interest in the 18-year-old. The youngster has impressed in training over the last couple of weeks but it is thought he has a lot of work to do physically to be ready for the Premier League.

Full-back Leo Shahar was in and around the first team last season as was striker Sean Neave. Alex Murphy, who started one game in the Champions League last season is expected to go out on loan before the window shuts, but starts alongside Fabian Schar in the centre of defence.

Worryingly there is no sign of Sven Botman and Will Osula who both played in the behind-closed-doors friendly against Darlington last weekend.

Joelinton, Tino Livramento and Lewis Miley are still being eased back into things after injuries at the end of last season.

Another new signing, goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen, is on the bench and will play the second half against their National League neighbours.

Gateshead lost manager Rob Elliot to Carlisle at the end of last season and are now managed by former Sunderland and Middlesbrough midfielder Lee Cattermole.

Arrivals in Gateshead 👋 pic.twitter.com/9hTtruxGEo

Ready for our return to the GIS! 🤍🔢 pic.twitter.com/lg1TfjyD6q

Fabian Schär returns from an ankle injury that has sidelined him since January, but only one of Newcastle’s four summer signings (Sean Steur) starts.

Welcome to live coverage of Newcastle United’s pre-season friendly against North-East neighbours Gateshead. Eddie Howe’s side make the three-mile journey south of the River Tyne having beaten Darlington 3-0 in their first outing of the summer last weekend. The Magpies’ National League opponents this afternoon, helmed by former Sunderland captain Lee Cattermole, have already played three times in pre-season, thrashing Blyth 6-0 and drawing against Heaton Stannington and Hebburn Town. The Heed threatened a shock win in their last meeting with Newcastle three summers’ ago, leading 2-0 at the interval before conceding three second-half goals.

This contest at Gateshead International Stadium will be Newcastle’s first match since the death of Kevin Keegan and the club have confirmed that a minute of silence will be observed before kick-off. Newcastle’s men’s, women’s and academy teams will wear black armbands for all pre-season matches this summer.

Newcastle United's men's, women's and Under-21s teams will wear black armbands across all pre-season matches this summer as the club honours the life of Kevin Keegan.Full details ⤵️

Newcastle will welcome Liverpool, with whom Keegan enjoyed success in the 1970s, to St James’ Park for their Premier League opener, and the two sides are in talks over a suitable pre-match tribute. Flowers, messages and mementos have been laid outside Newcastle’s ground since Keegan’s death on Monday, including a heartfelt message penned by fellow club legend Alan Shearer, which read: “I hope you realised how much you meant, to me, to this club, to everyone. Thank you does not seem enough. Rest In Peace Boss. Alan Shearer.”

With regards to the football, there is an acceptance among Newcastle supporters that, having finished 12th in the Premier League last season and lost Anthony Gordon, Kieran Trippier and Sandro Tonali, this is a summer of transition. The uncertainty surrounding the future of £100m-rated club captain Bruno Guimarães, who is on the radar of Arsenal, will be a concern; Newcastle will be keen to avoid a repeat of the furore that circled Alexander Isak’s departure last summer. Guimarães will join the team next week following his World Cup exploits with Brazil and is expected to take part in Newcastle’s La Manga training camp, which starts on July 31.

Summer signings Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen were each handed 45 minutes in the behind-closed-doors victory over Darlington, during which Howe used different XIs for the two halves. Bazoumana Touré – the £50m winger acquired from Hoffenheim – is expected to feature today having returned from his post-World Cup holiday. Yesterday Newcastle announced the arrival of midfielder Aladji Bamba, the France youth international, from Monaco and he was immediately integrated into team training. There is every possibility that he will feature this afternoon. Gateshead this week announced two signings of their own, as Luke Supyk, the New Zealand Under-20 forward, agreed a two-year deal having scored three goals in pre-season as a trialist. Defender Jack Robinson also joined the club.

#2244. Swansea City must offer new deal to emerging talent after outstanding first-team breakthrough: Opinion

Swansea City have been the surprise team in the Championship this campaign. The Swans sit 2nd in the table and have the joint-best defensive record in the league.

Their brilliant start after 13 games isn’t the only shock to Vitor Matos, with the emergence of Filip Lissah from the academy also welcome. The 21-year-old spent last season on loan at Falkirk in the Scottish Premiership, and his displays there have translated to the Welsh outfit’s first team.

The Swansea City defender has missed just one game this term due to suspension. With his improving performances each week, conversations within the club must be held to discuss his future, especially with his contract only running until 2028.

The Swans can extend Lissah’s current deal by 12 months when his contract expires at the end of the 2027 season. They are certain to take up the option, but they should address any future uncertainty by offering him a long-term improved deal.

The 21-year-old has been one of Swansea City’s standout players this term. Regardless of his contract status, the Welsh outfit must secure his future. The academy graduate has made 91 line-breaking passes this campaign and won 73 duels.

Despite being naturally a centre-back, Lissah has proven to be a dependable option in defence for his boyhood club. He has put in terrific displays also at right-back. The Czech U21 international has made 84 defensive contributions alongside winning 15 fouls for Matos’ side.

His quality in attack only adds value that the Swans must protect. He has made 506 successful passes this campaign and 26 accurate long balls. With his first goal for the club last Saturday too, the ceiling is sky high for the youngster.

Swansea City could have had hit a real dip in form should Lissah not have been able to step up at right-back. He has already proven to be a quality asset at centre-back with a particularly dominant display against Derby County back in August, where he made 12 clearances and won 86% of his aerial duels.

With Josh Key sidelined back in September for a month, the Swans technically had no replacements for the 26-year-old. When Lissah was suspended for a game, Matos had to turn to Ronald, and the Welsh outfit suffered defeat against West Ham.

Now, with Key returning to action at the weekend against Blackburn Rovers, the 21-year-old faces some competition for a spot in the starting XI. However, given the pedigree of his displays in his debut Championship season, it’s become his position to lose.

#2243. La Fiorentina vince la sfida tra le squadre in crisi. E il Sassuolo sprofonda

Importante successo della Fiorentina sul campo del Sassuolo, in una partita fra due squadre in crisi. I viola tornano a vincere 52 giorni dopo l'ultima volta, quando espugnarono Venezia per 2-4. E Al Mapei Stadium finisce col medesimo risultato.

Non è bastato ai neroverdi la doppietta di Armand Laurienté, che si è finalmente sbloccato. Dopo il vantaggio, gli emiliani hanno subito il pari nei minuti di recupero del primo tempo da Pellegrino su assist di Njie. Lo svedese con una perla nella ripresa porta avanti ai viola, prima del 2-2. Infine Mastantuono e Valdepenas portano i tre punti a Firenze.

È alla fine Njie a prendersi il premio di MVP della partita, mentre a Sassuolo la situazione precipita: nelle ultime 6 partite la squadra ha incassato un solo punto. E, cosa altrettanto preoccupante, la difesa colabrodo, capace di incassare 16 reti nelle ultime 4 partite. Il tecnico Alberto Aquilani ha evidenziato una preoccupante fragilità della squadra, al primo episodio sfavorevole. E preoccupa il calendario, che porrà i neroverdi prima della sosta nazionale contro la Roma, la squadra col migliore attacco del torneo.

#2242. A Bergamo l'Atalanta si scioglie davanti al cinismo del Parma: 0-3, la Dea è in crisi

Il Parma si ritrova a Bergamo, con 3 gol tutti insieme dopo un inizio davvero stentato dal punto di vista della produzione offensiva e fa entrare l'Atalanta nel tunnel della crisi, non sono di risultati. Dopo venti minuti arrembanti la Dea perde di mordente nei propri assalti e il Parma prende campo, anche se il gol arriva solo su episodio e al primo tiro in porta dei ducali (contro i due della Dea, ndr). Nella ripresa l'Atalanta si sfalda totalmente e la squadra di Gilardino dilaga, con l'autogol di Zappacosta e il supergol di Lontani che chiudono il discorso tre punti.

Ai microfoni di Sky, l’allenatore del Parma Alberto Gilardino ha commentato la vittoria di Bergamo: “Non avrei mai pensato al 3-0, ma di fare una partita importante sì. Così è stato, la fotografia della partita è chiara. Abbiamo sofferto nei primi venti minuti, dopo il vantaggio ci siamo sbloccati sia mentalmente che dal punto di vista del gioco. Difensivamente siamo stati incredibili, poi siamo stati bravi a fare il 2-0 e il 3-0. I ragazzi si meritano la vittoria, in queste settimane abbiamo fatto discrete prestazioni ma abbiamo perso. Lì abbiamo costruito questa vittoria: dalle sconfitte si crea qualcosa di forte, sono contento per i ragazzi”.

L'allenatore dell'Atalanta Maurizio Sarri ha parlato così a DAZN: "Abbiamo fatto i primi 40 minuti di ottimo livello, avevamo la gara in mano. Abbiamo preso gol su una palla ferma e ne abbiamo pagato le conseguenze. Siamo poi rientrati male e da lì è venuto fuori questo secondo tempo che si accetta male. Chiediamo scusa a società e tifosi per il secondo tempo, nel primo abbiamo giocato una delle migliori frazioni della stagione. Non si può essere così fragili difensivamente e mentalmente. Staremo insieme qualche giorno e parleremo. Ci è venuta paura, la partita era in controllo fino al primo gol. Ci siamo impauriti e innervositi e ne abbiamo pagato le conseguenze. C'era tempo per rimettere in piedi la gara, continuando sulla falsa riga del primo tempo e invece abbiamo fatto quello che abbiamo fatto".

#2241. ‘Surely’: Reporter makes bold prediction regarding ‘outstanding’ Middlesbrough summer recruit

Middlesbrough signed the attacker from Tottenham Hotspur in the summer and he penned a long-term five-year deal at the Riverside Stadium running until June 2031. He has since adapted well to life at Boro and has been prolific for Kim Hellberg‘s side.

Lankshear, 21, has made 16 appearances in all competitions this season, 13 of which have come in the Championship. He has chipped in with an eye-catching 15 goals already.

Journalist Cottier has delivered his verdict, as per a report by BBC Sport: “Fifteen goals in all competitions is an outstanding number to have reached before the end of October and Middlesbrough look to have quelled any concerns that they cannot be in this promotion race for the long haul. They are exciting, creative and solid at the back – and in Lankshear they have a young Englishman surely destined to get senior international recognition in the not-too-distant future.”

Middlesbrough beat Charlton Athletic 3-0 at home last time out and remain top of the table above Swansea City, Wolves and West Brom after 13 fixtures. They are back in action on Wednesday away at Wrexham as they aim to keep their momentum going for as long as possible.

Middlesbrough’s decision to snap up Lankshear from Tottenham Hotspur has turned out to be a masterstroke. He has established himself as Boro’s most prized asset.

Boro lacked a proper number nine in the last campaign and that was mainly the reason why they missed out on the top two. They then lacked a cutting edge in the play-offs, hence why they eventually lost to Hull City in the final at Wembley in May.

Lankshear has answered their prayers though and he has more than proved that he knows where the back of the net is. He is already on 15 goals and November has only just begun.

The ex-Arsenal and Sheffield United man played six times during his days at Tottenham Hotspur before they sold him permanently. He also had loan spells away from Spurs at West Brom and Oxford United to get some experience under his belt and to boost his development.

Middlesbrough ace Lankshear is one of the most exciting young English players around at the moment. The fact he is playing every week at Boro and not sitting around on Tottenham Hotspur’s bench will be doing him the world of good.

Hellberg’s men are on a roll right now but they can’t afford to be complacent as they aim to claw themselves into the top flight this term. They will need to be at their best to get another three points against Wrexham later this week.

#2240. Perché a Napoli la cabala non basta: come funziona davvero la roulette

Centottantadue estrazioni di assenza durò, tra il 2003 e il febbraio del 2005, l’attesa del 53 sulla ruota di Venezia, il ritardatario più celebre nella storia del Lotto italiano, su cui gli scommettitori riversarono diversi miliardi di euro nella convinzione che la sua uscita fosse ormai questione di giorni. A Napoli, dove la smorfia e la cabala fanno parte del lessico familiare tanto quanto il caffè, quella vicenda viene ancora citata come esempio di come il caso sappia sfuggire a qualsiasi calcolo affettivo, e le stesse convinzioni che accompagnano il Lotto finiscono spesso per trasferirsi davanti al cilindro della roulette, un gioco con regole matematiche molto diverse.

La smorfia napoletana nasce per il Lotto, e i suoi novanta numeri associati a sogni, eventi e figure della vita quotidiana (il 90 come la paura, il 33 come gli anni di Cristo, il 17 come la disgrazia) appartengono a un sistema di interpretazione simbolica, non a un metodo di previsione. Applicata alla roulette, la cabala incontra subito un ostacolo strutturale, perché il cilindro della versione europea contiene soltanto trentasette caselle, dallo zero al trentasei, e oltre metà dei numeri della smorfia non trova alcun corrispettivo sul tappeto verde. Molti giocatori aggirano il problema con riduzioni e somme di cifre, trasformando per esempio un 77 in un 14, ma ogni passaggio aggiunge soltanto un livello di arbitrarietà, senza alcun effetto sulla probabilità che la pallina si fermi su una casella piuttosto che su un’altra.

Il confronto tra i due approcci è netto. La cabala attribuisce ai numeri un significato, mentre la roulette assegna a ciascuno la stessa identica probabilità, pari a una su trentasette, indipendentemente dal sogno della notte precedente o dalla data di un anniversario.

La caccia ai ritardatari è forse la convinzione più radicata, e si basa sull’idea che un numero assente da molto tempo debba prima o poi “recuperare”. Il ragionamento ha un fascino intuitivo, ma la matematica lo smentisce da più di un secolo, perché ogni lancio della pallina è un evento indipendente, privo di memoria rispetto ai precedenti. La storia della roulette conserva il caso più famoso, avvenuto al Casinò di Monte Carlo il 18 agosto 1913, quando il nero uscì per ventisei volte consecutive e i giocatori persero cifre enormi puntando sul rosso, certi che la serie dovesse spezzarsi a ogni giro.

Gli statistici chiamano l’errore fallacia del giocatore, e il 53 di Venezia ne è la versione italiana. Nel lungo periodo le frequenze di ciascun numero tendono ad avvicinarsi alla media teorica, ma il riequilibrio avviene per diluizione su migliaia di estrazioni e non attraverso una “compensazione” a breve termine, come dimostra il fatto che il 53, una volta uscito, non abbia avuto alcun obbligo di ripresentarsi più spesso degli altri.

Accanto alla cabala si collocano i sistemi di progressione, metodi che regolano l’importo delle giocate in base agli esiti precedenti. La Martingala prevede di raddoppiare la puntata dopo ogni sconfitta sulle chances semplici, così che la prima vittoria copra tutte le perdite accumulate, mentre il sistema D’Alembert aumenta e riduce la posta di un’unità alla volta, con oscillazioni più contenute. Entrambi modificano la distribuzione delle vincite e delle perdite nel tempo, ma non toccano il dato che conta, cioè il vantaggio del banco, che nella roulette europea resta fisso al 2,7% su qualsiasi tipo di puntata, dal numero pieno pagato 35 a 1 fino al rosso o nero pagato alla pari.

La Martingala, in particolare, si scontra con i limiti massimi del tavolo, perché otto sconfitte consecutive con una puntata iniziale di 5 euro portano la nona giocata a 1.280 euro, una soglia che molti tavoli non accettano.

Se cabala e sistemi lasciano intatte le probabilità, la scelta della variante di roulette le modifica in modo concreto. La versione americana aggiunge al cilindro il doppio zero, con trentotto caselle complessive, e il margine della casa sale al 5,26%, quasi il doppio rispetto alla versione europea. La roulette francese prevede invece in molti casi la regola della partage, in base alla quale l’uscita dello zero restituisce metà della puntata sulle chances semplici, dimezzando il vantaggio del banco all’1,35% su quel tipo di giocata.

La conoscenza delle regole vale dunque più di qualsiasi numero sognato la notte prima, e le schede informative del gioco della roulette indicano per ogni tavolo la variante in uso, la tabella dei pagamenti e l’eventuale applicazione della partage, dati da leggere prima di puntare con lo stesso scrupolo con cui un napoletano consulta la smorfia, ma con la consapevolezza che a decidere sarà soltanto la pallina.

#2239. James Penrice hit with former referee verdict on 'instant red card' vs Aberdeen

James Penrice should have been "instantly" sent off for Rangers in their Premier Sports Cup semi-final against Aberdeen on Saturday evening.

That's the view of former FIFA referee Keith Hackett after he watched the defender catch Dons' Afeez Aremu high in a clash at Hampden.

Gers saw off their foes to reach the showpiece finale next month after Ryan Naderi found the net in his side's narrow 1-0 victory. But it could have been different had Penrice been shown a red card by referee Ryan Lee.

Penrice clearly caught Aremu on the hip with his studs and the debate raged on whether or not the force was enough to see Penrice given his marching orders. But after the whistler did not even produce a yellow for the challenge, VAR official John Beaton refused to intervene and the player continued.

Then he helped tee up Naderi for the winner.

Hackett had his say on Football Insider and insisted the former Hearts ace was lucky to avoid punishment. In fact the retired official could hardly believe the outcome.

He said: "I have to ask how James Penrice was allowed to stay on the field of play, when his high boot was in contact with the chest of his opponent.

"That was clearly serious foul play, and should have seen a red card produced instantly. The fact that no action was taken comes as a surprise. Why was there no intervention by VAR?"

Rangers will now face the winner of the Edinburgh Derby in the first cup final of the campaign.
