#2237. Chelsea in 10-goal thriller as ‘Alonso ball’ brings risk and reward

Chelsea’s first match under the management of Xabi Alonso was a 10-goal thriller in Australia, as the Premier League side eventually showed their class in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Star striker João Pedro, who was controversially left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming off the bench with half an hour of the friendly remaining.

Alonso had selected a youthful team for the first hour before bringing nine senior players, including João Pedro, into the side in the second half. According to Transfermarkt, Chelsea’s squad is valued at over £1.3bn while their opponents a more modest £5.86m.

Teenage signing Dastan Satpayev, midfielder Dario Essugo and winger Jamie Gittens also found the net for Chelsea, who were defensively vulnerable for long spells for the game.

Here are five things Telegraph Sport learned from Alonso’s first match.

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

As expected, Alonso tasked his players with deploying a possession-based strategy in which the ball is worked from back to front between the lines. At times, Alonso’s vision was executed in style: Chelsea’s two goals in the first half were both the consequence of slick passing moves.

There were plenty of other occasions, though, when Chelsea were sloppy in their passing and defensively exposed when they lost the ball. The best example of this was in the second half, when Estêvão’s error allowed Western Sydney Wanderers to score their fourth goal of the game.

Admittedly, Chelsea’s attempts to play passing football were not helped by the poor quality of the pitch in Sydney. A recent rugby game had created a bobbly, unpredictable surface which caused no end of problems for Chelsea’s midfield players. That may sound like an excuse for their sloppiness, but it is probably a fair one.

Chelsea started the game with two Reggies in their midfield. Reggie Walsh is a 17-year-old technician who last year became the club’s third-youngest player, and was loved by former head coach Enzo Maresca. He played as the No 10.

Reggie Watson, meanwhile, is the son of former Premier League midfielder Ben and is one of the most exciting talents in English football. A composed central midfielder, Watson is a regular for England’s youth teams and is the youngest player on Chelsea’s pre-season tour.

Both players showed glimpses of their talent in this match in Sydney. Watson was trusted with set-piece duties and produced some excellent deliveries, while also playing some lovely passes through the lines. Watson was the only Chelsea player to feature for the full 90 minutes, which spoke volumes of the quality of his performance.

Walsh was less involved but caught the eye in a couple of moments, not least when playing a delicate one-two with Essugo in advance of the midfielder’s first-half strike.

Satpayev is technically not a Chelsea player yet, as his deal officially commences when he turns 18 in August. His former club, Kairat, gave special dispensation to allow the teenager to join Chelsea’s pre-season tour ahead of the completion of his £3m transfer, which means he is officially in Australia as a “triallist”.

Satpayev is a player of obvious talent and has already played nine games for Kazakhstan. Before this move to Chelsea, he scored 21 goals in 41 games in the Kazakhstan Premier League.

The first sighting of Satpayev was an exciting one for Chelsea supporters, who saw the new man’s running speed and shooting power as he scored the opening goal of the game. Running in behind the Western Sydney Wanderers defence, Satpayev surged clear of the opposition and launched a scorching shot into the roof of the net.

Gittens endured a hugely disappointing first campaign at Chelsea last season, following his £52m move from Borussia Dortmund. Injury issues did not help his cause but he struggled to make much of an impact when he was fully fit, scoring just one goal in 27 appearances in all competitions.

Gittens is therefore a man with it all to prove at Stamford Bridge this season, and he has started the new campaign in promising form. His goal here came after two strikes in two behind-closed-doors friendly games before Chelsea left for Australia. Gittens was a constant threat after coming onto the pitch in the 63rd minute, showing his pace on the wing and his ability to go down the touchline or cut inside. His challenge now is to replicate this level of performance against better opposition.

A late revival ensures Chelsea win their first pre-season friendly under Xabi Alonso. There was a step up in class once Palmer, Pedro, Gittens, Estevao and Palestra were introduced, and the Australian side could not contain them. No injuries on a dogy pitching probably the biggest victory for the new manager.

Just the three minutes of added time to play.

Three goals in nine minutes for the Brazilian. Excellent corner delivery from Estevao, Fofana’s header blocked but then Joao Pedro turns home from close range. Baffling decision by Brazil not to take him to the World Cup.

Chelsea flooding forward again, and they have a corner in the last minute of normal time.

Chelsea now lead 5-4, Cole Palmer picking out Joao Pedro with the through ball but Western Sydney Wanderers were far too open. Joao Pedro shows his composure, sitting the defender down and rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

Estevao shows he has not lost his burst of speed after that serious hamstring injury but his shot flies straight into the side netting. Joao Pedro then delights the crowd with another piece of skill.

Jamie Gittens is having a good pre-season, having scored in two behind-closed-doors friendlies before this game in Australia. He has looked sharp since coming off the bench and has been involved in two of Chelsea’s goals.

Gittens had a disappointing first season at Chelsea following his £52m move from Dortmund last summer and is clearly keen to impress Alonso.

Robert Sanchez picks out Gittens with a raking pass, but his shot is blocked. The same is true for Joao Pedro’s follow up attempt. Gittens has impressed since coming on.

Poor defensive header back into a dangerous area from Gittens’s cross, but it is a crisp touch and finish from Joao Pedro, picking out the bottom corner. Chelsea level at 4-4. The move started with a quick free-kick, from Palmer, which he won.

Western Sydney Wanderers score their fourth goal of the game. Chelsea make another error when playing out from the back, it was Estevao who sold Reggie Watson short. One pass and one shot later, Awan Lual finishes beyond Sanchez.

Mazy run inside from Estevao off the right flank, but there was not quite enough power in his shot to beat the goalkeeper.

Joao Pedro is very good at taking the ball in and making it stick. Palestra looks very progressive from right-back, looks full of running and attacking intent.

Some of Western Sydney Wanderers’s corner routines have been quite nifty, Chelsea opened up from a short one again. Palmer with a velvety touch in midield and pass forward towards Palestra who was breaking forward.

Gittens scores, and the introduction of the senior players has made a difference already. Levi Colwill started the move with a longer pass forward, before Joao Pedro skips through challenges to tee up Gittens.

Nine changes made by Alonso: Palmer, Estevao, Palestra, Gittens, Sanchez, Colwill, Anselmino, Joao Pedro and Fofana are the players who have come on.

The Australian side now lead. Emenalo’s clearance deflects off a Western Sydney Wanderers player, and falls kindly to Scicluna, who drills his show beyond Sharman-Lowe into the bottom corner. He come the Chelsea changes.

Western Sydney Wanderers playing some good football in the last few minutes, Saptaev outmuscled in midfield and a shot comes in from the edge of the area. Sharman-Lowe saves, then Tosin clears after a short corner routine.

This young Chelsea side, which is still dealing with jet lag, looks a little tired now. They have not been under huge pressure but they can hardly complain about falling 3-2 behind. Here come all the big names, as Alonso makes huge changes for the last 30 minutes.

Chelsea enjoying a spell of comfortable possession, the tempo of the game has dropped. Good play again, from Reggie Watson, finding Emenalo on the overlap but he slices his shot high and wide when there was time to take aim.

Chelsea remain committed to passing out from the back, but the uneven pitch is making that difficult. Sharman-Lowe passes the ball straight out for a throw-in. Good defending from Acheampong to deal with a teasing cross.

Chelsea win a free-kick in a shooting position, and Reggie Watson takes it with his right foot. He goes goalkeeper’s side but, it shot curls just wide of the post.

Western Sydney Wanderers kick off in the second half.

Kellyman on for Essugo in midfield, and Nicoll-Jazuli replaces Kavuma-McQueen.

Some eye-catching football from Chelsea going forward, but some loose defending too. Suspect it is not long before we see Palmer, Estevao, Colwill and Joao Pedro. Walsh and Watson have done well in midfield for Chelsea.

Half-time! 🕰️Watch the second half LIVE on CFC+ 📺

Another really bad miss from Tosin. Free header from a corner, could see it all the way, but he skewed the ball wide from a just a couple of yards out. Chelsea should be in front.

Subuloye wins a back post header from the Chelsea corner, but the “home” team clear. More goals in this game, surely. Saptaev wins Chelsea a corner with another burst forward.

This is a great team goal. Essugo started the move, finding Saptaev down the left. Essugo moves the ball on two Walsh, who gives it him back with a slick one-two and Essugo rolls the ball into the bottom corner.

That’s the second impressive team goal that Chelsea have scored in this first half. Essugo to Walsh, Walsh to Essugo, Essugo finds the corner. Walsh, 17, has produced some nice touches in the No 10 position. Last year he became the third-youngest player in Chelsea’s history and you can see he is a supremely talented teenager.

Chelsea in trouble defensively again, passing their way into trouble on the edge of their defensive third. I’m sure there will be a raft of half-time changes, but that was probably the plan all along.

Chelsea have been alarmingly open and easy to play through. The collective structure and individual defending were both poor in advance of that second Western Sydney Wanderers goal. I expect they’ll tighten up when the more experienced players come into the game.

Hammond is the goalscorer, and it is a finish of genuine quality. Silky touch to flick the ball inside Josh Acheampong, and fire low into the bottom corner. Soft Chelsea defending, though.

Smooth combination play from Walsh and Watson, the two Reggies in Chelsea’s midfield, before Saptaev shoots over the bar form the edge of the box. A shame for marketing people and headline writers that one of Walsh or Watson are not called Ronnie.

Reggie Watson with a foul in midfield. Fair to say Chelsea’s youthful team are on the back foot now, but there was nice turn in midfield from Essugo after more passing out from the back. Clear that is an emphasis for Alonso.

Sharman-Lowe claims a cross, but Western Sydney Wanderers down their right flank again. I almost anticipated a hydration break at this stage, but it is back to business as usual. Chelsea flagging a touch after a lively start.

Chelsea’s defence looking a touch exposed again, but Borrello curls a shot wide of the post. Emenalo has down well going forward but there was space down his side there.

Two causes for concern for Chelsea in the first 15 minutes here. The first is the pitch in Sydney, which looks terrible. The ball is bobbling all over midfield, making it very difficult for Chelsea’s central players in particular. The second concern will be their defending for that set-piece, as Western Sydney Wanderers had two free headers.

Liam Delap has not been particularly involved, but Reggie Watson almost found him with a cute reverse pass. Watson the plays a progressive pass forward from deep.

Reggie Walsh pushes forward and takes on a shot from long range. Well struck, another save from the goalkeeper. From the resulting corner, taken by Watson, Tosin misses a free header. Good chance, should have hit the target.

Chelsea concede from the corner. Flicked on at the near post and a free header at the back stick for Anthony Pantazopoulos. One for Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’ new set-piece coach, to clip up and show in the team meeting.

Emenalo fouled after more neat football out from the back by Chelsea. Alonso is on his feet on the touchline, barking instructions. Emenalo has showed some silky touches.

Chance for Western Sydney Wanderers though, nut Sharman-Lowe tips Gillion’s shot around the post.

The pitch is very, very bobbly. Excellent strike from Kavuma-McQueen for Chelsea, but Holmes tips the shot around the post.

Was that the first glimpse of “Alonso-ball”? It’s a lovely team goal, worked from back to front with some incisive passing. Terrific, powerful finish by Dastan Satpayev, the 17-year-old Kazakh, who joined from FC Kairat this summer. He already has nine caps for Kazakhstan.

Technically speaking, Satpayev is not officially a Chelsea player yet and is a “triallist” on this tour. He will be formally unveiled when he turns 18 in August.

The 17-year-old summer signing from Kairat Almaty has put Chelsea in front. It was a nice move from their own defensive third, drawing Western Sydney Wanderers on creating a two-on-two against their defence. Satpaev goes through and blasts a shot into the roof of the net. Good through ball from Ryan Kavuma-McQueen.

Chelsea youngsters Walsh and Watson do well in midfield, and they have a free-kick on halfway. Reggie Watson is the son of former Crystal Palace and Wigan Athletic midfielder Ben. A couple of stray kicks from Chelsea’s goalkeeper Teddy Sharman-Lowe. An opening for the hosts, but Hammond’s strike is wayward.

Landon Emenalo is playing at left wing-back, and he is the son of former Chelsea director of football Michael. He has had one burst forward already, and is called into some early defending to concede a throw in.

Chelsea get the game under way. The pitch looks very patchy. Incredible how clubs are willing to play mutli-million pound assets on surfaces like this.

Western Sydney Wanderers in horizontal red and black stripes, Chelsea in the season’s new blue home kit.

Off the bus. 🚎 pic.twitter.com/0sBDuEtzog

A very youthful team from the start, with some big hitters on the bench. Dastan Satpaev, 17, is a £2.1m summer signing from Kairat Almaty.

Chelsea XI: Sharman-Lowe, Acheampong, Tosin, Subuloye, Emenalo, Walsh, Watson, Essugo, Delap, Satpaev, Kavuma-McQueen

Subs: Sanchez, Curd, Palestra, Colwill, Fofana, Anselmino, Diakite, Lavia, Kellyman, Nicoll-Jazuli, Palmer, Gittens, Estevao, Joao Pedro

Chelsea started their pre-season with a 3-0 victory over Bromley in a behind-closed-doors friendly, but this morning we will have our first proper look at Xabi Alonso’s team as they take on Western Sydney Wanderers.

There was some interesting news from Stamford Bridge on Monday when it emerged the club are in talks to sign Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson. Coming after the fruitless pursuit of Granit Xhaka, the strategy suggests that Alonso has made cultural improvement a priority in a dressing room that has been accused of lacking discipline and leadership.

As ever, Chelsea have been busy in the transfer market with Morgan Rogers and Marco Palestra their headline signings, and Geovany Quenda joins up with the club from Sporting CP having been signed in March 2025.

Rogers is yet to join up with his new team-mates following his World Cup exertions with England, but fans will be looking forward to seeing how he combines with Cole Palmer.

“In that position, we needed an important player, and I’m sure that there were not many more better options than Morgan,” the 44-year-old manager told reporters. “It means a lot for everyone.”

Tasked with reviving Chelsea after a turbulent, trophyless season in which the west London club finished 10th ⁠in the Premier League, Alonso believes Rogers can combine effectively with Palmer.

“I have a plan. I have an idea. I can see them linking really well,” Alonso said of ​Rogers and Palmer, who are close ‌friends and England teammates.

“You need to have a good mix, good stability players, and players that can play with more freedom.

“And if we get that ‌balance right, ​and we get ⁠those special players in the right positions, with good control, I think that we will be more ⁠competitive with the ball ​and against the ball.”

#2236. Four chances created: 30-year-old justifies new Southampton contract talk with starring role in QPR thrashing

Southampton continued their rise up the Championship table on Saturday as they defeated QPR 4-1, making it five undefeated. The Saints are now up in 5th, recovering well from the four-point deduction they started the campaign with.

It was a fine display from Tonda Eckert’s side in their routine triumph. The goals were shared across the team with Kuryu Matsuki, Cam Bragg, Keven Schlotterbeck and Welington netting, but one man who had a key role in two of the goals was Ryan Manning.

It was Manning’s pull-back that Bragg converted from for the second, and a deep corner of his found Schlotterbeck completely free at the back post to make it 3-0. In a week where news has emerged of Southampton’s talks to renew his contract, the 30-year-old further strengthened the case for his deal.

Creation was where Manning stood out on Saturday. Alongside his aforementioned pair of assists, the Irishman created the joint-most chances in the game with four – tied with Southampton teammate Finn Azaz.

His set-piece ability was on display as a deep, in-swinging cross to the back stick almost saw centre-back Schlotterbeck score in the first half too. Manning took five corners and delivered two successful crosses from open play.

Manning didn’t have much defending to do as he made only three defensive contributions against his former side QPR. However, he was victorious in four of his six ground duels and made three recoveries as well (all stats via Fotmob).

The Saints star’s contributions now put him on one goal and three assists in 13 Championship games this term. He set up one goal in the 2-0 Carabao Cup victory over Colchester United at the start of the season too.

Southampton fans won’t have had many complaints when news of Manning’s new contract talks emerged. He has grown into an influential player under Eckert with his creative abilities from left-back making him a valuable asset.

His case for a new deal has only grown stronger with his performance from QPR though. The technical ability he offers makes the Saints such a threat from wide areas and set plays.

A new contract would be a justified reward for how Manning has grown at St. Mary’s. Like many, he struggled during their last stay in the Premier League in 2024/25, but he will be determined to earn another shot as Southampton battle for promotion from the Championship this season.

#2235. Martin O'Neill explains Jota omission before Falkirk clash

Martin O'Neill has explained his decision to leave Jota out of Celtic's matchday squad against Falkirk.

The Portuguese winger has only recently returned from long-term injury with an ACL problem and he has made four appearances since his comeback against Motherwell last month.

He was not named in the squad at all by the manager for this afternoon's test against the Bairns who are sitting sixth in the Scottish Premiership and in decent form of their own.

O'Neill, though, put all worries about a potential setback to bed as he revealed the playmaker has been left out due to the fact that Falkirk play their games on an astroturf pitch.

Asked on Sky Sports why the wide man is not involved and whether that may be something for punters to worry about, the Northern Irishman calmed those fears.

"No, he's just back from the injury and I think in terms of the pitch, we felt it's best with the type of injury he's recovering from, to leave him," he said.

Celtic found themselves a goal down to Ethan Ross' finish within the first three minutes of action. At the time of writing they remain 1-0 behind.

UDINESE. UFFICIALE L'ESONERO DI RUNJAIC: IL SOSTITUO È PAOLO ZANETTI. I DETTAGLI SUL CONTRATTO. JACOBO RAMON, IL REAL LO PUÒ RIACQUISTARE PER 9 MILIONI MA IL COMO SI GIOCA LE SUE CARTE: IL PUNTO. ISAKSEN MAI COSÌ DETERMINANTE: LA LAZIO DEVE BLINDARLO, A CHE PUNTO È IL RINNOVO. PER IL FUTURO PIACE IL GIOVANE ANTE SIMONIC. MILAN, OCCHI SU SYLLA PER LA DIFESA: IL CENTRALE DELL'UNION SG PIACE AI ROSSONERI

L’Udinese cambia. Il club friulano ha comunicato, tramite i suoi canali ufficiali, di aver sollevato Kosta Runjaic dalla guida tecnica della prima squadra. “Le strade del tecnico e dei bianconeri si separano dopo oltre due anni puntellati da obiettivi importanti raggiunti - si legge nel comunicato stampa ufficiale -. Il club ringrazia sentitamente Kosta e i suoi collaboratori Małecki e Trukan e augura loro le migliori fortune professionali”. Già deciso il successere, con Paolo Zanetti che ha firmato fino al 30 giugno 2027:

"Udinese Calcio è lieta di annunciare di aver affidato a Paolo Zanetti la guida tecnica della prima squadra. Ha firmato un contratto fino al 30 giugno 2027. Il nuovo allenatore dirigerà domani pomeriggio la prima seduta di allenamento. La conferenza stampa di presentazione si terrà mercoledì alle ore 15.00.

Jacobo Ramon è uno dei pezzi pregiati di questo Como, che sta sorprendendo tutti sia in campionato che in Champions League. In questa stagione sta confermando tutte le sue qualità. Il suo rendimento è sempre a livelli alti: in 10 presenze ha realizzato anche 2 gol. In Europa è sempre stato in campo, togliendosi anche la soddisfazione di segnare una rete nella vittoria interna per 4-1 contro il Manchester United. Insomma un’altra grande operazione in prospettiva del Como, che nel luglio del 2025 lo ha acquistato per 2,5 milioni di euro dal Real Madrid, che mantenuto però il 50% sulla futura rivendita. Il Como è consapevole che la sua enorme crescita ha scatenato una grande attenzione da parte di tanto club. In realtà l’unico vero grande pericolo viene proprio dalla casa madre, che al momento delle cessione ha inserito anche la clausola di recompra valida fino all’estate del 2028. Il Real ha già manifestato l’intenzione di riportarlo alla base per una cifra già fissata di 9 milioni di euro. Insomma la lunga partita con il Como è già cominciata nel senso che già una situazione simile si è verificata con Nico Paz e poi alla fine sappiamo come è andata. E magari anche con lui potrebbe accadere la stessa cosa. Un concetto tra l’altro espresso anche ieri nel pre-gara contro il Venezia da Cesc Fabregas. Ramon si gode intanto questo momento magico, sapendo che comunque vada ha il futuro assicurato. E la sensazione è che il Como possa giocarsi ancora le sue carte.

Un bellissimo gol e il cross da cui nasce il 2-1 di Andre Pinamonti: il volto sorridente dell'attaccante ha preso le copertine del successo della Lazio contro il Genoa, ma c'è tanto, tantissimo di Gustav Isaksen nel primo posto in solitaria dei biancocelesti. Siamo alla terza stagione italiana del danese, arrivato nell'estate 2023 nella Capitale italiana dal Midtjylland. E quello visto fino a qui è sicuramente il miglior Isaksen visto in maglia biancoceleste. Libero di testa, determinante e incisivo. Lo dimostrano prima di tutto i numeri: il suo record in una stagione in Serie A è di 5 gol, siglati lo scorso anno, con un assist all'attivo, in 30 giornate. Beh, con Gattuso è già a 4 gol e un assist in 10 partite. Ma come dicevamo per quanto riguarda il gol di Pinamonti, il suo apporto va oltre ai numeri in termini di gol e assist e infatti, dopo l'alternanza iniziale, Gattuso non lo leva più dal terzetto lì davanti. E ora l'attenzione si sposta anche sul suo contratto, che non è così lontano dallo scadere: l'attuale accordo arriva fino al 30 giugno 2028. Il club e l'entourage del giocatore sono già al lavoro per allungare la scadenza ed evitare altre telenovele come quelle recenti che hanno riguardato altri giocatori: si tratta per far firmare il ragazzo fino al 2030.

Se in classifica la Lazio vola, la società non vuole di certo farsi trovare impreparata sul mercato di gennaio, quando un paio di innesti potrebbero aiutare ulteriormente Gattuso a inseguire obiettivi impensabili fino a poche settimane fa. Gli scout biancocelesti nelle ultime settimane sono stati impegnati ad osservare il classe Ante Simovic, un difensore centrale croato classe 2009 dal profilo moderno e di grande prospettiva. Paragonato per caratteristiche tecniche a un giovane David Alaba, si distingue per l’ottimo piede sinistro, l’eccellente tecnica individuale e una velocità che gli permette di recuperare terreno con facilità. Dotato di grande personalità con la palla tra i piedi, ama avanzare e partecipare attivamente alla manovra, rendendolo un difensore dinamico e propositivo, capace di saltare la prima pressione con qualità.

Il Milan non sta sondando solo la pista che porta a Goncalo Inacio per la difesa e continua a monitorare anche altri profili, tra cui c'è quello di Massire Sylla, difensore centrale dell'Union Saint-Gilloise che ha un contratto in scadenza nel 2030 e a soli 21 anni sta dimostrando di poter calcare ben altri palcoscenici, vista la straordinaria continuità di rendimento avuto in Belgio fino a questo momento. A riportarlo è Matteo Moretto.

FENERBAHÇE, NON C'È ANCORA L'ACCORDO CON CONCEICAO PER LA PANCHINA. IL PUNTO DELLA SITUAZIONE. LIVERPOOL ALLA CACCIA DELL'EREDE DI VAN DIJK: ANCHE MURILLO E SCHLOTTERBECK NEL MIRINO. ARSENAL, RAYA SI CONFERMA SU ALTISSIMI LIVELLI: IL CLUB PRONTO AD ALLUNGARGLI IL CONTRATTO

Diversamente da quanto riferito dai media turchi lo sbarco di Sergio Conceiçao in Turchia non sembra essere imminente. Secondo quanto raccolto dalla redazione di Tuttomercatoweb.com infatti l'accordo fra il tecnico lusitano, reduce dall'addio all'Al-Ittihad in Arabia Saudita, non sarebbe ancora stato trovato nonostante i contatti recenti e una proposta già avanzata nei confronti dell'ex Milan. L'assenza di un accordo dunque fa slittare l'arrivo di Conceiçao a Istanbul con l'allenatore che non ha ancora prenotato alcun volo verso la Turchia e attende di capire se l'accordo si farà oppure se tutto è destinato a saltare nonostante quanto emerso nelle scorse ore. Contro il Liverpool in Champions League, nella giornata di mercoledì, dunque in panchina potrebbe andare ancora quel Dirk Kuyt che è stato nominato ad interim dopo le dimissioni di Kartal dall'incarico. Ricordiamo che gli altri nomi accostati al club turco in queste ore sono quelli di Julian Nagelsmann, Roberto Martinez, José Luis Mendilibar ed Ernesto Valverde.

Il Liverpool continua a cercare l’erede di Virgil van Dijk in vista della prossima stagione. Il centrale olandese infatti è in scadenza di contratto e finora non ha ricevuto alcuna proposta per rinnovare, il tutto fa dunque pensare a un addio a fine anno del classe ‘91 arrivato a Liverpool nel 2018. Secondo quanto riferito dai media inglesi il club starebbe monitorando attivamente soprattutto due profili: si tratta del brasiliano Murillo, classe 2002 legato al Nottingham Forest fino al 2030, e di Nico Schlotterbeck, classe ‘99 del Borussia Dortmund a cui è legato fino al 2031. Quest’ultimo in particolare sarebbe il giocatore su cui la dirigenza dei Reds punta maggiormente tanto che nelle prossime settimane potrebbero essere intensificati i contatti con i tedeschi e gli agenti dello stesso centrale difensivo. Nelle scorse settimane era emerso anche un forte interesse per Luka Vuskovic, classe 2007 arrivato la scorsa estate al Brighton dall’Amburgo. Il croato, che vanta già 10 presenze in nazionale maggiore, in questo avvio di stagione è sceso in campo già in 13 occasioni nelle varie competizioni attirando l’attenzione di diversi club che lo stanno monitorando con attenzione. Vuskovic potrebbe dunque diventare un obiettivo del Liverpool per la prossima estate anche se i Seagulls hanno già fatto sapere di poter aprire a una cessione solo di fronte a un’offerta da 100 milioni di sterline.

Nonostante nella nazionale spagnola venga dopo Unai Simon nelle gerarchie del ct De La Fuente, per l’Arsenal David Raya non è solo un titolare indiscusso, ma anche uno dei punti di forza che hanno portato i Gunners a vincere il titolo in Premier League e arrivare in finale di Champions League lo scorso anno. Anche quest’anno il portiere iberico è partito alla grande giocando su altissimi livelli tanto da spingere l’Arsenal a volerlo blindare ancora più strettamente a sé nonostante il desiderio, mai nascosto, del classe ‘95 di giocare ne LaLiga. Secondo quanto riferito da Football Insider il club londinese sarebbe infatti pronto ad allungare di un ulteriore anno il contratto di Raya in scadenza nel 2028. Un modo anche per allontanare le possibili sirene di mercato.

#2233. Cesar Peixoto must manage Wolves’ creative machine carefully with star potential emphasised in Cardiff City win

Wolves continued their improved run of form on Saturday as they defeated Cardiff City 3-0 at Molineux. The triumph made it 10 points from the last 12 available for Wanderers, continuing their fine response to back-to-back losses in the first two games after the September-October international break.

Cesar Peixoto‘s side were two up within 15 minutes thanks to goals from Fer Lopez and Adam Armstrong, Ladislav Krejci made it three just before the hour mark to really secure the points, heading home from a Kieran Tripper corner.

Alongside assisting the third goal, right-back Trippier was a standout creative threat for Wolves with the joint-most chances made at three – tied with Bluebirds winger Chris Willock. The 36-year-old and captain on the day showed why he has a key role to play at Molineux through his technical ability and leadership.

Trippier was Wolves’ leading creator on Saturday with his three opportunities made. He hugged the right-hand side for the vast majority of the match and saw a lot of the ball, with his 74 touches more than any other player for the Old Gold.

He completed 35 passes, 11 of which were into the final third and 14 of which were line-breaking. He made two accurate crosses too, showing how he mixed up his work in possession with deliveries into the box and others into spaces occupied by Lopez, Jean-Ricner Bellegarde and Armstrong.

Trippier did his defensive duties too, with 12 defensive contributions the joint-most in the game. He made four tackles, five clearances and three interceptions, so it was a very well-rounded display from the veteran right-back.

Creatively, his display saw the theme of his performances continue. Trippier currently ranks in the top 4% of Championship right-backs for successful passes (52.53), accurate long balls (4.35), line-breaking passes (16.39), chances created (3.01) and chances created (3.01) per 90 (all stats via Fotmob).

From deep areas on the right-hand side, Trippier is a major creative outlet and a go-to player in possession. This paired with his vast experience and leadership from a storied career to date make him a crucial asset for Wolves.

There are few doubts over what Trippier can contribute at Wolves. His past at the very top of club and international football means he provides a level of pedigree few in the Championship can offer, and he sets an example on and off the pitch as a vocal leader.

He’s a standout creatively too, serving as a key asset in possession and from set-pieces. Such traits mean that, in an ideal world, Trippier could play every minute of every match.

However, at 36 and with injury issues arising over his last two years at Newcastle United and early on this term, Peixoto faces the challenge of managing his workload. Trippier can not be expected to play every minute of a Championship season, so they must be careful not to demand too much of the right-back to limit the risk of injury.

It will be a tough balance to strike, but it is key to getting the best out of him all season. Trippier needs to be rotated with Jackson Tchatchoua to keep him fit and at the top of his game.

#2232. Celtic face key fixture shunting thanks to Rangers as precedent set

Celtic could be forced into a fixture reshuffle after Rangers booked their place in the Premier Sports Cup Final with victory over Aberdeen.

There is already a precedent for such a move. Last season, Rangers had to switch an Ibrox clash with Hibernian after Celtic's Hampden showdown with St Mirren was scheduled for the same day. The match was pushed back to the Monday evening, with Emmanuel Fernandez scoring the winner for the Gers.

A similar scenario is now looming for Martin O'Neill's side, who are due to host Hibs at Parkhead on Sunday, December 13, the same day as this season's Hampden showpiece.

While Hibs could still reach the final themselves if they beat Edinburgh rivals Hearts in the second semi-final, their Premiership trip to Glasgow looks almost certain to be moved should they fall short.

The SPFL and Police Scotland are traditionally reluctant to have Celtic and Rangers playing separate matches in Glasgow on the same afternoon, making a change the most likely outcome.

Celtic are unable to simply bring the fixture forward by 24 hours. The champions are in Europa League action away to Omonia Nicosia on the Thursday night before the scheduled league encounter.

That leaves Monday evening as one potential solution, mirroring the arrangement made for Rangers and Hibs last season.

However, officials could also decide to move the match to an entirely different date depending on fixture congestion and broadcast requirements.

For now, Celtic's schedule remains unchanged, but Rangers' victory over Aberdeen has left a major question mark hanging over Hibs' planned visit to Parkhead.

#2231. Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC

Tottenham Hotspur fans enjoyed their first glimpse of summer signings Andy Robertson and Sandro Tonali in the shirt, with both players scoring penalties in the shoot-out that followed a 1-1 draw with Sydney FC.

Spurs took the lead through a first-half Mathys Tel free-kick, before Roberto De Zerbi’s youthful defence was undone by Takahiro Sekine, who tucked away one of the Australian side’s only chances of the game.

Magic from Mathys Tel 🪄A brilliant free kick from the Frenchman gets @spursofficial off to a flyer, as the striker puts it top bins to take a 1-0 lead in SydneyWatch #TOTvSYD live and exclusive on Paramount+ 📺 pic.twitter.com/ntqTgleasJ

Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

Spurs win the shoot-out 4-2. That will be that.

Hoefsloot dives to his right and pushes Donley’s penalty around the post.

But then Dubravka saves from Popovic, and Spurs remain 3-2 up. Score the next one and they win the shoot-out.

Very similar placing to Tonali’s penalty. Does Dubravka have a save in him?

He doesn’t need to have one because Josh Lacey has hit the post. 3-2 to Spurs after three pens each.

Plenty of power and right into the side netting. No mistake from Spurs’s big money summer signing.

Dubravka then guesses the right way, but Toure finds the bottom left corner. 2-2.

The 17-year-old takes the mickey a little bit, dinking the ball straight down the middle. Spurs score their first penalty.

Then Popovic steps up and sends Dubravka the wrong way. 1-1.

Spurs were the game’s dominant force, but they did not convert that control into enough goals. No cause for alarm though, and no injuries from what we can tell. There will be some penalties on the way.

Williams-Barnett with a superb piece of control and turn forward, but the danger was snuffed out as he dribbled the ball into the penalty area. Then the youngster shoots from outside the box, deflected behind for a corner.

Andy Robertson has been impressive, and the goalkeeper makes a fingertip save to flick his low cross away from danger. Almost third time lucky for Yang who was waiting at the back post for a tap-in.

Andy Robertson's first outing as a Spurs player 🫡 pic.twitter.com/q5bdzQknJ2

Spurs controlling possession, pushing for the goal that would spare them having to take some penalties. As happens with this friendlies, the game has become more bitty since all the changes.

If the game finishes as a draw, there will be a penalty shoot-out. Donley has fizzed some crisp forward passes since coming on in midfield. Then Donley underlaps, picked out by Williams-Barnett but his low cross is straight at the goalkeeper.

Andy Robertson getting forward to good effect once again, standing up a cross for Yang in the middle but the substitute heads wide from seven or eight yards out.

Referee waves play on as Spurs pour forward and Robertson flashes a ball across the box, and the slight deflection was enough to put off Yang at the back post and he missed the target. Should have been a tap in.

Spurs close to a second, but Tonali’s shot from the edge of the box is pushed around the post. There was more good approach play from Williams-Barnett to tee up the Italian.

More Spurs changes: Andy Robertson is on, and takes the armband, he replaces Kyerematen. Up front, Richarlison and Solomon are off, replaced by Min-Hyeok and Dane Scarlett. Donley and Melia replace Gray and Gallagher in midfield.

A couple of appeals for a Spurs penalty after Kyerematen burst beyond the Sydney defence from left-back. He could have crossed sooner, but was tackled, and then there was a challenge on Richarlison. Referee waves it away.

Very youthful Spurs back four on the pitch now, which played a part in the nature of the equaliser they conceded. No Romero, Van de Ven, Van Hecke or Senesi available for selection today, but Andy Robertson is warming up on the touchline.

Spurs straight back into another long spell of possession, with Tonali winning a foul in midfield after a smooth turn forward.

A touch of ill fortunate for Spurs, the half-time substitute Takai inadvertently poked the ball through to Sekine who lifted the ball over Dubravka to equalise. Delicate finish, and Spurs are breached.

Conor Gallagher still closing down tirelessly, but he has been a little untidy with the ball at his feet. I suspect he was the bleep test winner in training. Sydney do well to play through the pressure and keep possession for a while.

Good industry from Tonali in midfield to regain possession, and Williams-Barnett shows real poise on the ball again. Easy to see why Spurs are excited about him.

Kyerematen defends well at the back post when it looked like Macallister was about to head at goal.

Then Spurs are away on the break, and Williams-Barnett skims the crossbar with a left-footed shot from a tight angle.

Three half-time Spurs changes: Tel, Bergvall and Davies off, Takai, Tonali and Williams-Barnett are on. Takai goes to centre-back with 17-year-old Williams-Barnett in an attacking midfield position.

A decent half’s work from Spurs, they look in a good place physically and their high pressing has caught the eye. Not quite clinical enough in the penalty area so far though, they have butchered some good chances.

Sydney have come to life as an attacking force, Spurs’s defence undone by a ball over the top. Dubravka caught in no-man’s-land, and Mac Allister poked the ball beyond him but did not generate enough power to score.

Cracking effort from the Sydney forward Macallister, trying to chip Dubravka from some 45 yards out. The goalkeeper was worried and scrambling, the effort misses the target.

Sydney looking ragged now, and Gallagher cracks a shot off the foot of the post from the edge of the box. Then Youlley takes on a shot from long range which is high, wide and handsome. Richarlison is then fouled by Popovic, dragging down the forward to stop a counter. Yellow card.

Conor Gallagher is charging forward at every opportunity, applying pressure on Sydney’s defenders whenever they have the ball. With no European football, Spurs can really lean into a high-octane approach this season.

Great take, right footed to the the goalkeeper’s side, and the strike was too powerful for Hoefsloot. A clean hit, and Spurs now lead. A well-deserved goal on the balance of play.

The game has slipped into a lull now, after a bright Spurs start. De Zerbi’s team do now have a free-kick at the edge of the D after Manor Solomon is fouled.

Tel amnd Gallagher threaten down the left for Spurs, with the midfielder finding the winger with a reverse pass. Tel’s cross is cleared.

Then Sydney muster their first shot of the game, Youlley with a strike from 25 yards out which Dubravka pushes away from danger.

Sydney FC starting to get their foot on the ball a little more now, but still no sign that they have capability to hurts Spurs going forward. Kyerematen is then fouled in the Sydney half.

Sydney are yet to have a touch in the Spurs penalty area, it has been one-way traffic so far. De Zerbi will be pleased with what he has watched so far, but no killer touch in the box as yet.

Conor Gallagher with a nice touch to win a free-kick near the left touchline. Sydney just about hanging on. The goalkeeper claims Tel’s cross from the free-kick.

Spurs’s closing down is choking Sydney’s build up play, and Gallagher wastes a good chance when free in the box. Shot blocked when there was time and space to pick his spot.

Lucas Bervall’s low cross is turned behind for a corner and Spurs remain in the ascendancy. Another threatening delivery, and Ben Davies may well have had a shout for a penalty, dragged to the turf by Grant. If this was a Premier League game, I’m sure VAR would have taken a close look at that.

Hoefsloot with a really poor pass from his six-yard box, straight into the path of Tel 25 yards out, but his side-footed effort was saved by the goalkeeper. Pitches like this make technical errors an inevitability.

Sydney’s goalkeeper Hoefsloot punches a corner clear under some pressure, attacking set-pieces were a rare positive for Spurs last season. The Premier League team are dominating possession in the early minutes.

Conor Gallagher and Richarlison leading an aggressive Tottenham press in the early exchanges. Tel enjoys plenty of touches down the left flank, but his inswinging cross from the left is headed clear. Rio Kyerematen is puhsing on from left-back.

After a rendition of Oh When The Saints Go Marching In on the trumpet, we are under way. A chance for Aussie Spurs fans to feel like they are in N17 for the evening.

The pitch looks slightly more lush than the surface Chelsea had to play on across town yesterday. The Allianz Stadium looks distinctly similar to the Etihad. Archie Gray captains Spurs.

No James Maddison in the squad for this game, perhaps still being managed physically after last year’s serious knee injury. Suspect we will see a more senior side picked for the friendly against Chelsea on Saturday.

The 21-year-old has a sweet left foot, on display when he scored this goal against Manchester City while on loan at Leyton Orient.

JAMIE DONLEY. THAT'S INCREDIBLE. 🤯The @SpursOfficial loanee with an incredible effort from distance that ends up in the net to give @leytonorientfc the opening goal against Manchester City 😱#EmiratesFACup pic.twitter.com/bHnKg92Q2y

Lucas Bergvall has been linked with a move away from Spurs, but he starts in midfield. No Fernandes in the squad at all. No summer signings in the starting line-up, but Tonali and Andy Robertson are on the bench.

Spurs starting XI: Dubravka; Kyerematen, Davies, Hardy, Tye Hall; Gray, Bergvall, Solomon, Gallagher, Tel; Richarlison

Subs: Kinsky, Robertson, Takai, Tingey, Byrne, Tyrese Hall, Russell-Denny, Donley, Tonali, Ajayi, Yang, Williams-Barnett, Scarlett

Spurs fans took their first look at summer signing Mateus Fernandes in a 2-0 victory over Auckland, and their pre-season tour continues today against Sydney FC.

Fernandes, an £85m purchase from West Ham United, also scored a stunning volley in a behind-closed-doors game against MK Dons.

Sandro Tonali is part of the travelling squad for these friendlies, as is new centre-back Jean Paul van Hecke. Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero and Pedro Porro have been given extra time off after their respective nations reached the World Cup final, won by Porro and Spain.

Van Hecke and Senesi ranked very highly among defenders for progressive passing, which offers an insight into the qualities Roberto De Zerbi is prioritising this summer.

The Italian likes his teams to bait opponents into pressing them high up the pitch, before moving the ball through central areas using third-man combinations and wall passes. The addition of two ball-playing centre-backs and two new central midfielders should mean Spurs can play like a recognisable De Zerbi team.

While Dane Scarlett and Richarlison scored against Auckland, Spurs’s squad still lacks high-class options in forward areas, with a move for Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi mooted earlier in the summer.

Spurs fans will be excited to watch 17-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett, the midfielder who is one of the outstanding players in his age group in the country.

“He’s a talent,” Ledley King said. “There’s a lot of hard work ahead of him, but there’s no doubt that he’s someone with great ability.

“He’s seen players like Harry Kane come through the academy and, through sheer hard work and determination, put themselves in a position to kick on. He couldn’t have a better role model.

“There’s no doubt we’re excited by his talent and the next part will be up to him.”

#2230. Kieran McKenna on West Ham’s three-man managerial shortlist as Nuno doubts grow

West Ham slipped to 8th in the Championship after defeat against West Brom on Saturday. WHUFC are currently in the play-off positions, but back-to-back losses to fellow promotion hopefuls have brought concerns.

Now, reporter Alan Nixon states that the Hammers have a three-man shortlist of potential targets if they decide to part ways with the under-fire Nuno Espirito Santo. Nixon says that Kieran McKenna, Rob Edwards and Scott Parker are all on the radar at the London Stadium.

All of the names mentioned are currently available, but it remains to be seen if the interest develops into anything concrete.

West Ham have some favourable fixtures coming up, with Cardiff City, Blackburn Rovers, Preston North End and Portsmouth all to play before the end of November. This run could be crucial for Nuno as pressure on his position grows.

Unlike Championship rivals Burnley, who have recently appointed Fabio Celestini, it appears West Ham are looking for experience in the division as they weigh up potential Nuno replacements.

It may be hard to persuade McKenna to return to the second tier, however, Parker and Edwards may be tempted by the opportunity.

Parker has gained promotion from the Championship with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley. He operated with possession-based football and defensive organisation within his ranks. However, his time at each club ended on a sour note in the Premier League with relegation campaigns.

Edwards has also gained promotion from the division with Luton Town, whilst showing positive signs at the likes of Middlesbrough. He deploys his sides with a compact, high-energy system, putting an emphasis on pressing and attacking width.

McKenna meanwhile has only managed Ipswich Town, taking them from League One to the Premier League. He left the club earlier this year, but the Tractor Boys would still be owed a sizeable compensation fee.

Although Parker has multiple promotions on his CV, a move for the Englishman may be a risk. He might take West Ham out of the Championship, but his spells at other clubs has indicated that he may not be able to keep them in the Premier League if they return.

McKenna would be a very exciting appointment for West Ham, however it would be a surprise to see him drop to the Championship again. He is the most attractive target of the three, but the most unlikely.

Edwards, may be a more feasible appointment though. He’s proven his promotion pedigree in the Championship and takes pride two things WHUFC are currently lacking: defensive organisation and battling spirit.

Time will tell if Nuno can turn the tide, but the Hammers are seemingly prepared if they do opt for change.

#2229. Chris Sutton skewers 'pathetic' Celtic star as big money signing called out

Unimpressed Chris Sutton branded Haissem Hassan's defending "pathetic" after the Premiership champions fell apart in a 2-0 defeat to Falkirk.

The Parkhead icon has long been a supporter of the Egypt international's attacking threat, but he could not hide his frustration at the winger's lack of effort tracking back.

Hassan, bought for £6m in a deal which includes £3m in add-ons, was hooked in the 84th minute after an afternoon full of near misses. Goals from Ethan Ross and Scott Tanser in the first half secured a famous victory for the Bairns over the Premiership champions.

The latest setback means Martin O'Neill's struggling side have managed just three wins from their last 10 games.

Read more: Celtic face key fixture shunting thanks to Rangers as precedent set

And it was Hassan who found himself firmly in Sutton's firing line, with the former Celtic striker making his feelings clear while on commentary duty for Sky Sports. O'Neill admitted on Friday that Hassan's defensive game needed added work.

Sutton said: "Absolutely pathetic from Hassan on a couple of occasions. He doesn't want to defend.

"You thought Celtic would come out in the second half and play with purpose, but they're being bullied by Falkirk."

#2228. Celtic fall to Falkirk defeat as Scott Bain shines for Bairns

Celtic paid the price for a sloppy start and a superb display from former goalkeeper Scott Bain as they fell to a 2-0 defeat at Falkirk.

Ethan Ross netted in the third minute after a mistake by Cameron Carter-Vickers and Scott Tanser put Falkirk two ahead in the 38th minute.

Bain made 10 saves as Martin O’Neill’s side endured an afternoon of frustration and suffered a sixth defeat in 10 matches.

The champions remain four points clear at the top of the William Hill Premiership but have now played a game more than second-placed Rangers.

Falkirk moved up to fourth in the table after their fourth consecutive victory and their first over Celtic since 2007.

Read more: Celtic face key fixture shunting thanks to Rangers as precedent set

Carter-Vickers returned to the starting line-up after injury, while Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain was handed his first start in two months. Winger Haissem Hassan was recalled.

Kasper Hogh might have fancied himself to end his barren run on Falkirk’s synthetic pitch given most of his career goals have come on artificial surfaces, but the former Bodo/Glimt striker was dropped as Camilo Duran led the line.

The Danish striker came on for the final 25 minutes but was barely involved as he went 14 games without a goal.

Falkirk got an early lift after the Celtic central defence failed to deal with a long ball.

The hosts worked the ball out to Ryan Strain, whose cross was knocked into the path of Ross by Carter-Vickers. The wide player lapped up the chance.

The goal came at a cost as Strain injured himself while crossing. Jack McMillan was a natural replacement at right-back.

Both sides made opportunities in the first half.

On-loan Derby winger Owen Eames was a hive of creativity on Falkirk’s left wing and helped set up two half chances for Jacob Murrell, who could not make the most of them.

The 19-year-old wide player set up the second goal as left-back Tanser ran on to his infield pass before slotting past Sam Johnstone.

Duran hit a post after getting in behind and Celtic were kept out by a string of excellent first-half stops from Bain, who denied the Colombian three times and also foiled Hassan with a diving save.

Falkirk were almost out of sight early in the second half when Murrell bundled the ball over the line after Celtic failed to deal with a long throw, but the ball had hit the American’s hand when it bounced off a post before going in off the striker’s waist and the goal was disallowed by VAR.

O’Neill had brought on James Forrest for Callum Osmand at half-time and the winger forced Bain’s first save of the half before Callum McGregor, Kieran Tierney and Hassan missed the target from inside the box.

O’Neill turned to Hogh and Benjamin Nygren as Duran and Oxlade-Chamberlain made way.

But Bain quickly pulled off a brilliant double save from Forrest and Nygren to spark chants of ‘Scotland’s number one’.

The former Celtic goalkeeper soon denied Forrest again before Nygren was thwarted by a diving block from Finn Yeats.

It grew increasingly clear that Celtic were never going to score as Liam Scales headed over and Bain saved long-range efforts from Nygren and Mika Baur.

#2227. Middlesbrough should be optimistic about 21-year-old’s future amid bright loan stint for struggling League One side

Middlesbrough have built a squad that is readily challenging for promotion to the Premier League. Boro currently sit top of the Championship and have responded well to their play-off final defeat last season.

As a result of their big spending in the summer, several loans were sanctioned for players whose game time would be questionable. Out of the three departing for the campaign, Finley Munroe is the player for Kim Hellberg to monitor closely.

Middlesbrough signed the 21-year-old from Aston Villa in January 2026 after impressing on loan at Swindon Town. Now with his move to Blackpool almost three months in, Boro’s prospect is finding some success at Bloomfield Road.

Munroe has made a step-up this season despite being sent out on loan by Middlesbrough. Last campaign, the 21-year-old was playing in League Two and now he is playing in the third tier.

Despite just five starts in the league for Blackpool so far, the left-back has made a good account of himself. The youngster has made eight successful dribbles and won 57 duels. He has just featured at left-back in League One action, and his tenacity is evident with 31 tackles made.

He has been on the bench for the Tangerines’ last three outings, but he has done well to compete with Ilmari Niskanen for a starting XI spot. Munroe’s best display for his loan club came in a 2-2 draw with Bromley back in September.

The 21-year-old grabbed an assist and won 86% of his ground duels. While the Middlesbrough prospect may not have featured as much as they would’ve liked, there has certainly been many positives to take from his stint away from the Riverside.

Middlesbrough currently have two senior left-backs at the club with Neto Borges and Alex Bangura. The former has been Hellberg’s go-to option as the Brazilian has appeared in all 13 league games this season.

His performances have been quality too, with 131 line-breaking passes made and 16 chances created. Defensively, the 30-year-old has been astute too. He has made 50 recoveries and blocked seven shots.

Munroe’s first-team chances are slimmer next season if Borges remains and certainly so if they achieve promotion to the Premier League. That being said, the Brazilian could be a perfect role model for the 21-year-old to learn from, and a position off the bench could be necessary for the youngster.

With the youngster’s ability to play further forward on the left wing too, it does improve his chances of breaking into the first team. However, for his development’s sake, Boro must identify his natural position and work on strengthening him in that specific area.

Possession: Chelsea 46%-54% TottenhamShots: 14-7Shots on target: 4-4Corners: 1-1

There is the final whistle and the 10 men of Tottenham snatch victory at the death with Richarlison scoring with seconds remaining.

In the final few seconds of the game, 10-man Tottenham win it. Donley’s shot from just outside the box hits the post and Richarlison follows up to score. It would have been a close call on offside if VAR was in use but it is not and Tottenham will take victory in Sydney.

Tottenham are being forced into a late change as Kyerematen, who come on for Robertson and nearly scored that wonder solo goal, is being forced off injured and is replaced by Tingey.

Delap is found in the centre of the Tottenham box with a cross from the right but the striker’s header from around the penalty spot goes wide and does not really trouble the target.

Initially, after Danso’s red card, Chelsea were in the ascendancy with a man advantage but Tottenham have dealt pretty well down a man.

Kyerematen nearly scores a quite sensational solo goal from inside his own half before driving forward. As he approaches the Chelsea penalty area, he tries to pick out the top corner and his effort comes off the top of the bar.

Xabi Alonso is making seven changes, yes seven, at once! That includes the likes of Delap and Tosin, who takes the captain’s armband.

The changes keep coming as Williams-Barnett replaces Tel for Tottenham.

A reminder that if the game is level after 90 minutes there will be a penalty shoot-out.

Roberto de Zerbi is making a double substitution as Tye Hall and Kyerematen replace Bergvall and Robertson.

17-year-old Satpaev, who hails from Kazakhstan, is replacing Estevao for Chelsea. Satpaev, who was at Kairat and turns 18 in 11 day’s time, scored the other day for Chelsea against Western Sydney.

Moore, who was on loan at Rangers last season, is replacing Solomon for Tottenham.

Robertson is so, so lucky. He is under no pressure as a cross comes over from the left and he should clear it with ease. However, he tries to be too clever and chests it back looking for his goalkeeper. There is not enough on it, allowing Pedro to nip in but his effort from inside the six-yard box is saved. Pedro probably should have scored and Robertson is a relieved man. Kinsky at the moment is the reason why Tottenham are not a couple of goals behind.

Tottenham have found it tough to get forward a lot since Danso’s red card but they do counter now and it ends with Tonali having a shot from just outside the box but his effort is easily saved by Sharman-Lowe.

Chelsea make a change as Anselmino comes on for Hato.

Palmer plays a ball down the right channel to pick out the run in behind of Palestra, who then returns it back to Palmer inside the Tottenham penalty area. Palmer’s first-time effort from the edge of the box is blocked.

Kinsky makes another big save to deny Chelsea. Tonali, who thought he had been fouled, loses the ball deep inside his own half, before Estevao has a great chance to put Chelsea in front from inside the Tottenham penalty area but Kinsky makes the save. It would have been a touch soft to give a free-kick to Tottenham but in the Premier League you suspect Tonali would have been awarded a free-kick there.

Tottenham are going to make a change at the back in light of Danso’s red card. Hardy is going to come on for Gallagher, who is booed by some of the Chelsea fans inside Accor Stadium. The England Under-18 international Hardy has come on at right centre-back in place of Danso.

Chelsea hit the frame of the goal. Pedro cuts it back from the byline to the penalty spot. Estevao gets to it first and his shot takes a deflection off Robertson. Kinsky makes a brilliant reflex save to push it onto the bar before Colwill blazes over.

Roberto de Zerbi is slumped in his seat distinctly unimpressed, shaking his head in frustration and perhaps disgust.

Palmer takes the free-kick but his effort is always curling wide of the far post.

The Austrian defender came on at half-time but has lasted just three minutes before being given his marching orders. Danso makes an absolute mess of a pass back to him from Gray and lets the ball run past him. Pedro gets around him and looks destined to drive towards the Tottenham penalty area but is brought down. Danso is shown a red card as Davies was probably not going to get across in time and it was the denial of a goal-scoring opportunity. Why do that in a pre-season friendly? Stupid.

Tottenham are making two changes at the break as Richarlison and Danso come on for Solanke and Van Hecke. Chelsea have also made a substitution as 16-year-old Nicoll-Jazuli comes on.

It appears the more times you see the incident involving Wesley Fofana and Conor Gallagher right at the end of the first half the more it looks like a penalty. Fofana did not appear to get the ball and instead catches Gallagher so Tottenham can probably feel a little aggrieved not to be given a penalty.

What have you made of that first half? Remember you can share your thoughts and opinions in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Possession: Chelsea 31%-69% TottenhamShots: 3-3Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 0-1

The first half is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break in Sydney.

Should Tottenham have been awarded a penalty? Robertson whips the ball in from the left to pick out the run of Gallagher into the box. Gallagher appeared to get to the ball ahead of Fofana, who seemingly then took Gallagher out but the referee does not point to the spot. That was a risky challenge to say the least from Fofana and on first viewing probably should have result in a penalty.

Palmer plays the ball forward to pick out the run in behind of Pedro, who has a two-on-one with Kinsky but the offside flag quickly goes up. Pedro was miles offside.

That was a decent opportunity for Tottenham. Tel finds the underlapping Davies with a pass towards the byline and the latter plays it across the six-yard box but Solanke was not there to meet it. Had Solanke read that, it would have been a simple tap-in.

Tel comes close to putting Tottenham back in front. It would have been a great solo goal as he drives inside from the left wing and moves into the Chelsea penalty area. He gets the better of Essugo on the corner of the six-yard box but is denied by a decent save from Sharman-Lowe.

Pedro has a chance to put Chelsea in front but his effort goes wide. Chelsea steal possession inside the Tottenham half after a poor pass from Robertson and the ball is then played forward to Pedro, who shoots from just inside the Tottenham box but his effort goes wide of the far post. Davies did just enough to put Pedro off.

Tottenham have two penalty appeals in quick succession turned down. First was for a potential handball by Essugo and then a push by Palestra on Tel. The handball would have been very harsh and the second incident was never a foul on Tel, who was losing his balance anyway.

Chelsea gift possession away deep inside their own half and Tel’s eyes light up. The ball rolls across to the Frenchman in a central position just outside the box and he opens up his body, trying to curl one into the top corner, but gets his first-time effort all wrong and his shot misses the target by a mile.

Like London buses, two goals come in quick succession and Chelsea are back on level terms. Chelsea counter from deep inside their own half and the ball ends up with Gittens on the left. From the corner of the box, he crosses towards the far post. It takes a touch off a Tottenham defender and ends up at the back post where Estevao, one of the smallest men on the pitch, beats Robertson and heads into the opposite corner.

Tottenham take the lead in Sydney courtesy of £100m signing Tonali. Solomon lays it back to Tonali who, from just outside the box, hits it first time and his shot takes a big deflection off Colwill, taking it into the far corner and giving Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal no chance. That was probably Tottenham’s first proper foray forward in the game.

It has been a pretty stop-start game as play continues to be halted by fouls. The two managers might enjoy seeing the passion of their teams but they will also want to see their sides actually play, which is quite difficult when fouls are being committed left, right and centre.

Van Hecke has already fouled his former teammate Pedro once and he bundles into him again. Van Hecke has a wry smile as he walks away and Pedro tells the referee that is now twice he has been fouled by Van Hecke. I think it is a fairly safe assumption that Van Hecke and Pedro do not like each other that much!

We are not even 10 minutes into this friendly but there is absolutely no love lost between these two sides and the challenges are flying in. Former Chelsea man Gallagher slides in on Essugo, which infuriates the Chelsea players. The referee takes his time to make his decision as both sides come to blows before giving out the first booking of the game to Gallagher.

Pedro is caught by Van Hecke out on Chelsea left and the latter is absolutely furious with that decision, believing he got the ball. However, replays show that he did not get the ball and a free-kick was the right decision. Those two were teammates at Brighton and supposedly were involved in a training ground altercation just over a year ago!

The free-kick is whipped in towards the back post and the last touch is deemed to have come off Chelsea, much to their chagrin.

Lavia catches Tonali late and eventually the referee blows his whistle to bring play back for the free-kick. In a Premier League game, that may well have been a booking for Lavia. It might be a pre-season game but there will be no love lost between these bitter rivals.

The pitch in Sydney is on the bobbly side, which will make slick passing more challenging, dare I say it probably not really possible or realistic.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, with Tottenham led out by Archie Gray and Chelsea by Levi Colwill. There is a lights show inside Accor Stadium as the teams making their way onto the pitch.

Tottenham: Kinsky, Robertson, Van Hecke, Gallagher, Tel, Gray, Bergvall, Tonali, Solanke, Solomon, Davies.Substitutes: Danso, Richarlison, Takai, Dubravka, Donley, Scarlett, Moore, Tyrese Hall, Russell-Denny, Melia, Kyerematen, Yang, Ajayi, Hardy, Williams-Barnett, Byrne, Tingey, Tye Hall.

I went on holiday and I was thinking ‘where do I go next?’ I kept checking when I was back in. To be fair, I got bored in the sixth week. Mykhailo Mudryk, the Chelsea winger, has been cleared to return to competitive football with immediate effect after the anti-doping case against him was resolved.

Mudryk has not played for Chelsea since November 2024 after he tested positive for meldonium, a banned substance.

The Ukrainian has consistently insisted that he never knowingly used the substance and that he did not understand how it had entered his system.

Chelsea have avoided a points deduction for making off-the-books payments during the Roman Abramovich era, but have been fined £10m and given a suspended two-window ban on signing players.

Chelsea’s punishment follows an investigation into 74 alleged breaches of the Football Association’s regulations regarding agent, intermediary and third-party payments.

It has now been revealed that Chelsea were initially punished with a six-point deduction, suspended until June 2027, but successfully appealed against that sanction.

It is a Premier League encounter Down Under as Chelsea take on Tottenham at the 82,000-capacity Accor Stadium in Sydney. Chelsea won both meetings in the league last season, winning 1-0 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium before a 2-1 victory at Stamford Bridge in the final few weeks of last season.

It is the start of a new era at Chelsea, with former Bayer Leverkusen and Real Madrid midfielder Xabi Alonso taking over. They began their tour down under with a crazy 6-4 win over Sydney Wanderers, with Joao Pedro scoring a hat-trick. Chelsea have broken the British transfer record to bring in Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa. Rogers is not on this tour as he enjoys time off following England’s World Cup exploits, with the likes of Reece James, Enzo Fernandez and Malo Gusto also not involved.

It has been a busy week for the club off the pitch as they secured the signing of French centre-back from Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace and are closing in on deals for both Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson. Chelsea’s opening game of the new Premier League season will be a west London derby as they travel to Craven Cottage to take on Fulham.

Tottenham have already played two games on their tour down under. A 2-0 win over Auckland FC in New Zealand was followed up by a 1-1 draw against Sydney FC on Wednesday. Tottenham have been very active in the transfer market this summer. In particular they have targeted Premier League players including Andy Robertson, Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke. Mohammed Kudus, Xavi Simons, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert have remained in the UK as they continue their rehabilitation from injuries.

Goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario has also stayed at home with a minor knock but the Italian has been linked with a move away from Tottenham this summer. Djed Spencer, Pedro Porro and Cristian Romero are not on the tour following their World Cup exploits. They begin their Premier League campaign with a London derby as they take on Brentford at the Gtech on the opening weekend.

#2225. Journalist takes brutal dig at Chelsea player after one incident which highly amused Van Dijk

One journalist was far from impressed with the antics of Chelsea defender Malo Gusto in his team’s Carabao Cup clash against Liverpool at Anfield on Wednesday night.

Early in the second half, the 23-year-old received the merest of contact from Virgil van Dijk and threw himself to the ground in apparent agony, clutching his leg in melodramatic fashion while the Reds captain simply looked at him with a face of bemusement.

A couple of minutes later, the Blues left-back was gently nudged by Bradley Barcola in front of the Kenny Dalglish Stand and again fell to the turf dramatically, even removing his boot and waving it at the assistant referee to try and dupe him into thinking that he’d been grievously harmed.

After the first of those rather amusing incidents, Liverpool Echo reporter Ian Doyle took to X with a rather sardonic verdict on the coming together between the Chelsea defender and the LFC skipper.

The journalist posted with tongue firmly in cheek: ‘Gusto is down after an altercation with Van Dijk and may now have to retire from the sport’.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

We just hope that the Chelsea left-back watches those two incidents and is shamed into cleaning up his act, with his amateur theatrics not painting him in a positive light whatsoever.

The way in which he threw himself to the ground after the mildest of contact from Van Dijk and Barcola was embarrassing, as was his waving of his boot towards the assistant referee.

That’s not the kind of behaviour that we want to see from any player on a football pitch, no matter what team’s colours they’re wearing, and Xabi Alonso should pull him aside and reprimand him over it.

We can only imagine how melodramatic Gusto would’ve been if a Liverpool player had shoved him in the same way that Emmanuel Emegha did to Van Dijk later in the second half.

For his own sake, we’d implore the 23-year-old to refrain from such needless play-acting in the future.

#2224. How Dave Challinor’s strongest Sheffield Wednesday XI will look as new boss gets to work

Sheffield Wednesday confirmed Dave Challinor’s appointment as first-team manager over the weekend, and after watching the 1-1 draw with Blackpool from the stands, he starts his work now.

The former Stockport County boss is tasked with leading SWFC back to the Championship as they rebuild after relegation and administration. He has a strong squad at his disposal, and the pressure is on to succeed where the departed Henrik Pedersen failed.

One of the first challenges Challinor faces is to identify his strongest and favoured starting XI. His squad is brimming with talent and boasts depth in all areas, so there is strong competition for a place in the plans of the new manager.

Lumley; Bernard, Cooper, Weaver; Valery, Mitchell, Slattery, M. Lowe; Barry, Keillor-Dunn; Burstow

The Owls’ summer rebuild means they have good squad depth across the board, so Challinor will be able to tinker with his setup as he works out the best XI. However, there will be a familiar feel to the setup, as the 51-year-old’s preferred formation has been 3-4-2-1 over the course of his career.

This setup was Pedersen’s go-to last season, although he occasionally switched to a 3-1-4-2 or 3-5-2 at times. Danny Rohl also used a 3-4-2-1 during his tenure, but like Pedersen, he switched to a 4-2-3-1 – which Challinor has deployed too – later in his reign.

As for the personnel, Joe Lumley will be backed to reclaim his starting spot from Ashley Maynard-Brewer when fit.

The centre-back positions will be a point of contention, with all of Di’Shon Bernard, Liam Cooper, Ernie Weaver, Ricardo Santos, Sil Swinkels, Gabriel Otegbayo and the versatile Max Lowe to pick from. All of those players could feasibly start, but Bernard has been a Championship standout at his best, Cooper provides leadership, experience and a left-footed presence for balance, and Weaver has the highest ceiling of the lot.

Yan Valery seems a shoo-in for Challinor’s right wing-back spot, and Lowe should be favoured on the left.

In the middle, Callum Slattery could emerge as Billy Mitchell’s regular partner with Barry Bannan enduring a tricky start to the campaign. This is another area where competition is strong, with all of Bannan, Jaden Heskey and Jarvis Thornton up for consideration while Tyler Onyango recovers from his ACL injury.

In the two roles behind the striker, Davis Keillor-Dunn is emerging as an influential player, and Louie Barry will be backed to land a key role when fit given his past success under Challinor. Slattery could also play in one of these advanced roles.

Up top, Mason Burstow could get the nod over top scorer Jamal Lowe. Again, there is strong depth here with Harry Gray, Ali Al-Hamadi, Will Grainger and Keillor-Dunn all capable of playing at striker.

The 3-4-2-1 has been Challinor’s go-to, but a 3-5-2 at Sheffield Wednesday could see Barry start as a striker with a midfield three of Mitchell, Slattery and Heskey or Bannan.

A 4-2-3-1 would facilitate a similar midfield, while a centre-back drops out. The depth in the SWFC squad means Challinor is spoiled for choice as he works out his best lineup.

Challinor has plenty of experience now, but this is a new task for him. With the greatest respect to his previous jobs, Sheffield Wednesday are a different beast in terms of club stature and expectation.

At Stockport County and AFC Fylde, he built them into teams that were truly his, and they grew over time. At Hillsborough, he faces the task of getting the most out of a group with big names and personalities. It will be a test of his abilities as both a coach and man manager.

Challinor’s record is excellent, but this is the biggest challenge he has faced in his managerial career to date.

#2223. VIP pundits rip Celtic to shreds as major next manager claim goes public

Celtic's shock defeat to Falkirk has sparked a blistering backlash from some of Scottish football's biggest names, with Martin O'Neill's leadership, team selection and transfer planning all coming under fierce scrutiny. Kris Boyd insists serious questions now have to be asked of the under-pressure boss and even fears the Parkhead hierarchy lack a clear succession plan should they decide to make a change. Chris Sutton has branded Celtic's current set-up a mess, from goalkeeping concerns to midfield shortcomings, while claiming O'Neill's starting XI has become impossible to predict. Pat Bonner also voiced concerns over whether every member of the squad is capable of meeting the demands expected at Celtic.

"The midfield is really vulnerable, but it's not just in the midfield.

"The goalkeeping situation is a mess. Sam Johnstone doesn't really excite and inspire me, and I think he's going to be safe.

"You've got Liam Scales dribbling out from the back thinking he's Baresi - he's not. The lack in midfield athletically and physically.

"Then you sign two strikers, but you can't play them together. Why not? Because you can't play 4-4-2 because the midfielders aren't athletic enough to do that and he doesn't want to play a back three.

"Martin needs to be forthright in how he wants to play and stick to one thing. It's a lottery waiting for the Celtic team, who knows what team Martin is going to pick?"

"Overall if you look at Celtic right now, where are they going? If you're operating as a top football club, you should already have a list of who your next managers are.

"Celtic haven't a clue what they're doing... the hierarchy will say, 'we're still successful, we're still winning', but eventually it catches up with you if you don't have a plan in place."

"Celtic have got a team that if they're all functioning - as we saw against Hearts - they can still cause problems for every team in the league. But they're not functioning properly.

"There are other managers under severe pressure. There has to be serious questions asked about Martin [O'Neill] now. Last season is over now... and right now, for Celtic to have lost six in the last ten in all competitions still isn't good enough. They're miles off it."

"It was a terrific display from Falkirk defensively. They had much more penetration than Celtic, who just go from side to side. Scott Bain was unbelievable. Absolutely unbelievable. I counted eight saves he made.

"Falkirk deserve it. They've got a terrific young team. John McGlynn has done a great job with them. But there are big question marks over whether or not these players are good enough for Celtic."
