#2222. Julien Stephan confirms ‘long-term injury’ for QPR forward ahead of Burnley clash

QPR were beaten 4-1 by Southampton on Saturday, and the result wasn’t the only dampener on a tough day at the office for the Hoops. After being introduced as a second-half substitute, forward Alfie Lloyd hobbled off through injury.

Now, speaking to West London Sport ahead of Tuesday’s tie against Burnley, R’s boss Julien Stephan revealed the 23-year-old looks set for an extended spell on the sidelines. Lloyd is set to be out for two months, likely keeping him sidelined until 2027.

“It’s a long-term injury,” Stephan said. “It will probably be difficult for him to come back before the end of the year.”

Jake Clarke-Salter is also expected to miss the Burnley tie, though his issue is undisclosed at present. Nicolas Madsen, Rumarn Burrell and Tariq Lamptey are on course for returns right after the November international break, and Ilias Chair is set to be eased back in with more substitute appearances after his return on Saturday.

Stephan does not have the biggest of squads at QPR, but he has good depth in all positions. That has been put to the test in the first quarter of the campaign, especially in attack.

Lloyd offers his services across the front three, and his versatility has helped deal with a shortage of options. Up top, all of Richard Kone, Justin Obikwu, Burrell and now Lloyd have had time on the sidelines, while Rayan Kolli was omitted too.

On the wings, Karamoko Dembele is still working back to full fitness after his ACL injury. Chair and Koki Saito, have had their issues as well, so it has been a heavily impacted area.

Stephan’s options have replenished over recent weeks, but Lloyd now drops out to leave the boss without a flexible forward and a strong physical profile. It will be hoped he can recover swiftly to return as soon and as safely as possible.

Lloyd’s long-term absence serves as a blow, but QPR do have the players to deal with the blow.

Stephan could recall one of Leon Scarlett or Justin Obikwu to the bench to cover. Kone will be backed to hold onto his starting berth having netted again in the Southampton loss.

Burnley have conceded 25 times in 13 games this season, and that record is something the Hoops will be ready to target. They have scored nine goals in their last two matches at Loftus Road, and they have the attacking style and talent to find a similar level of success against the Clarets.

#2221. City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier  League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

Rayan Ait-Nouri misses! Spooned over the bar.

Ait-Nouri is offside as he takes the ball on the left wing, and Inter have it back briefly.

McAidoo, yet again. A shot to the far post, yet again. A miss, yet again. He looks dangerous though.

Foden commits his own foul in midfield, this time on Mkhitaryan. There are a few minutes left before half-time, at which point we may see a few changes from both sides given the early stage of pre-season.

Foden swings in a corner that Savinho briefly keeps alive before Diouf clears, and Dimarco cannot quite reach the ball before it’s played back to Donnarumma.

Barella fouls Reijnders in midfield, but it’s nothing vicious.

Mkhitaryan continues to find space in pockets on the left. In general, Inter are finding it very easy to trundle to the edge of the City box.

Inter are keeping the ball calmly at the back, finding spaces between the pressing City attackers.

They break through and Donnarumma beats away a low shot from Stankovic.

Benjmain Pavard scores! Manchester City fail to clear their lines and Pavard, who started the move, is on hope to finish with the keeper stricken.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester City and Inter Milan.

The two sides meet  at Kai Tak Sports Park, Hong  Kong as their pre-season work kicks up a gear ahead of the new campaign.

City are still getting used to life without Pep Guardiola, the coach who left after a decade of high spending and high performance.

In his place is Enzo Maresca, who is not shy with the chequebook himself.

Ayyoub Bouaddi, the outstanding 18-year-old Moroccan international, should soon arrive from Lille when a fee is agreed, but Elliot Anderson and Jeremy Monga have already been signed.

City were runners-up last season, so Maresca is under pressure not just to keep things going without Guardiola, but to get the team back to the top of English football. That looks to be a tough prospect with Arsenal likely to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle in the coming days.

Inter, meanwhile, have swooped to pick up John Stones on a free transfer after his contract ended at the Etihad Stadium, and he is joined by Manuel Akanji, another former City centre-back whose loan turned permanent in the summer.

Inter won Serie A last season under head coach Cristian Chivu, and they are still one of the best sides in Europe.

While this friendly is likely to be played at a reduced pace, and will be disrupted by rustiness and substitutes, we could still learn a lot about both sides going into the new campaign, and there may be the odd surprise thrown up by a young player looking to stake a claim ahead of his senior colleagues this year.

#2220. EFL club consider building new 15,000-seater stadium on old Airport site

Cambridge United have played their football at the Abbey Stadium since the venue opened in 1932 - but could they be making their move away to pastures new in the near future?

The U's were founded 20 years before the opening of the stadium they currently play at, with a number of pitches around the city used before the building of what is now a 7,937-capacity home.

Cambridge will soon celebrate 100 years in the Abbey Stadium in five-and-a-half years time - but will they still be there in 2032?

United are on an upward trajectory under Neil Harris, and have started life in League One rather well since promotion earlier in the year.

With an average of over 7,000 fans attending home matches, there may be the need to expand the capacity beyond what the Abbey Stadium currently holds - but it's not going to be possible at the current location.

The Abbey Stadium is tightly packed into a small location, and there's several road blocks on each side of the ground that means expansion is limited, including a lake, houses, allotments and an A-road.

It means that a different site away from their current venue would need to be found if a new stadium is going to be financially viable - have they found one already though?

As per a report from the BBC, Cambridge are already looking into future alternatives for a 15,000-capacity stadium, with a site on the soon-to-be closed Cambridge Airport a possibility.

The club have confirmed that discussions have begun with a local developer over a potential move to the site, which is based on the outskirts of the city, just like the Abbey Stadium is, with the two locations only one mile apart.

Collect every point to win the round. Don’t let Neil Warnock catch you.

Arrow keys or WASD to move. P to pause, M to mute.

Swipe on the pitch or use the pad to move.

The vast area is set to be up for grabs though, with Cambridge Airport scheduled for full closure in 2029, having closed to public passenger flights 10 years ago.

United are 'exploring the feasability of the site for now', with that work expected to go on until Easter 2027, but any new stadium won't be rushed, with club chairman Godric Smith saying that he expected them to remain at the Abbey Stadium for at least another decade.

The Hill Group - who bought Cambridge Airport and its adjacent land in June - are keen to build a new stadium on their premises though, with the potential to also build 10,000 new homes and a new railway station too.

As a prestigious university city, Cambridge has a bit of untapped potential when it comes to trying to recruit new fans, and there's also a decent enough catchment area to try and bring new faces to watch the club.

At the Abbey Stadium though, new growth will be limited thanks to the lack of expansion on offer for the facilities, but a brand, spanking new complex not far from the original would certainly go down a treat.

Which sets of EFL fans have the most misery induced by their clubs?

It would of course cost a significant amount of money to come to fruition, with AFC Wimbledon's Plough Lane complex costing £34 million to construct, and that only has a capacity of just over 9,000.

Given they're close to maxing out their capacity already at the Abbey Stadium, there won't be that much growth in the next decade, where they intend to stay at their current home, but in 10 years time, they could be ready to move into a new home, and perhaps Championship ambitions can be realised.

#2219. Tony Mowbray confirms early Blackburn Rovers winter transfer hope with key position targeted

Blackburn Rovers have had a strong first quarter of the 2026/27 campaign, despite a challenging summer. Many at Ewood Park felt more was needed in the transfer window as only three new players signed, and now eyes are already on January.

Speaking to the Lancashire Telegraph, Tony Mowbray has confirmed one position he wants to strengthen is central midfield. He said: “We’ve talked about positional stuff and I think that’s very much an area where we can create competition for places. I’m sure we’ve got a department looking and I think within the next week or so I’ll be shown some players.”

Sam Morsy was signed on a free transfer and has made a positive impact at Ewood Park, but depth is limited and at 35, the Egyptian isn’t a long-term fix. Kristi Montgomery, Moussa Baradji and Jake Garrett are the other midfield options at present with Adam Forshaw out through a hip issue.

The Blackburn Rovers hierarchy have not got a great reputation. A dismal year of recruitment left them in relegation danger last season, and there have been justified concerns over their fate this term given just how few new arrivals there were in the summer.

Mowbray has made a good start to his latest Rovers stint as he gets a tune out of the group at his disposal, but they can not afford to rest on their laurels. If they do not strengthen in January, the Lancashire outfit are certainly at risk of a slide down the table.

It means Blackburn have to do business in the winter, and the midfield is a good place to start. Identifying targets now will allow them to make their moves early in the next transfer window, rather than scrambling for late additions like they have in recent times.

A new midfielder is clearly a priority. However, goalkeeper is another position of focus for Rovers amid doubts over Balazs Toth’s future as his deal runs down.

Morsy provides experience, leadership and pedigree in the middle of the park for Blackburn Rovers. Someone of a similar profile to him could be ideal, but perhaps a few years younger.

Montgomery is developing well and Baradji is settling into Championship football too, and they will both benefit from an experienced player alongside them. Targeting another central midfielder who has played plenty of football at a similar or higher level will be wise – someone who can guide their partner through the match and offer a bit of bite out of possession.

Forshaw and Morsy have proven to be players of value for Rovers, but at 35, the club will be aware that they are not long-term options. Perhaps a signing like the 2023 swoop for Sondre Tronstad would be ideal to keep the balance of youthful exuberance and experience in the middle.

#2218. ‘Ask him’ – Virgil van Dijk shrugs off bizarre incident with Chelsea player in Liverpool triumph

Virgil van Dijk has refused to be drawn on an incident involving him and Emmanuel Emegha in Liverpool’s Carabao Cup fourth-round clash against Chelsea on Wednesday night.

The Dutch striker came on for his senior Blues debut midway through the second half at Anfield, and within a few minutes he initiated a bizarre tussle with his compatriot.

After the Reds captain played the ball backwards to Trey Nyoni, the Chelsea substitute charged straight at our number 4 and shoved him to the ground, with the pass having been made at least a second earlier.

Speaking to reporters after the match, Van Dijk was asked about the curious incident with Emegha, and the Liverpool skipper swiftly shut down the question.

He replied (via Liverpool Echo): “Ask him. I don’t know. Maybe he’s trying to get into the national team as well and trying this way. I don’t know. You have to ask him. When he comes by, just ask him.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

We’re at a loss for an explanation as to why Emegha ran at Van Dijk well after the ball had been played, and he came from enough of a distance to have stopped himself in his tracks and realised that he’d have been better off not getting involved.

What was the Chelsea striker’s motivation to run at his fellow countryman and shove him to the ground? Beats us…

The Liverpool captain seemed momentarily irritated over the bizarre altercation but mostly bemused, just like he was at Malo Gusto’s comical play-acting after making the slightest of contact with the French left-back earlier in the second half.

Van Dijk had the last laugh as it was his team who prevailed on penalties, and although the 35-year-old had been substituted before the shootout, he’d done his bit for the Reds with a solid performance and an important interception to thwart Danny Welbeck.

We eagerly await Emegha’s explanation as to why he went over and accosted the veteran defender for no apparent reason…

#2217. Alfred Johansson hails returning stars as Motherwell end seven-game wait for victory

Motherwell boss Alfred Johansson insists welcoming back a host of first-team regulars was the icing on the cake in their William Hill Premiership victory over St Mirren.

The Fir Park boss was delighted to break a seven-game winless run and he believes an easing injury list is another cause for celebration.

He said: “It was so good to be manager of Motherwell for this game and being able to put that quality onto the pitch in the second half. Wow, that makes a massive difference. Regan Charles-Cook came on and was involved in the penalty situation.

“Oscar Priestman had a huge influence as did Eythor Bjorgolfsson and Callum Hendry, so that is a big joy and also something we will be able to build on.

“There was a lot of joy and happiness in the locker room after the game. After the draw in midweek at St Johnstone there was a lot of anger, fire and frustration, so the emotions were different and we are delighted to get the win.

“Even more than relief I felt there was determination and this group have been doing very well recently. To get four points from our last two games brings only praise to the players.

“The most important thing was we never gave up anything, we were very solid defensively and we pressed well.

“The solidity is something we need to build on and offensively we need to create even more from the advantages we have.

“There were spells when we were going too direct at times and making the game a bit more 50-50. In the second half we had to focus on the things we needed to take care of to win this game.”

Saints boss Craig McLeish admits his side will get back on the training ground in a bid to rediscover their early-season form and regain some belief.

He said: “There is a lack of belief and we will get back in on Monday and work hard on regaining that freedom of play which marked our performances at the start of the season

“We didn’t do enough to test Motherwell, I don’t think their goalkeeper had a save to make.

“We got into some promising areas but lacked a bit of quality in the final third. There were some really promising periods and we got into promising areas but didn’t manage to take advantage of them.

“Motherwell are a good side and will maybe feel a bit aggrieved that they didn’t take more of their chances.”

#2216. Ex-West Brom boss rushed to hospital

Former West Brom boss Pepe Mel was rushed to hospital in his native Spain during the weekend after he suffered a stroke.

The Baggies have released a statement on social media sending their sympathies with the 63-year-old, who was in charge at the Hawthorns from January 2014 to May 2014.

The experienced manager is currently out of work, but has worked in Spain, Greece, England and Morocco.

His most recent managerial stint came with IR Tangier, where he oversaw seven games in charge before departing in March 2026.

Mel began his coaching career in 1999 with Coslada, and has worked with clubs such as Getafe, Alaves, Real Betis and Deportivo de La Coruña.

West Brom were his only foray into English football, taking over the team after Steve Clarke’s dismissal midway through the 2013/14 campaign, ultimately overseeing a 17th place finish in the Premier League table.

West Brom have posted a message on their X account wishing Mel a speedy recovery after it was reported that he was rushed to hospital at the weekend with a stroke.

The 63-year-old underwent successful emergency surgery, and the club have told him that they will be with him every step of the way in his process of returning to good health.

“Everyone at West Bromwich Albion wishes former boss Pepe Mel a speedy recovery following surgery, after suffering a stroke,” wrote the club.

West Brom and Southampton shouldn't be the only Championship sides taking an interest in Dimitris Kaloskamis

Mel is believed to be in intensive care in the aftermath of his emergency surgery, where he will begin his road to recovery.

The Spaniard was appointed at West Brom in January 2014 after Clarke oversaw a challenging first half of the campaign.

However, he led the Baggies to just three wins from 17 fixtures, which led to his departure at the end of that season after keeping the club in the Premier League for another year.

He was succeeded by Alan Irvine, with Mel going on to return to his former club Betis in December 2014.

James Morrison’s West Brom side are currently fourth in the Championship table after the first 13 games of the campaign.

Albion have won seven, drawn three and lost three, leaving them four points adrift of leaders Middlesbrough.

The Midlands outfit are also four points clear of ninth place QPR, and are level with rivals Wolves but below them in the standings due to an inferior goal difference.

Next up for Morrison’s side is a home clash against Southampton on 3 November in an 8pm kick-off.

It was a nice message from West Brom to wish Mel well in his recovery from a stroke, particularly as he only spent a few months at the club.

The football world has joined them in hoping that he can get back to full health in the near future.

Mel is particularly beloved at Betis, where he not only enjoyed two managerial stints but he also played as a forward before going into a coaching career.

Everyone will be hoping that a positive update on Mel’s progress follows soon, and that he could even potentially return to management in the future, if he chooses.

#2215. Wolves and Swansea City handed major boost involving Peixoto & Matos

Wolverhampton Wanderers and Swansea City have received a major managerial boost after their respective head coaches were linked with the vacancy at Liga Portugal side, Sporting CP, across the weekend.

Indeed, it has been widely reported that Sporting are nearing an agreement with Olympique Lyonnais boss, Paulo Fonseca, which increases the likelihood of Cesar Peixoto and Vitor Matos staying put.

Both clubs enjoyed emphatic victories on Saturday and are well-placed inside the Championship's early-season promotion picture as a result.

Wolves made it two home victories in the space of a week by seeing off Cardiff City 3-0 at Molineux, whilst Swansea responded to successive losses with a 4-0 thumping of Blackburn Rovers.

As such, the aforementioned managerial news will be the latest lift for both sets of supporters and the respective squads in WV1 and SA1.

It was reported on Saturday that the two Championship managers had emerged on the radar of Sporting, who have terminated Rui Borges' contract after just under two years in charge.

Peixoto's move to Molineux in the summer was his first managerial role outside Portugal, having finished sixth in the top-flight last season with Gil Vicente, whilst Matos also enjoyed a brief spell with Maritimo after coaching at Liverpool and RB Salzburg.

Fonseca was also namedropped in said report, and it has since been claimed by RMC Sport that the 53-year-old has said his goodbyes to his squad at the Groupama Stadium, with Lyon currently sat third in Ligue 1 after nine matches.

Sporting are also third in the Portuguese top-flight at present, but are already nine points behind leaders Porto, with Borges' final match in charge being a 2-0 away win against Casa Pia on Friday.

There are a number of young coaches in charge of Championship clubs right now - but who are the youngest?

It is, of course, a positive and a hindrance to clubs if their head coach is being eyed by clubs of a greater stature in terms of history or current divisional status.

Since taking charge 12 months ago, Matos has won 22 of his first 45 Swansea matches across all competitions, giving his side a strong platform to build from after a strong end to last season.

As well as being linked with the Sporting vacancy, which is set to be filled by Fonseca, the 38-year-old recently emerged as a potential target for UEFA Conference League holders, Crystal Palace, who have endured an underwhelming start to Pierre Sage's reign as they sit inside the Premier League's bottom three.

Five players, five careers. Name them from the clubs they played for.

Each day there are five current or former EFL players to identify. For each one you’ll see their senior clubs in the order they played for them. Loan spells are left out.

You get four guesses per player. Every wrong guess unlocks a clue: first their position, then their nationality, then their initials.

Get it first time for 4 points, then 3, 2 and 1. The best possible score is 20. A new set of players arrives at midnight.

Just a matter of weeks ago, Peixoto was in the firing line from sections of the Wolves fanbase after a disappointing run of form post-international break, but his team have since taken 10 points from 12 and are now just one place behind the Swans after 13 games.

Given the strength-in-depth at both his and Matos' disposal, both clubs will hope for stability in both the short and long-term to give themselves the best possible chance of success.

Wolves and Swansea fans, what is your reaction to this news? Comment below!

With another international break looming, they also have the chance to build on their weekend victories on Tuesday and Wednesday against Portsmouth and Bristol City respectively.

#2214. How Hibernian made Hampden history against Hearts and booked final date with Rangers

Hibernian made a little piece of Hampden history this afternoon when they came from behind to beat Hearts in the second Premier Sports Cup semi-final.

The Easter Road club had lost all four of their previous meetings with their age-old Edinburgh adversaries at the Mount Florida venue before today.

When Claudio Braga put the Tynecastle men ahead in just the fourth minute it looked like they might be heading for another defeat.

But first-half goals from Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath gave Hibs a deserved lead and they held on to book a place in the final against Rangers next month.

Marink Reedijk, who had failed to win any of his first four games as manager, savoured the victory as much as any supporter.

Here are five talking points from the last four meeting.

Stragglers were still taking their seats inside the packed stadium when Hearts broke the deadlock.

Braga got in between Jason Kerr and Marko Ivezic and on the end of a Calvin Miller cross in the Hibs six yard box and headed beyond Raphael Sallinger from a few yards out.

The Portuguese forward was mobbed by his team-mates on the touchline as the maroon half of the stadium celebrated wildly.

But there was not much more for them to shout about after they had edged ahead.

Hibs recovered superbly from the early setback. Felix Passlack, their captain, was unfortunate not to restore parity just a few minutes later after being sent through on goal by Joe Newell. Beau Reus just managed to keep his deflected attempt out.

Owen Elding also should have done better after being supplied by Adam Mayor. The striker shelled over when he only had the keeper to beat. But he atoned for his miss soon afterwards by teeing up the leveller.

He controlled a pass from Newell and then scooped a chip over the heads of the opposition defence to Boyle who turned a shot in off of Reus and the inside of the left post.

The Hearts players and fans appealed for offside but linesman Douglas Ross kept his flag down.

VAR officials Andrew Dallas and Nick Walsh had a long look back at the replay over at Clydesdale House and found that there colleague had made the correct call. Jordi Altena had played the winger on.

Jamie McGrath put his side in front with an opportunistic strike at a Boyle corner three minutes before half-time.

The ball broke to Newell, who had just skimmed the top of the crossbar from distance, and he burst forward and then unleashed a powerful shot which was blocked by Malachi Fagan-Walcott. McGrath was perfectly positioned to net the rebound.

Hibs fans had high hopes of seeing their struggling heroes produce some Total Football when Dutchman Reedijk replaced David Gray as manager at Easter Road last month.

There has, though, been little evidence of that in the former Ajax youth coach’s opening games.

His charges produced some nice passages of play after falling behind at Hampden and deserved to go in front. They dominated long spells of the encounter with their capital rivals. But they did so by winning their battles and bullying their opponents.

Josh Mulligan and Kerr were booked by referee David Dickinson for fouls on Stephen Kinglsey and Dhanda respectively. The players in green and white shirts were hungrier and far more physical.

Miller going off injured – he was replaced by Sabri Guendouz shortly after the half hour mark and was later seen hobbling about on crutches – did nothing to help Hearts’ cause. He had set up the opener and posed a threat whenever he got on the ball.

Still, they could have no complaints about the scoreline when they returned to their dressing room. Braga had headed a Josh McPake cross well wide after his side had fallen behind. But if he had found the target and levelled it would have flattered them.

Hearts, doubtless after a few choice words from their manager Vrancken, played with far greater purpose when the action resumed in the second half. Sallinger had to produce fine saves from both Braga and Guendouz to keep the Leith men in front.

McPake, who should be named in the Scotland squad for the Nations League games against North Macedonia and Switzerland on Tuesday, was a real handful throughout.

However, Hibs looked dangerous on the counter too. Reus had to deny Boyle and Ivezic and Kingsley slid in a denied Passlack on two occasions as well. It was, to use an old football cliché, real end-to-end stuff.

The meeting between Aberdeen and Rangers on Saturday evening had been a tense affair that was devoid of chances as well as a difficult watch for the neutral observer. This was the perfect antidote. Everyone in the 41,673-strong crowd was royally entertained.

This has been another wretched season for Hibs fans and they travelled along the M8 in hope rather than expectation.

The Leith men last won a William Hill Premiership game back in August and are in bottom spot in the top flight table.

But Passlack and his team-mates buried the memory of the Scottish Cup defeats that Hibs they had suffered against Hearts at Hampden in 2006, 2012 and 2022 and the League Cup loss they were on the receiving end of on the South Side of Glasgow in 1955.

There were tears in the eyes of their longsuffering followers during the rendition of Sunshine on Leith which they belted out following the final whistle.

If Hibernian perform as well in the final against Rangers next month then their fans may have more reason to party.

#2213. 6 Steve Evans replacements Bristol Rovers must consider as sack calls grow

After a nightmare few weeks, it is fair to say that pressure is increasing on Bristol Rovers manager Steve Evans.

Evans took over at the Memorial Stadium in December with Bristol Rovers sitting in the League Two relegation zone, but the 64-year-old led his side to a 14th-placed finish last season after a stunning second half of the campaign that included a run of eight consecutive victories.

The Gas' momentum continued into this season as they won four of their opening five games to top the table in early September, and as Evans' impressive work started to attract attention from elsewhere, he was said to have been on the radar of Scottish Premiership side Hibernian.

However, since a 1-0 win over Rotherham United on 5th September, Rovers have won just one of their last nine league games, and they slumped to a seventh defeat during that run as they were beaten 3-1 by Fleetwood Town at Highbury Stadium on Saturday.

As they continue to slide down the table, the Gas currently sit 17th, but while they are just four points clear of the relegation zone, they are also the same distance from the play-off places in what is an incredibly congested division.

After their latest defeat at Fleetwood over the weekend, growing numbers of Rovers fans are calling for Evans to be sacked, and we have looked at some of the potential replacements the club should consider if they decide to make a managerial change.

Stuart Maynard has been out of work since his shock departure from York City in July, just three weeks before the start of the season.

Maynard led the Minstermen to the National League title last season with an incredible total of 108 points, but owner Matt Uggla made the surprise call to part company with the 46-year-old over the summer, much to the dismay of the fanbase.

While Maynard's last managerial role was in the fifth tier, he previously had an 18-month spell in charge of Notts County in League Two, guiding the Magpies to a sixth-placed finish in the 2024-25 season before being dismissed following defeat to AFC Wimbledon in the play-off semi-finals.

It was reported that Maynard rejected an approach from National League side Hartlepool United in September, which suggests he may be eyeing up an EFL job, and he should be high on Bristol Rovers' wish list if they were to sack Evans.

If Bristol Rovers feel that Maynard is too much of a gamble, they could go for a manager with more recent experience of the division in former Salford City boss Karl Robinson.

Robinson led the Ammies to a fourth-placed finish in League Two last season, only missing out on the automatic promotion spots by a single point, but he was sacked in June after a 3-0 defeat to Notts County in the play-off final at Wembley.

The 46-year-old has achieved one promotion during his managerial career, having guided MK Dons to the Championship in 2016, while he also oversaw two play-off finishes in League One during his five-year spell in charge of Oxford United.

Robinson held talks with Peterborough United in September prior to the appointment of Robbie Savage, so he may be keen to hold out for a League One job, but the Gas would surely have a strong chance of tempting him back to the fourth tier.

Another manager with an excellent recent record at League Two level is ex-Bromley boss Andy Woodman.

Woodman took over at then National League side Bromley in March 2021, and after leading the Ravens to promotion to the EFL for the first time in their history in 2024, he defied the odds once again as he inspired his side to the League Two title last season.

However, after a tough start to life in League One that included a number of heavy defeats, Bromley parted company with Woodman last month, and the 55-year-old broke his silence on Monday to express his disappointment at his exit from the CopperJax Community Stadium.

Given that he has only just departed Bromley, Woodman may wish to take a break before returning to the dugout, particularly with emotions still running high about the way he was treated by his former employers, but he may find it difficult to turn down a club the size of Bristol Rovers.

Like Woodman, former Peterborough United boss Luke Williams is another manager to have been sacked by a League One club this season.

Williams saved Posh from relegation last season after taking over at the Weston Homes Stadium last October, but after an underwhelming summer transfer window, his side made a slow start to the new campaign, resulting in his departure in September.

While Williams' time at Peterborough did not go to plan, the 46-year-old led Notts County to promotion from the National League in 2023, and he steered Swansea City to a 14th-placed finish in the Championship in the 2023-24 campaign before being dismissed midway through the following season.

Williams' career is at something of a crossroads after his exit from Posh, which could mean that he may have to consider taking a job at a lower level than he would ideally like, but Bristol Rovers could be the perfect place for him to rebuild his reputation.

Although his stock has not fallen quite as low as Williams, it has been a tough few years for ex-Luton Town and Oxford manager Matt Bloomfield.

After taking his first steps into management with Colchester United, Bloomfield then made the move to Wycombe Wanderers, where he spent much of his playing career, and his side emerged as serious automatic promotion contenders in League One in the 2024-25 season.

Despite the Chairboys sitting second in the table at the time, Bloomfield opted to depart Adams Park to take over at Luton in January 2025, but he was unable to prevent their relegation from the Championship, and he was dismissed last October after an inconsistent start to life back in League One.

Bloomfield was handed another opportunity in the Championship by Oxford in January, but he suffered his second consecutive relegation after failing to save the U's from the drop, and he was sacked in June after just over five months in charge at the Kassam Stadium.

The 42-year-old's recent record does not make for good reading, but it could be argued that he was rather unfortunate in each of his last two managerial roles, and he would certainly arrive at Bristol Rovers with a point to prove.

Should Bristol Rovers sack Steve Evans or does he deserve more time at the Memorial Stadium? Tell us in the comments below!

Many of the above candidates are on the market, but if Bristol Rovers are willing to poach a manager who is currently employed, Worthing's Adam Hinshelwood could be an exciting option.

After a successful first spell at Worthing, Hinshelwood took over at then National League side York in February 2024, and after keeping the Minstermen in the division in his first season, he led them to a second-placed finish in the 2024-25 campaign before losing to Oldham Athletic in the play-off semi-finals.

Despite making an unbeaten start, Hinshelwood was sacked by York just four games into last season, and after making a surprise return to Worthing just over a month later, he guided the Rebels to the fifth tier for the first time in their history after winning the National League South title.

Hinshelwood's managerial reputation has continued to flourish this season, with Worthing currently sitting sixth in the table after an outstanding start to the campaign, and the Gas should consider swooping for the 42-year-old.

#2212. ‘Come on, referee’ – Ex-PGMOL chief calls out Darren England over one incident in Liverpool win

Darren England has been criticised for not issuing a yellow card in response to one contentious incident in Liverpool’s Carabao Cup tie against Chelsea on Wednesday night.

The referee booked four players over the course of the match at Anfield, but he didn’t reach for his pocket when Emmanuel Emegha inexplicably charged at Virgil van Dijk off the ball and shoved the Reds captain to the ground.

The veteran defender shrugged off questions about that incident afterwards, although a former chief executive of the PGMOL (now Pro Ref) believes that the Blues striker should’ve been cautioned for his indiscetion.

Speaking to Football Insider, Keith Hackett said: “Virgil van Dijk had every right to be annoyed with the referee and his opponent. The referee took no action for what was a very aggressive run and push that met the criteria for being reckless.

“Van Dijk ended up on the floor, so this player is very fortunate not to receive a yellow card. Come on referee, you had a reasonable game, but you could have done better here.

“This could have easily caused a mass confrontation. I am surprised and disappointed that a yellow card was not issued to the Chelsea player.”

Virgil van Dijk was NOT HAPPY with Emmanuel Emegha 😒 pic.twitter.com/UEtoJ7n5va

— ITV Football (@itvfootball) October 29, 2026

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Hackett is right – Emegha was fortunate to avoid a yellow card for his shove on Van Dijk, especially considering some of the bookings that England handed out earlier in the match.

For example, Lewis Koumas was harshly cautioned after just 10 minutes for a minor foul on Maxence Lacroix, which was far less of an indiscretion than what the Chelsea substitute did to his fellow Dutchman in the second half.

There was no discernible reason for the Blues attacker to run at the Liverpool captain and barge him to the ground, and as Hackett said, it could easily have led to a large-scale brawl between players from both teams.

We don’t want to see cards being dished out unnecessarily, but Emegha’s petulance would have deserved a booking, certainly more so than Koumas for his foul on Lacroix.

#2211. Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

United fought back after conceding an early goal against Atletico to secure their second win of pre-season.

They fell behind in the sixth minute when Arnau Ortiz’s cross into the box evaded everyone, including United keeper Tom Heaton before hitting the back of the net.

United got the equaliser their performance deserved when the impressive Shea Lacey showed his skill in the box and was fouled. From the resulting penalty, Bryan Mbeumo sent the goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

In the 72nd minute, Mbeumo got his second of the afternoon after he bundled the ball home after the United press forced Atletico into a mistake.

The Spanish side hit the post twice in the closing stages but United held on to win.

“We had a clear plan before the game, everyone stuck to it and made the game enjoyable,” Mbeumo said. “We work really hard during training for these games, the main goal is to be ready for the season starting. I have done great things on the right but also as a striker.

“I think I am more experienced on the wing but I enjoy playing as a striker. For an offensive player, it is always good to score for the team.”

Gianni Infantino is facing an ultimatum from Uefa: resign or face an emergency no-confidence vote.

It is understood all 55 of Uefa’s member nations would opt to oust Infantino in a vote of no-confidence if he refuses to step down. Uefa can trigger such a vote with just 43 member nations.

European football’s governing body announced a loss of confidence on Saturday morning and has demanded change after Infantino was forced to scrap his £15bn plan to sell a stake in the World Cup.

Uefa’s statement followed widespread opposition and a revolt within Fifa’s ranks that staff are calling “kill the monster”.

The Football Association backed Uefa’s stance, saying: “We fully support Uefa’s position. It is time for a full and robust review of Fifa’s leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart.”

Good afternoon and welcome to pre-season coverage of Manchester United against Atletico Madrid.

Michael Carrick’s squad continue their preparations for the new season with a trip to the Swedish capital, Stockholm, where they face Diego Simeone’s La Liga side.

Last week, United cruised to a 5-0 victory over Rosenborg but today will be their first real test. They are slowly starting to get players back but the likes of captain Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans will not be involved.

“I think we’re in a good place. I think there’s four weeks to go to the start and we’re gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup as we progress,” Carrick said.

“But I think a little bit of patience and time and trying to keep ahead and as I said, keeping everyone fit but moving forward is a really good direction to go in. And as it stands right now, I think we’re in a pretty good place. So, the boys will get better as we go.”

One player who will be looking to impress is Mason Mount. He has had an injury-hit spell at Old Trafford but is fit and ready to go for the season. He is also growing into a leadership role at the club.

He told BBC Radio Manchester: “You have different types of leaders, you have ones that are very vocal. I always want to see myself as one that leads by example and never stops working on the pitch.

“I’ve been captain previously years ago. I love the role especially with a lot of younger players on the pitch being able to speak to them and make them feel comfortable in the game and off the pitch as well. It’s a role that I really like and loved having it [the captain’s armband] in the second half.”

Then, after making his debut in the final game before the international break against West Ham United, he picked up another setback over that three-week gap between games.

Jamie McGrath believes Hibernian's win over Hearts in the semi-final of the Premier Sports Cup was "reward" for fans who have supported through thick and thin this season.

The Easter Road outfit saw off their Edinburgh rivals in the derby clash at Hampden on Sunday to seal their spot in the cup final against Rangers to be played on December 13.

Their form in the Scottish Premiership has been poor by comparison and Marink Reedijk's side are languishing at the foot of the Premiership table. But for McGrath that is somewhat of a false position.

Hibs have been unfortunate not to take more points this season and secure more victories, the midfielder says, as they have struggled to turn performances into results.

Jamie McGrath reacts after firing @HibernianFC into the #PremierSportsCup Final with his Edinburgh Derby winner 🥬 "Today, I think we got our reward" 🗣️ #PremierSportsCup https://t.co/0xRwKJwDdU

So he hopes the derby victory can catapult his side back to form and help push them up the division and give their fans more to shout about.

#2208. Liverpool have only one club to fear amid Rio Ngumoha contract talks

Bayern Munich are still interested in signing Rio Ngumoha.

Gianluca Di Marzio now reports that the Bavarian giants will try to make a push for the teenage gem in the upcoming January transfer window.

The simple fact of the matter for FC Bayern is that their season – or, to put it more accurately, the fate of their Champions League campaign – may hinge on how they solve their left wing concern.

Luis Diaz, without question, is a sensational talent, but his hamstring injury (picked up in the 2-2 draw against Arsenal) raises questions around the security of the position long term.

Hypothetically, were the reigning Bundesliga champions to find themselves deep in European competition, they’re unlikely to want to be forced to use either Tim Binder or Alphonso Davies. Serge Gnabry can also cover the left flank, if need be, but this is a far from perfect solution.

So, if anyone could do with an extremely talented, 18-year-old left winger whose long-term pathway wouldn’t be obstructed by a senior starter (in this case, 29-year-old Diaz) – it’s most definitely Bayern.

“It’s true that Bayern Munich want Rio Ngumoha, and it’s true that Liverpool want to extend his contract – so it’s a difficult situation because anything is possible,” Di Marzio told Wettfruende.

“Liverpool are pushing to extend his contract and keep him in the team in the future, but it’s also true that Bayern Munich will try to sign him as early as January.”

The journalist went on to add: “I think it’s not a very high probability, but a good one that he will extend his contract, as he enjoys his time at Liverpool and has a good relationship with the manager; therefore, it’s hard to imagine Liverpool letting him go.

“FC Bayern Munich is pushing for it, and Arsenal is also interested.”

We’re pretty confident that Rio Ngumoha will commit his immediate and long-term future to Liverpool with a contract extension.

The Englishman made clear that he chose life at Anfield over staying at Chelsea due to the pathway that was offered to him at L4, telling ITV Sport earlier in October: “Liverpool was always the right option – and the only option really.

“[I thought]: ‘If I go here I’ll get the opportunity and the pathway to showcase what I can do’. It looks like so far it’s paid off!”

After the 2-1 win over Brentford, the winger suggested that talks between his agent and the club were going well.

Yet, here we are, with rumours swirling around Arsenal and Bayern Munich. If we’re talking about a pathway to more regular first team minutes – we’re not particularly worried about Arsenal. We just can’t see the Gunners offering Ngumoha a better deal in that regard.

The concern for us is whether the teenager looks at the current state of play in English football – and the joy talents like Diaz and Michael Olise have had since departing – and opts for life in a less demanding league. Or, to put it differently, one in which he can operate without being kicked around quite as much.

In that sense, it would be naïve of us to just assume that Liverpool is definitely the “better” project compared to Vincent Kompany’s Bayern Munich.

If anything, the current climate, coupled with Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or win in London, indicates that life in Germany isn’t quite so bad.

#2207. Middlesbrough's £3m winger has hit trouble after surprise Turkey move

Middlesbrough have flown out of the traps in Kim Hellberg's first full season at the Riverside Stadium, showcasing exactly why they were viewed as automatic promotion potential before a ball was kicked.

The Teesside outfit have spent almost a decade at Championship level under several names, but the Swede is certainly the one who has made the biggest impression in terms of having such an immediate impact during said timeframe.

Hellberg will mark one year at the Riverside Stadium at the end of the month - one which his current chargers have begun two points clear at the top of the table, having lost just one of their first 13 matches.

In the past 12 months, Boro have adopted an unrelenting, high-pressing style in which several chances are created and, indeed, now being put away, largely by big-money summer recruit, Will Lankshear, whilst other creative forces were added to Hellberg's ranks throughout an eye-catching summer window.

Whilst such strong quality was added, a plethora of players on the fringes of the squad saw exits sanctioned, as well as the high-profile departures of Hayden Hackney and Morgan Whittaker.

However, there still remains a big question mark over Sontje Hansen's long-term future, albeit one which is highly unlikely to lie in the North East.

With Ajax famed for their infamous production line, Hansen was a player seen to have a fairly high ceiling in terms of potential, representing the Netherlands across all youth age groups and scoring the Golden Boot in the Under-17 FIFA World Cup of 2019, which saw him linked with Manchester City.

Having scored 12 times in 64 appearances for NEC Nijmegen, there was excitement in the air when Hansen penned a four-year contract under Rob Edwards last summer.

Despite scoring his first Boro goal in his fourth Championship outing against Preston North End, it soon became apparent that the midfielder was still somewhat of an enigma to his then-new head coach.

"Sontje is a real talent. I think we’re still working out everything he has got. I think he’s someone we’re going to be able to use in different positions and ask him to do some different things," Edwards said 13 months ago.

The Spygate scandal affected Middlesbrough's players last May, but does it affect them now?

Despite starting Hellberg's first game in charge against Derby County, Hansen was barely utilised by the new head coach despite a brief period with illness in the early weeks of his tenure.

Between New Year's Day and Good Friday, the Dutchman played just two minutes of Championship football and was an unused substitute in 13 of 15 league outings.

With minutes hard to come by despite a 14-minute cameo in the play-off final, speculation was rife over his immediate future, with Hellberg making a rather honest admission as to why Hansen didn't feature in the EFL Cup success over Wrexham at the start of the competitive season.

Middlesbrough fans, what do you make of Sontje Hansen's current situation? Comment below!

“Sontje was not involved, but it was no injury or anything like that. He played a game [for the Under-21s] because we looked at his physics," he revealed.

At 24, the seven-time Curacao international still has much of his senior career in front of him, but there is a risk of stagnation if Hansen is unable to turn his current fortunes around.

Shortly after Hellberg's admission, it was confirmed that a loan agreement had been struck with Turkish Süper Lig outfit, Gaziantep, which reportedly includes an option-to-buy at the end of the season.

Five players, five careers. Name them from the clubs they played for.

Each day there are five current or former EFL players to identify. For each one you’ll see their senior clubs in the order they played for them. Loan spells are left out.

You get four guesses per player. Every wrong guess unlocks a clue: first their position, then their nationality, then their initials.

Get it first time for 4 points, then 3, 2 and 1. The best possible score is 20. A new set of players arrives at midnight.

A figure is yet to be revealed, but based off short-term evidence, there is no indication that such a clause will be triggered as the winger has started just one of his five league appearances — the last of which came in mid-October as he is currently sidelined with a hamstring issue.

Hellberg will certainly feel his decision to sanction a loan exit for Hansen has been vindicated, although there will still be an element of frustration that he is yet to establish his place in the side at Gaziantep for various reasons.

It is a stark contrast to the form being enjoyed by Middlesbrough's current attacking options, even if you look beyond Lankshear's 15 goals, with Amario Cozier-Duberry continuing his own fine form on loan from Brighton and Hove Albion, whilst Tommy Conway and Riley McGree have also chipped in with seven assists combined.

#2206. Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running

Teenage sensation Max Dowman was the star of Arsenal’s first pre-season match, as he scored one goal and assisted another in a 4-1 victory over Girona.

Dowman, 16, was joined on the scoresheet by new signing Christos Tzolis, who struck with a low effort in his first game since his £34m move from Belgian side Club Brugge.

Established attackers Kai Havertz and Gabriel Jesus also scored for the Premier League champions, who were largely comfortable against opposition from the Spanish second tier.

Here are four things Telegraph Sport learnt from the match:

It was this time last year that Dowman first announced his remarkable talent to the wider world. Then only 15, he sparkled in pre-season and made it clear to Mikel Arteta that he was ready to impact matches at the highest level.

A year on, Dowman is now an established first-team player. He is the youngest ever Premier League winner and the competition’s youngest ever scorer, and he looks set to make even more of a mark this season.

In this friendly against Girona, Dowman created Arsenal’s opening goal with a gorgeous defence-splitting pass for Havertz. He did so after receiving the ball under pressure and spinning into space. Dowman then scored Arsenal’s third with a powerful low drive from the edge of the box.

Dowman is in competition with Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke for a place on the right wing, which means this summer represents a huge opportunity for the teenager. After playing for England at the World Cup, Saka and Madueke will both miss most of pre-season.

Dowman, therefore, has a serious chance of going into the new campaign as the starting right-winger. The Community Shield on August 16 must be a target in his mind.

“We know what he’s capable of doing,” Arteta said. “We want to be more consistent in terms of the performances and the actions that he can deliver, but I think today he had a really good game.”

Arsenal are close to completing a deal for Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimarães but, for now, their only outfield signing of the summer has been Tzolis. This was the Greek winger’s first match in front of supporters and he immediately demonstrated why Arsenal were willing to pay £34m to buy him from Club Brugge.

With Tzolis, it is all about the final product. Goals and assists. He struck 22 times for Club Brugge last season, and registered 29 assists.

How did he produce such impressive numbers? The answer could be seen in his first-half goal against Girona. Receiving the ball on the left wing, Tzolis quickly accelerated towards the penalty area and unleashed a low shot. It was perhaps a more direct approach than Arsenal would usually have seen from Leandro Trossard, the player Tzolis has replaced, and it caught Girona off-guard as the ball deflected into the net.

“I’m very pleased with him,” Arteta said. “First of all, the way he has adapted to the club, to the team. The connection he’s already generating with the boys. I think you’re going to love the player.

“A player who’s very direct. He’s got the goal between the eyes. He has a lot of similarities with Leo [Trossard] in a lot of the things that he can do and the spaces he can occupy. And then the work rate that he has... He’s a boy that comes with so much hunger. He wants to prove himself, it’s a dream for him. And we are here to help him.”

Havertz was one of the few Arsenal players who benefited from playing at the World Cup. His injury issues mean that, unlike most of his team-mates, he did not end the 2025-26 season in a state of exhaustion.

After returning to the pitch in the spring, Havertz enjoyed an impressive end to the campaign for Arsenal. He then performed well at the World Cup, scoring three goals for Germany.

He remains one of Arteta’s favourite players, not least because of his versatility. He started in attack in the crucial end-of-season games in May, but played in midfield against Girona. His low finish, from Dowman’s pass, represented his eighth goal in his last 12 matches for club and country.

Girona’s goal, scored by Arnau Martínez, was perhaps the only alarming moment of this comfortable pre-season victory. Martínez was unmarked from a left-wing corner when he powered a header into Arsenal’s net.

For a group of players who pride themselves on their set-piece prowess, this was a disappointing moment. It also perhaps showed Arsenal’s reliance on their two first-choice centre-backs, William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães, when they are defending crosses into their box.

Gabriel arrived at Arsenal’s pre-season training camp a few days ago, so he should be in good shape by the start of the new campaign. Saliba, though, will be missing for months with a back problem.

Without Saliba’s height and power, will Arsenal be as effective from set-pieces in the opening chunk of the campaign? Coventry City, Arsenal’s opponents on the first night of the season, will undoubtedly look to test the champions in these situations.

The reigning Premier League champions are handed the Costa Brava Trophy, which is half-heartedly lifted into the air by White. There will be far bigger trophies on offer to Arsenal in the upcoming campaign.

Arsenal have cruised to a routine 4-1 win over Girona, with Havertz, Tzolis, Dowman and Gabriel Jesus all finding the net. Arteta will be delighted with his side’s professionalism and ruthlessness.

Meslier takes too long on his goal kick, gifting a corner to Girona. However, the delivery from the hosts is so poor as it flies harmlessly out of play. That sums up Girona’s difficult evening.

There is another round of substitutions for both sides.

Arsenal’s makeshift line-up, which is full of Hale End graduates, is holding firm, with Girona evidently struggling for attacking inspiration. If Arsenal can see out this victory without any injuries, then it would have panned out exactly how Arteta would have wanted.

We are back under way for the second half.

That was a straightforward half for Arsenal. Arteta will be pleased with Havertz’s showing in his 33 minutes on the pitch. After missing so much of last season through injury, it has been a good summer for Havertz so far. He scored three goals in Arsenal’s final six games of 2025/26, and then netted four times for Germany in June.

The 2009-born playmaker was Arsenal’s standout player in that first half. Dowman’s confidence and class on the ball has been brilliant, with his expertly-crafted assist for Havertz’s opener an obvious highlight.

Tzolis registered 22 goals and 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He is an end-product machine, and that goal was a little indication of how he racks up such eye-watering numbers. After receiving possession on the left wing, he was so quick to shift the ball onto his right foot and fire the shot at goal. He describes himself as a “direct” player and that was evidence of it.

The new winger is one-on-one with Martinez and darts inside, before firing a low effort into the bottom corner. It took a slight deflection, leaving Gazzaniga with no chance. Tzolis has looked lively and slotted into Arsenal’s attack seamlessly so far.

Since their goal, Arsenal have assumed real authority of this encounter and look like the far superior side.

After his extraordinary breakthrough campaign last year, Max Dowman has a huge opportunity this summer. With England wingers Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke not returning until later in pre-season, Dowman has a chance to take ownership of the right wing position ahead of the Community Shield. His assist for Kai Havertz, a lovely measured pass after an excellent piece of skill in midfield, was a sign that Dowman means business.

Dowman drifts inside and pops up in the right channel, wriggling past Moreno, before threading a delightful pass through to Havertz. White leads Arsenal out onto the pitch to face Girona, who boast the likes of Van de Beek, Gil and Moreno in their starting XI.

Talking earlier this week, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta sent out a determined message to other clubs by outlining their ambitious transfer plans.

“A lot is happening,” Arteta said. “We all know about the context of this transfer window. From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

“That is going to require a better squad, better individuals. We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way.”

Arteta also believes that last season’s Premier League title has served as added motivation for his squad to improve and hit new heights.

The way we behave daily with more and more determination and ambition, because we’ve shown that we’ve got it. Now we have to show that we belong to this level and we want to increase and take this football club to a different dimension.”

It had been a relatively quiet transfer window for Arsenal, who have recruited just goalkeeper Illan Meslier and winger Christos Tzolis.

However, Arsenal are now moving very bullishly, closing on Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães, while also targeting Real Madrid’s Vinícius Júnior.

Sam Dean has the full breakdown of a potential deal for the Real Madrid star and how Arsenal are prepared to continue flexing their muscles in the transfer market in what would be one of the biggest moves in Premier League history.

It was January 2025, with Arsenal earning a hard-fought 2-1 comeback victory in the Champions League courtesy of first-half goals from Jorginho and Ethan Nwaneri.

Since this European encounter, Girona have been on a seriously downward trajectory, enduring lowly 16th and 19th finishes in La Liga, with the latter ensuring relegation to the Segunda Division, where they’ll play in the upcoming campaign.

Arsenal are closing in on one of the statement signings of the summer, with Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães getting closer to joining the Premier League holders.

This deal means that Christian Norgaard is expected to leave and seal a move to Everton for around £7m.

As previously reported by Telegraph Sport, Guimarães has been Arsenal’s top target for weeks. It is believed that he will cost around £80m.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

#2205. Paul Merson makes Premier League title claim Andoni Iraola may disagree with

Paul Merson has claimed that Liverpool will need to beat Arsenal this Sunday to be involved in the Premier League title race.

A victory at Anfield would see the Reds leapfrog Brighton in third (pending the result of their trip to the Etihad on Saturday) and go within three points of Mikel Arteta’s men.

A Premier League title race still feels a little early for an Andoni Iraola side that’s still trying to patch up the damage done in the 2025/26 season. Not to mention a summer transfer window that saw the club add quality but not necessarily balance to a side that finished fifth last term.

Nonetheless, Merson appears to be of the mind that beating the reigning champions would put the Merseysiders firmly in the race.

“Liverpool are starting to cook a little bit, but they have got to win this Sunday if they want to be in the Premier League title race,” the former Gunners star told Sky Sports.

“If they don’t win, they stay six points behind at least and still have to go to the Emirates.

“You’re then asking Arsenal to lose two football matches without you losing one. And given Liverpool will lose more games this season, you’re then asking Arsenal to lose three or four games for the rest of the season. That’s a lot of games.

“But at the same time, it’s also must-not-lose for Liverpool as they still need to stay on track for the Champions League places.

“If Arsenal go and win against Liverpool, that could nearly be it for the Premier League title. You then start to think: who’s going to go and beat them?”

We’re not necessarily opposed to that viewpoint – and it’s worth emphasising that Liverpool should be heading into every individual game thinking it puts them a step closer to mounting a challenge on the title.

But ultimately, we’re not sure nine games represent enough of a sample size to indicate that we’re potential Premier League champions in 2026/27.

We’ve seen enough to suggest that Iraola is the right fit at Anfield and the club is showing green shoots, but there’s a lot more than needs to come from Liverpool both on and off the pitch.

As we say, if Liverpool do find themselves in a position where they’re increasingly looking up at the top of the table, and at a slim gap between themselves, City and Arsenal, why not go for it?

But as things presently stand, we’d be amazed to see this version of Liverpool mount and maintain a title challenge over the course of the season. Especially once the games start coming thick and fast past the turn of the year and the club is juggling knockout games in the Champions League and cup competitions.

In that sense, if Liverpool appear to be negotiating their way through a title challenge come the opening of the January transfer window, the market could prove pivotal in enabling us to go the distance.

We’re all firmly aware of the weak points within the squad; the fullbacks have question marks (albeit, Ronald Araujo has excelled and Milos Kerkez is showing signs of improvement), Liverpool need a holding midfielder that can protect the backline and pass the ball forward, and there’s a clear need for a right-sided winger. We could add a backup striker on top of that, but at this point it just seems like the club will wait for Hugo Ekitike to return to the fold.

Either way, if Liverpool somehow find themselves in the thick of battle at the top of the table come January – we hope the club will back the manager in the market rather than laud the Basque head coach for being ahead of schedule.

#2204. Martin Boyle's goosebumps as Hibs hero salutes fans after downing Hearts

Jubilant Martin Boyle dedicated Hibernian's stirring Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Hearts to the supporters who have stood by the team through a difficult campaign.

The Easter Road hero was emotional at full-time after helping fire Hibs into the final at Hampden, where they will face Rangers on December 13.

Boyle cancelled out Claudio Braga's opener before Jamie McGrath netted the winner in a dramatic Edinburgh derby comeback that sparked wild celebrations among the green-and-white half of the national stadium.

With Hibs sitting bottom of the Premiership, Boyle believes the result can provide a major boost heading into the rest of the season.

Speaking to Premier Sports, he said: "Unbelievable. I thought we were brilliant in the first half, apart from the corner. After that, the reaction from the boys was great and I thought we probably deserved it.

Read more: Marink Reedijk challenges Hibs to 'create new history' in huge Hearts Hampden clash

"In the second half we dug in and defended the box really well. It's a derby, we knew form would go out the window and we stuck together. We always believed we could win this game and we have."

Asked how a side at the foot of the table could produce such a performance on the big stage, Boyle insisted confidence has never disappeared within the squad.

He said: "Nothing's changed, we've always had that belief.

"We're going through a bit of a transition phase at the moment and the squad is quite young, so us senior boys really need to step up.

"The experienced boys coming on helped us at the end. It's brilliant and the fans deserve it for sticking with us."

Boyle reserved special praise for the travelling support, who created a thunderous atmosphere throughout the afternoon.

He said: "Hopefully we can enjoy a cup final and get ourselves up the league table. That's the main objective.

"The noise behind us here was unbelievable."

The 33-year-old, who has made more than 400 appearances for the club, admitted the occasion brought back memories of some of the greatest days of his Hibs career.

"It's a special feeling," he said. "I've got goosebumps. It's a great day out.

"Moments like this don't come around often and you've got to create them. We did that today and the fans have stuck by us.

"I know the league performances haven't been great, but thank you to everyone who came to support us today. They can go home with a smile on their face and enjoy their night out."

Hibs will return to Hampden next month looking to lift the trophy, but Boyle is refusing to get carried away ahead of the showdown with Rangers.

He smiled: "I'm not getting carried away, fingers crossed.

"I've still got some legs in me at the tender age of 33. As long as I'm playing and contributing to this club, I can enjoy moments like this and we can all enjoy the day out in the final.":

#2203. 'Nonsense!' - Ex-QPR & Southampton star Charlie Austin launches rant on social media

Former Southampton and QPR striker Charlie Austin has criticised coaches preying on gullible parents of young children trying to make it in the world of football.

The former forward has posted a message on social media in which he complained about coaches advertising the importance of ball mastery by the age of 10 or 12.

The 37-year-old’s playing career saw him reach the Premier League with the likes of QPR, the Saints and West Brom.

He also competed at a Championship level with the likes of Burnley, before moving to Australia in 2022 with Brisbane Roar.

Austin has since returned to British football, and he continues to compete at a non-league level.

However, he has also become a prominent voice in expressing his football opinions online, and this includes on his personal social media pages.

Austin has attacked the coaches that advertise their business by claiming that kids have to master certain skills with the ball by certain ages, suggesting that those claims are utter nonsense.

He believes that they are preying on gullible parents who won’t know any better, and that this is taking advantage of kids trying to fulfill their dream of making it as a professional footballer.

Pick any two players. Send the code, and your mate enters it here to play the same pair.

“I keep seeing coaches, etc. on Instagram talking about ‘oh, you’ve got to master these ball mastery skills by the age of 10. Oh you’ve got to do this by the age of five. Oh you’ve got to do this by the age of 12’. No you don’t,” said Austin, via Instagram.

Harry Redknapp has opened up on the reaction he received from Portsmouth fans when he took over at Southampton

“Just go about your business, and I certainly get you’re advertising your business, which is great, which is absolutely fine.

“But to come up with nonsense, spout nonsense to gullible parents — and there is plenty of gullible parents that want their kid to live the dream.

“And I get you want to charge £35 an hour, or £20 an hour to make a few quid because you don’t want to work, you don’t want to do the occasional nine to five job, or whatever, totally understand that.

“It’s all about growing your business, but seriously stop talking rubbish, stop hassling parents with nonsense.”

Austin originally started his career in the Reading academy system, but was released at the age of 15.

The striker took an unconventional career path from there, working his way through a number of non-league sides before earning an opportunity with Swindon Town at the age of 20.

He made 54 league appearances for the Robins after being given a place in the first team squad, which led to him signing for Burnley in 2011.

But it was at QPR where he first received a taste of Premier League football, helping the Hoops earn promotion from the Championship in 2013/14.

Austin scored an impressive 18 times in 2014/15, but it wasn’t enough to keep QPR in the top flight, with the club succumbing to relegation with a 20th place finish.

But the striker earned another shot at top flight football with a move to Southampton in 2015/16.

Injuries hampered his time at St. Mary’s, but he still contributed 16 goals and three assists in the division for the Hampshire outfit across four campaigns.

Austin went on to help West Brom earn Premier League promotion in 2019/20, but he played just five more times in the top flight in the remainder of his career.

Austin is clearly thinking about his own path to playing in the Premier League when going on this rant about kids needing to master certain skills by certain ages.

His opportunity to make it at the top level looked to be over as a teenager, but he was able to continue working on his own skills to eventually make it when he was in his 20s.

So it’s not too surprising that he is taking an issue with this kind of framing when it comes to underage player development, as he is an example that there is no perfect path to becoming a professional player.

Perhaps Austin should try his own hand at coaching in the future, as his experience could be quite a valuable asset for young kids to learn from.
